Three conventions this file obeys and you must too:
- **A number carries its measurement date**, or it is not written down.
- **Code references are symbol anchors** (`path › symbol`) or grep patterns. Never a bare line number.
- **Deploy state is a measurement.** This file records the COMMAND, never the answer. The tree holds claims, not deploy facts.

## 1. Layout & file size

- **Feature-first.** `src/features/<name>/` owns its UI, hooks, types, `server/`. No cross-feature imports — shared things go to `src/shared/`. Never a top-level `lib/` or `components/` under `src/`.
  - 🔒 ⚠ **ONE RECORDED EXCEPTION, AND IT IS VISIBILITY PREDICATES (2026-09-17, F-716).** `src/features/search/server/repository-visibility.ts` imports `knowledge › canSeeBase`, `skills › canSeeSkill`, `chats › canSeeChat` and `agent-identities › canSeeIdentity`. **The alternative was a FIFTH hand-written copy of four security predicates**, and search had one: `visibility = <widest> OR <owner> = caller`, which both MISSED every lent row and LEAKED every `access_mode='teams'` row. **A security rule with two answers is worse than a layering rule with one exception**, and `agent-identities › canSeeBaseRow` is the standing example of what the copy costs (*"IF THAT FILE'S RULE CHANGES, THIS ONE IS THE COPY THAT WILL NOT NOTICE"*). ⚠ **ITS LIMITS ARE PART OF IT**: PREDICATES ONLY (no repository, no service, no DTO), ONE WAY (nothing imports search), and the grant/team SETS the predicates take come from `src/shared/tenancy/`, never from another feature's reader. ⚠ **ONE ADDITION, 2026-09-17, AND IT IS INSIDE THE SUBSTRATE RATHER THAN OUTSIDE THE RULE**: closing F-716's teams residual, `repository-visibility.ts` also calls `teams/server/access.ts › listEffectiveAccess` + `› resolveLevel` — the same pair `knowledge › filterTeamVisibleBases` calls. It is the teams SUBSTRATE (the next sentence), not a fifth feature's reader, and it is still a PREDICATE-shaped call: a batch read plus a resolver, no repository of another feature reached. ⚠ Note that `@/features/teams/server/*` was ALREADY imported by four features (knowledge, skills, chats, workspaces) before this — teams is the access substrate and this bullet is what that practice should have carried all along.
- 🔒 **`packages/contracts` (`@dopl/contracts`) IS THE ONE DECLARATION OF EVERY CLOSED SET THAT CROSSES A TREE BOUNDARY (2026-09-02, v2 slice A13).** `packages/dopl-client` and `packages/mcp-server` **cannot import `src/`** — separate `tsc` programs resolved through `node_modules` — which is why 24 unions and shapes were re-typed by hand and three drift scripts existed to hold the copies together. Both trees now IMPORT and RE-EXPORT: `src/features/channels/types.ts`, `types-{sessions,direction,launch,ping}.ts`, `src/features/workspaces/types.ts`, `src/features/agent-identities/types.ts`, and their SDK counterparts. ⚠ **NOTHING IS RENAMED FOR A CONSUMER** — the server keeps `Role`, the SDK keeps `ChannelMemberRole` / `ChannelAuthorKind`, aliased through the import — and **no feature module may import `@dopl/contracts` directly**: the one path to a name is still its own tree's types file, or a second path to one symbol reappears. ⚠ **BOTH PACKAGES DECLARE IT AS A DEPENDENCY, INCLUDING `@dopl/mcp-server`, WHICH NAMES NO SYMBOL FROM IT (2026-09-02).** That is not a stray entry: `@dopl/client`'s emitted `.d.ts` files `import type … from "@dopl/contracts"`, so the mcp-server's own `tsc` program has to RESOLVE the package to typecheck the SDK it consumes. It did so only because npm workspaces hoist it — a phantom dependency, green until the day something installs the package alone or the hoist changes.
  - ⚠ **IT IS TYPE-ONLY, AND THAT IS WHAT LETS IT HAVE NO BUILD AND NO `dist/`.** `package.json` points `types` straight at `src/index.ts`, every import of it is an `import type`, and all four toolchains (Next/webpack, the SPA's Vite, two NodeNext `tsc` programs) erase it — verified by a runtime `require()` of the built SDK finding no reference. **A single `const`, function or `enum` in this package makes it a build input for every one of them** and re-opens the committed-`dist/` problem it exists to close. `workspaces/types.ts › isStandardWorkspace` is the worked example of something that therefore stays a hand mirror (§4A).
  - ⚠ **A TYPE BELONGS THERE WHEN THE SAME SET IS STATED IN TWO TREES — NOT BECAUSE IT IS SHARED-ISH.** A DTO only one tree ever builds does not go in, however tempting; the package's value is that it is small, closed and argued-over. `check-role-drift.ts › checkWorkspaceMirror` is the counter-example held OUT on purpose: those two interfaces were never the same shape (`iconUrl`, F-335).
  - **The census that keeps it true is `src/shared/contracts/canonical-sets.test.ts`** — the drift gates caught two copies DISAGREEING, and the failure that matters now is a second copy APPEARING, which compiles and silently shadows the package. It scans both trees INCLUDING the committed `dist/`, and counts literal declarations only (a re-export is the correct shape).
- 🔒 **A /home FACE THAT TWO TREES RENDER IS DECLARED IN `src/`, AND THE SPA RE-EXPORTS IT (2026-09-17).** `apps/desktop-ui` CAN import root `src/` (`@/shared/**`, and feature components — eleven /home pages already do); the Next tree can NOT import `apps/` at all (root `tsconfig.json` excludes it, and those files resolve `#/*` against the SPA's own src). So when the landing page's hero demo (`src/features/marketing/components/banner-demo/`) had to stop being a hand-transcribed copy of /home, the shared halves moved DOWN rather than being duplicated: `src/shared/ui/page-action-button.ts` (the black page pill), `› home-card-marks.tsx` (the card face and the two unread marks), `› home-channel-row.tsx` (the channel row's two lines), `src/features/home/tabs.ts` (the five faces) and `src/features/channels/components/home-channel-wells.ts` (the Pinned/Recent/Earlier set). ⚠ **EVERY SPA IMPORT PATH IS UNCHANGED** — `pages/home/{panel-buttons,channel-row-marks,home-tabs,channel-wells}` re-export, so nothing on that page learned a new specifier. ⚠ **WHAT DID NOT MOVE IS THE DERIVATION**: `channelTitle` / `channelPeople` / `hasLinkOut`, the `?? EMPTY_X` cache-shape fallbacks (§8) and `channelWellOf`'s pin-then-24h rule all stay with the reader of the cached payload — the shared modules take ANSWERS, so no fallback is applied twice. ⚠ **A SECOND DECLARATION OF ANY OF THESE IS THE BUG**, and two suites say so: `pages/home/panel-buttons.test.tsx` (no `"auth-btn-3d ` recipe anywhere in `pages/home`) and `marketing/components/banner-demo/demo-home-chrome.test.tsx` (no kit recipe re-spelled in the scene).
  - 🔒 **AND THE HERO SCENE IS CLIENT-ONLY, BECAUSE SHARING THE PRODUCT'S RECIPES MEANS SHARING ITS ASSUMPTION THAT A BROWSER IS RENDERING (2026-09-17).** `hero-banner.tsx` mounts `BannerDemo` through `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`. Server-rendering it failed hydration on every fresh load (`DemoChannelList → WellsColumn`), and **not because of anything the scene does wrong**: it prints channel-row stamps through `shared/lib/format-time.ts › formatChannelTimestamp`, which is correct for an app that only runs in a browser and has THREE reads a server cannot agree with — the fixture's `Date.now()` anchor at MODULE scope (server and client bundles are separate instances evaluated seconds apart), `toLocaleTimeString`'s RUNTIME time zone (UTC on the deploy, the reader's on the client), and its own `new Date()` same-day test. ⚠ **THE MIDDLE ONE CANNOT BE FIXED WITHOUT FORKING THE SHARED FORMATTER**, which the visual-match rules forbid — so the boundary is the fix, and `banner-demo-hydration.test.tsx` pins BOTH directions (clean under one clock; still failing under a 61s skew, which is the measurement the boundary rests on). ⚠ **A RECOVERABLE HYDRATION FAILURE RE-RENDERS THE WHOLE DOCUMENT ON THE CLIENT**, which is separately why the root layout's pre-paint `<script>` was logging *"Scripts inside React components are never executed when rendering on the client"* — one boundary, two symptoms, and `src/app/layout.tsx` carries the note so that tag is not "fixed" next time.
  - 🔒 **BUT SHARING THE COMPONENT DOES NOT SHARE THE STYLESHEET, AND THAT IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE RULE (2026-09-17).** The SPA loads `apps/desktop-ui/src/styles/index.css` — Tailwind, `tokens.css`, `kit.css` — **plus every CSS MODULE its pages import** (`pages/home/home.module.css`, `app-shell/account-rail.module.css`, …). The landing page loads `src/app/globals.css` (root layout) and `src/features/marketing/marketing.css` (`src/app/page.tsx`) and **nothing else**: no kit copy, and no module, because a module's class names are hashed and belong to the importing file. **So a recipe that lives only in a module or only in `kit.css` renders as NOTHING in the hero scene, silently** — which is how that scene can be built entirely from the product's own components and still read, in Samuel's words, *"super off"*. **A /home recipe the scene needs is PORTED into `marketing.css` under the demo's own prefix, byte-identical, with a comment naming its source rule** (`.lp-demo-rail*` ← `account-rail.module.css`). ⚠ **ONE SUCH PORT WAS DELETED ON 2026-09-17 AND THE REASON IS THE RULE, NOT AN EXCEPTION TO IT (R-38):** the six account-palette rules `.lp-demo-record` carried were a copy of `pages/home/home.module.css › .frame`; that fence is gone and the skin is `src/app/globals.css` › THE ACCOUNT PALETTE SKIN, **which the landing DOES load** — so the scene wears `data-frame-skin` and there is nothing left to port. **A recipe that moves from a module into `globals.css` un-ports itself; check before re-porting one.** ⚠ **THE GATE IS `marketing/components/banner-demo/demo-class-coverage.test.tsx`**, which COMPILES those two sheets with the same PostCSS plugin the Next build runs and asserts every class the scene renders resolves in the output — the answer cannot be grepped, because Tailwind generates its utilities from a source scan. It found a dead class (`lp-demo-rail-create`, emitted and defined nowhere) on its first run. Its one exemption is `lucide*`, which carries no style in either tree.
- **Hard cap 500 lines, lint-enforced at `error`.** `eslint.config.mjs › "max-lines"` = `{max:500, skipBlankLines:false, skipComments:false}` over **three globs: `src/**`, `packages/*/src/**` AND `apps/*/src/**`** — the SPA is capped too, on the same block. **Both `skip*` false — every physical line counts.** "It's mostly comments" is not an argument for an exemption.
- **A file at 500 cannot absorb a COMMENT.** Correcting a stale docblock in an at-cap file is a split, not a doc fix.
- **Exemptions are a closed list in `eslint.config.mjs` carrying "DO NOT ADD TO THIS LIST — split the file instead."**
- ✅ **THE SWEEP RETURNS THE EXEMPTION LIST AND NOTHING ELSE, AND THE ROOT LINT IS GREEN — re-measured 2026-09-17 (F-688 CLOSED).** `src/`+`packages/` answers THREE rows, and the exemption list names exactly those three: `src/shared/supabase/types.ts` (generated), `src/features/knowledge/server/seed-fixtures-data.ts` (data table), `src/features/billing/server/webhook-handler.test.ts`. `npm run lint -- --max-warnings 0` at the root exits 0, `apps/*/src` is at zero, and `packages/` is under the cap with no exemption list at all (F-689's split). **Re-measure, never quote** — and use THIS form, which prunes `node_modules`/`dist` and drops `wc`'s `total` row:
  ```
  find src packages \( -name node_modules -o -name dist \) -prune -o \( -name '*.ts' -o -name '*.tsx' \) -print | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>500 && $2!="total"'
  ```
  ⚠ **The naive `find src packages -name '*.ts' -o -name '*.tsx' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>500'` returns 73 rows, not 3** — the unparenthesized `-o` loses the path restriction, so it sweeps `node_modules` and the committed `dist/`, and `xargs` splits into batches that each emit their own `total`. A verification command that over-reports is worse than none: it trains you to ignore it.
  ⚠ **THIS BULLET SAID THE OPPOSITE FOR FIVE DAYS AND THE STORY IS WORTH ONE LINE**: on 2026-09-09 the sweep answered TWENTY, sixteen of them unexempted, and F-688 recorded the root lint as RED for reasons predating any one change. Sixteen splits then landed as their own contract changes arrived (§1's own rule: a split scheduled on a line count waits indefinitely, one scheduled by a new reason-to-change lands the same day), and F-689 took `packages/` the same way. 🔒 **The cap was never weakened to get here and must not be read as weakened** — it is still `error`, and a NEW file over it is still a bug. The exemption list also SHRANK by one over that window (`billing/components/upgrade-modal.tsx` left it), which is the only direction it may ever move.
- **Carve-outs (justify at top of file):** generated code, dense type-only files, pure data/config tables, and a single-function switch reducer that is one coherent state machine.
- **`dopl-desktop-app/` and `scripts/` are outside the root config.** The desktop has its own `eslint.config.js`, same rule, same severity, **zero exemptions**. `test/live/**/*.js` is its own block — the `.js` extension is load-bearing, it keeps that tier out of `node --test 'test/**/*.mjs'`.
- **Desktop runs with no headroom, and the NAMES change faster than the fact does.** ⚠ This bullet listed six files measured 2026-08-11 (`ui-sync.js`, `session-reducer.js`, `session-profiles.js`, `session-engine.js` at 500; `mcp-config.js`, `auth-tokens.js` at 499); **re-measured 2026-08-20, five of the six had moved** (397 / 498 / 374 / 477 / 424), which is exactly why a list of names is the wrong thing to write down here. **Re-run, never quote:**
  ```
  find dopl-desktop-app/{main,renderer,test,scripts} -name node_modules -prune -o -type f \( -name '*.js' -o -name '*.mjs' \) -print | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>=490 && $2!="total"' | sort -rn
  ```
  ⚠ **"Nothing in the desktop tree is over" WAS TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND IS NOT NOW — re-measured 2026-09-13: SEVEN desktop files exceed 500** (`renderer/app-preload.js`, and six `main/session-*.js`), so `cd dopl-desktop-app && npx eslint .` is red for reasons predating any one change and the honest local reading is "only NEW violations", exactly as the `src/` half of this section already says (F-688's shape, in the other tree). **The rule is not weakened by that**: the cap is still `error` with ZERO exemptions, and a NEW file over it is still a bug. Run the command; do not quote the number. ⚠ **AND "NOTHING SITS AT 500 EITHER" WAS TRUE ONLY FOR THE 2026-08-20 MEASUREMENT** (corrected 2026-08-23): **several `main/` modules sit AT the cap and several more are within two lines of it** — run the command above rather than trusting a list — which is the state this section's own next bullet is about — such a file cannot absorb a comment, so the next correction to any of them is a SPLIT. F-282 and F-283 are the standing entries. **Re-run the command; a list of names here rots faster than the fact does.** `test/eslint-config-coverage.test.mjs` asserts (via ESLint's own `calculateConfigForFile`) that every desktop file resolves to the cap — `main/`, `renderer/`, `test/**/*.mjs` and `test/live/**/*.js` alike, **zero exemptions**.
- **Split by responsibility, layer, or sub-feature** — one file per reason to change. For `op`-dispatched MCP tools the pattern is fixed: the original stays the thin **registrar** (schemas + `op` routing) and delegates to `<tool>-ops-read/-write/-admin.ts`, shared resolvers in `<tool>-shared.ts`/`-render.ts`. Keep the re-export barrel if callers import through it.
- **A split scheduled on a line count waits indefinitely; a split scheduled by a new reason-to-change lands the same day.**
  - ⚠ **AND ON 2026-09-02 THAT SENTENCE COST SEVEN SPLITS IN ONE SLICE.** The delivery-keystone wave (A9, §5) landed a contract change across `types.ts` (480), `schema.ts` (493), `service-writes.ts` (494), `service-launch.ts` (469), `packages/dopl-client/src/channel-types.ts` (500) and `main/session-dispatch.js` (448) — **every one of them within thirty lines of the cap, and one exactly AT it** — so the change could not land without splitting all six. **The seams were chosen by reason-to-change, never by size**: `types-delivery.ts` + `types-consent.ts`, `schema-members.ts` (matching `service-writes-members.ts`), `service-writes-direct.ts` (the DM lifecycle), a launch-posture module (on `service-launch-identity.ts`'s precedent; deleted 2026-09-23 when the web posture gate became a pass-through, review F9), `delivery-types.ts` + `session-types.ts` in the SDK, and `verdictFor` moving to `main/delivery-ack.js` beside the rank it spends. **This is the bullet above, measured**: a tree that runs at the cap converts every contract change into a refactor, and the refactor is the cheap part only while the seam is obvious.

## 1A. Loading states — per-page skeletons

**Written and measured 2026-08-28**, and **re-measured in full 2026-08-30** against the restructured
shell (see the GROUND bullet) — the whole section, not bullet-by-bullet, so the file-header date
above does not apply to it.

> ⚠ **LETTERED, NOT NUMBERED**, for the reason §5A states: §2…§14 are cited by number from `CLAUDE.md`
> and from docblocks across three trees. **Do not renumber this file to "fix" it.**

- **A PAGE'S LOADING STATE IS *THAT PAGE'S* SHAPE.** Samuel's ruling 2026-08-28, over the generic ghosts: *"way off"*, **re-stated 2026-09-10 over the two states that still had none** (see the FRAME bullet). ELEVEN surfaces now paint their own geometry — `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/home/home-skeleton.tsx` (the /home frame + its Knowledge and Agents faces), `src/features/channels/components/channel-record-skeleton.tsx` (the CHANNEL RECORD pane's face, 2026-09-13 — see the RECORD bullet; ⚠ **it moved down out of the SPA on 2026-09-17** and `pages/home/channel-record-skeleton.tsx` re-exports it, so the file counts below still resolve), `apps/desktop-ui/src/components/skeletons/knowledge-skeletons.tsx` (the knowledge ROOT and an OPENED base, one file because both hosts of that surface load through it), `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/overview/overview-skeleton.tsx`, `› pages/channels/channels-skeleton.tsx`, `› pages/identities/identities-skeleton.tsx`, `› pages/members/members-skeleton.tsx`, and `› components/skeletons/shell-skeleton.tsx` (the WORKSPACE SHELL's chrome, 2026-09-10). A ghost that resolves into a different surface than the one it stood for is worse than no ghost: it moves the content the operator was already reading toward. ⚠ **THE COUNT IS SHAPES, NOT FILES** (eight files export the eleven) — measure the files with `ls apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/*/*skeleton*.tsx apps/desktop-ui/src/components/skeletons/*skeleton*.tsx` and the shapes with the `SHAPES` table in `› components/skeletons/page-skeletons.test.tsx` (TEN PAGE shapes since 2026-09-13, when the /home record pane's channel ghost joined it — that row is what puts a shape under the three rules every one owes, while its byte-share pins live in `pages/home/channel-record-skeleton.test.tsx`, since they are all reads of ONE feature tree and this file sits at the 500-line cap) plus `› components/skeletons/frame-skeletons.test.tsx` (the shell's chrome, which is not a page and has no row in that table).
- 🔑 **THE GROUND IS THE SHELL'S, NOT THE SKELETON'S — and that is what the 2026-08-30 restructure settled.** A workspace page renders inside `src/shared/layout/app-shell/app-shell.module.css › .pageCard`, the WHITE card floating in the one gray panel, and `› .pageCard :global(.page-float)` collapses the page's own float to a plain filling box. **A skeleton wearing `page-float` therefore lands on exactly the ground its page lands on, with no per-skeleton repaint** — which is why the four pre-restructure ghosts needed no re-grounding and why adding one here would be the bug. What DOES follow the levels is anything a skeleton draws INSIDE the card: a section panel is the gray WELL (`SECTION_PANEL_GROUND`, level 3) in both the Agents ghost and the opened-base ghost, and the members detail band is `--surface-invert` because the real header is. Level table: `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md › The frame model ALTERNATES`. ⚠ **READ THE FLAT bullet BELOW BEFORE APPLYING THIS TO A NEW GHOST** — since 2026-09-21 a skeleton container paints no face at all, and the three ghosts named in this sentence are simply the ones not converted yet.
- 🔒 **SKELETONS ARE FLAT — SHIMMER BLOCKS ONLY (Samuel's ruling, 2026-09-21: *"we basically just shouldn't have elevated components"*).** A skeleton CONTAINER keeps its geometry and carries **no fill, no border and no shadow**; the only thing on screen is `src/shared/ui/skeleton.tsx › Skeleton` on the page's own ground. ⚠ **`border-transparent`, not a dropped border** — the box model must not move (`src/shared/ui/section-panel.tsx › SECTION_PANEL_GROUND`'s reasoning). ⚠ **THE APP FRAME IS NOT A SKELETON CONTAINER**: `app-shell.module.css`'s `.root` / `.surface` / `.pageCard` and the account rail are chrome that survives the read, and flattening them would tear the frame down for the load. ⚠ **CONVERTED THIS PASS: THE OVERVIEW GHOST, THE SHELL GHOST AND /home** — `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/overview/overview-skeleton.tsx` (the `bg-bg-inset` well and the `.bento` chart card are gone from the GHOST and still on the PAGE) and `apps/desktop-ui/src/components/skeletons/shell-skeleton.tsx` (the brand pill and the Pro card, stripped by `.brandPill[data-skeleton]` / `.wordsCard[data-skeleton]` — an ATTRIBUTE rule beside the real recipes, so the loaded sidebar is untouched and the ghost restates none of their padding). **/home converted too (`pages/home/home-skeleton.tsx › GHOST_FLAT_FACE`): the Usage cards dropped `.bento` and the channel-row ghost dropped `home-card-marks.tsx › HOME_CARD_FACE`'s `auth-btn-3d-light`, both still on the PAGE. ⚠ `SECTION_PANEL_GROUND` IS NOT ELEVATION AND STAYS — it is a flat panel gray, and the Knowledge and Agents ghosts Samuel named as the REFERENCE already stand on it. The members and channels ghosts are not converted — Samuel is looking at these first.** Pinned: `components/skeletons/page-skeletons.test.tsx › the overview ghost paints no container face, and the page still does` and `› frame-skeletons.test.tsx › strips the raised faces without restating an inset`, both bidirectional.
- 🔑 **THE COLD OPEN AND THE WORKSPACE SWITCH ARE FRAME STATES, AND THEY WERE THE LAST TWO GENERIC GHOSTS (Samuel, 2026-09-10: *"the loading skeleton for when i first open the app/when i switch workspaces doesnt look at all like the actual UI"*).** Both rendered `PageLoading` inside a bare full-screen box — `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/boot/index.tsx` (its `BootCover`, on `fixed inset-0 bg-white`) and `apps/desktop-ui/src/components/app-shell/app-shell.tsx`'s `isPending` gate (on `h-screen w-screen`) — so the app's frame (account rail, dark ground, sidebar, page card) was TORN DOWN for the read and rebuilt after it. **A frame that survives the read must survive its skeleton.** The switch now mounts `apps/desktop-ui/src/components/skeletons/shell-skeleton.tsx › ShellChromeSkeleton`, which composes the shell's own six boxes (`.root` / `.body` / `.surface` / `.sidebar` / `cn("page-float", .panel)` / `.pageCard` — six, not five: the sidebar ghost is drawn and pinned too, corrected 2026-09-14) around the ROUTED section's own page skeleton (`apps/desktop-ui/src/components/skeletons/section-skeleton.tsx › sectionSkeleton`, keyed off the same `activeSectionFromPath` the nav highlights with); the cold open mounts `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/home/home-skeleton.tsx › HomePageSkeleton`, because a cold launch resolves to the PERSONAL container and /home is its surface. ⚠ **THE RAIL IS RENDERED FOR REAL ON A SWITCH** — `GET /api/workspaces` is cached and IndexedDB-persisted, so the tile strip is known and stays clickable, lit off `parseSegment` of the ROUTED path (a publicId survives a slug rename). ⚠ **ONE `role="status"` PER SCREEN**: the chrome stands in `src/shared/ui/skeleton-surface.tsx › SkeletonChrome` — the module class WITHOUT the announcement, moved down 2026-09-17 with `SkeletonSurface` and re-exported from `apps/desktop-ui/src/components/skeletons/skeleton-surface.tsx` — and the page skeleton inside the card brings the status region.

the knowledge ghosts import the v2 module (`.cardGrid`, `.baseHead`, `.rail`, `.detailPane`, `.infoBody`) and contain **no** `232px`/`244px`; the Overview ghost byte-shares three strings with `pages/overview/{index,stat-cards,period-stats}.tsx` and **IMPORTS** its plot height from `components/charts/bar-series.tsx › PLOT_HEIGHT_CLASS` (2026-09-01 — the constant was module-local and unexported in `activity-chart.tsx`, so the ghost byte-shared a literal instead; the plot moved to a module SHARED with /home's Overview face and the ghost now takes the value the way the Channels ghost takes `COMPOSER_BOTTOM`, which is why the pin asserts the IMPORT and the ABSENCE of the literal); the Channels ghost byte-shares eight with `channels/components/{sidebar,sidebar-search,sidebar-rows,bits,message-pane,composer}.tsx` and **imports** `composer-input.tsx › COMPOSER_BOTTOM` rather than retyping `pb-4` (⚠ the 52px search strip is read from `sidebar-search.tsx` since 2026-09-17, when the column's search head was split off — the count did not move, the file did, exactly as the pane header's row did on 2026-09-01); the Members ghost byte-shares the page's grid identity and mounts `members-v2/bits.tsx › SECTION_CARD` itself; and each gate names its own skeleton and no longer imports `PageLoading`. ⚠ **THE FRAME PINS LIVE IN `› components/skeletons/frame-skeletons.test.tsx` SINCE 2026-09-10**, split off the 500-line cap: the shell ghost byte-shares its five box expressions with `app-shell.tsx`, the rail ghost mounts `account-rail.module.css`'s own `.rail` / `.tile` / `.workspaces` (the 2026-08-28 /home ghost restated `pt-[7px]` and silently stopped being the rail's shape when 2026-09-09 moved that pad to a `calc()`), /home's header ghost byte-shares `home-header.tsx`'s list CELL and draws one pill per `HOME_TABS` entry, and its record pane ghosts `HOME_DEFAULT_TAB`'s face — Overview — rather than the Channels transcript it drew for nine days after the page stopped landing there. ⚠ **A BYTE-SHARE PIN IS BIDIRECTIONAL** — it fails when the SKELETON drifts and when the PAGE does, which is the half that matters, since a re-tuned page is the only way a correct skeleton goes wrong. ⚠ **The scans strip comments first** — these files explain what they replaced, so a raw-text scan would fail on the very docblock recording the decision.

## 2. Data layer — repository / service / handler

- **Three layers.** `server/repository.ts` = pure data access, one function per query. ⚠ **It obtains its own client** — `supabaseAdmin()`, or `shared/supabase/caller-client.ts › readClient()` for a caller-scoped read (the split below) — **it does NOT take one from the service** (corrected 2026-09-23: this bullet said "takes a `SupabaseClient`, never creates one", which no feature repository did; only `knowledge/server/repository-audience.ts` and `repository-channel-grants.ts` take a `db: SupabaseClient` parameter, re-derive with `grep -lE ':\s*SupabaseClient' src/features/*/server/repository*.ts`). `server/service.ts` = business logic, throws domain errors. `server/dto.ts` = `snake_case`→`camelCase`. `server/errors.ts` = error classes.
- **No `snake_case` key leaks past `repository.ts`.**
- **Every workspace-scoped query is filtered by `workspace_id` at the repository.** This holds even where the read runs as service role — **service role bypasses RLS entirely**, so on that path the service IS the fence and RLS is not a backstop.
- 🔒 **A KNOWLEDGE, SKILL, IDENTITY, CHAT OR GRANT READ CAN NOW RUN AS THE CALLER, BEHIND `RLS_CALLER_SCOPED_READS`, AND THE FLAG IS OFF (2026-09-02, Wave B B7 then B12 / ruling B5).** `shared/supabase/caller-client.ts › readClient` returns the caller's own Postgres client when the flag is on inside a request and `supabaseAdmin()` otherwise, so **with the flag off every sentence above is unchanged**. The caller client is the anon key plus a 60-second JWT minted per caller (`caller-jwt.ts`) carrying `sub` and the CREDENTIAL AXES — one mint for BOTH lanes, the cookie/bearer session and the `dopl_at_` token, so `auth.jwt()` has one shape. The scope it is built from is established in `shared/auth/with-auth.ts` (the wrapper `withWorkspaceAuth` composes) via `with-auth-scope.ts`, from an ALREADY-VALIDATED credential — never from a header.
  - **THE SPLIT INSIDE THE REPOSITORY IS THE RULE, and it is stated in all six repository headers**: a read answering *what may this caller see* takes `readClient()`; a SYSTEM read — slug uniqueness, storage accounting, the `max(position)` append helpers, the chats re-export idempotency lookup, `countMessages`, the folder-propagation target set — keeps `supabaseAdmin()` and says so at the call site, because scoped to the caller it would answer a different question (a slug "free" because someone else's private base holds it). ⚠ Nothing ENFORCES the split yet (F-521); the RLS plan's Phase 0 lint rule is still unwritten.
  - ⚠ **THAT NUMBER IS STALE AGAIN — the gate prints FIFTEEN covered tables and SIXTEEN SELECT policies, re-derived 2026-09-09.** The five ontology tables joined with `20261001130000_ontology_readable` and `revisions` with `20261002120000_revisions` the same day; the bullet below still describes the NINE of phases 1–2 and is correct about those. **Do not trust the count in prose — run `npx tsx scripts/check-rls-pair-gate.ts`, which prints it.**
  - **NINE TABLES ARE COVERED, across two migrations, NEITHER APPLIED** (Docker is down here; replay owed). ⚠ **THIS BULLET SAID TEN AND LISTED `skill_files` AMONG THEM UNTIL 2026-09-02** — that table was dropped CASCADE in July 2026 (`20260716064733_collapse_skill_files_into_skills.sql`), so the eleventh entry was a policy for nothing and the tenth left with it (F-586, D1). **Re-derive: `npx tsx scripts/check-rls-pair-gate.ts` prints the count.** Phase 1 `20260919120000_rls_helpers_and_caller_scope`: `knowledge_bases`, `knowledge_folders`, `knowledge_entries`. Phase 2 `20260921120000_rls_phase2_policies`: `skills`, `agent_identities`, `chats`, `resource_grants` — the spec's target of SEVEN — plus the two CHILD tables fenced by a parent's rule (`chat_messages`, `agent_identity_knowledge_bases`). **Each rule is written ONCE as a predicate the policies call** — `dopl_knowledge_base_readable()`, `dopl_skill_readable()`, `dopl_chat_readable()`, `can_current_user_read_agent_identity()`, over the shared `dopl_public_teams_admits()` (the matrix `canSeeSkill` and `canSeeChat` share), `dopl_teams_mode_visible()` (the teams axis, `scope_type='team'` and all) and, since `20260923140000`, `dopl_grant_admits()` (the `channel|container` grant arm, F-604 — added to the KB and identity predicates in place, no policy moved). Each EQUALS its TS predicate; phase 2 closed four wider-than-fence gaps doing it (F-570). ⚠ **A CHILD IS COVERED WITH ITS PARENT OR NOT AT ALL**: `listVisibleChats` selects `*, chat_messages(count)`, so the child policy filters an embedded count. ⚠ **NO TS PREDICATE IS DELETED, AND B16 DID NOT DELETE ONE EITHER (F-650, 2026-09-02).** The spec gave B16 that row; the row's own condition was unmet twice — `RLS_PHASE_2` is default-OFF over migrations no database has, and the `rls-redteam` job that would make a "green redteam test" mean anything has never run — so with every repository still on `supabaseAdmin()` the TS predicate is the ONLY live fence and deleting one would replace a fence with nothing. **Deferred to RLS phase 3, whose two preconditions are named in F-650:** the flag default-ON for one release, and `rls-redteam` green in CI per predicate against a real database. ⚠ **AND THE AGENT AUDIENCE CEILING IS NOT IN THE POLICIES** (§10, F-524): it is a per-request bound, not a property of a row, so `service-audience.ts › audienceAdmits` is NOT covered and must not be deleted with `canSeeBase`.
  - **THE PROOF IS ONE REDTEAM SUITE PER TABLE, and they share a scanner.** `{knowledge,skills,chats,agent-identities}/server/rls-redteam.test.ts` + `shared/supabase/rls-redteam-resource-grants.test.ts`, over `shared/supabase/rls-policy-scan.ts` (replays every migration in filename order — a later `DROP POLICY` is as load-bearing as the `CREATE`) and `rls-redteam-fixture.ts` (the live half, **skipped-with-reason**: no database here). ⚠ **A STRUCTURAL ASSERTION IS NOT A BEHAVIOURAL ONE** (F-523): the SQL half proves the rule is written once and names every arm; only the live half proves Postgres agrees.
- **A route handler is ≤80 lines and thin.** Pages never talk to Supabase; an RSC and its API twin read the same service code so they cannot drift.
- **A DTO carrying PII needs an ENTITLEMENT decision, not just a shape decision.** The viewer is a DTO INPUT: `channels/server/dto.ts › mapMemberRow` takes `viewerUserId` and scrubs private fields to the caller's own row.
- **Per-member settings are private BY COLUMN PRIVILEGE — not by policy, not by the DTO.** RLS filters ROWS; the requirement is a COLUMN. `channel_members` has `SELECT` revoked from `anon`/`authenticated` with a per-column `GRANT` of public columns only; `agent_tool_profile` is service_role-only, which binds PostgREST and realtime frames both. **Standing rule for any NEW per-member setting: add it to the DTO scrub AND leave it out of that migration's `GRANT` list. Two edits; the second is the one that binds.** Keep the scrub — it shapes the API response, where the server reads as service role and the column privilege redacts nothing.
  - **The worked example is `favorited_at` (`20260819120000`, §5's favourites bullet).** ⚠ The second edit is an ABSENCE, not a statement: a column added by `ALTER TABLE` inherits nothing from the earlier per-column `GRANT`, so it is service_role-only the moment it exists and the migration adds no grant. An absence is what silently stops being true — so that file **asserts the outcome in a `DO $$` block** (`has_column_privilege('authenticated', …, 'favorited_at', 'SELECT')` must be false) rather than trusting it, because restoring the table-wide grant (the documented ROLLBACK of `20260810120000`) would hand this column out with no error anywhere and take `agent_tool_profile` with it.
  - ⚠ **AND IT IS A CONVENTION RATHER THAN AN EXAMPLE SINCE 2026-09-07**, when `channel_members.unaddressed_responder` (`20260928130000`, §5) became the second per-member setting to pay both edits: scrubbed in `channels/server/dto.ts › mapMemberRow` (which now nulls **four** own-preference fields for everyone but the viewer — `notify_scope`, `agent_tool_profile`, `favorited_at`, `unaddressed_responder`), absent from every `GRANT`, and **carrying `favorited_at`'s `DO $$` assertion block verbatim in shape**. ⚠ **THE ASSERTION IS NOT OPTIONAL BOILERPLATE**: it is the only thing that turns "we added no grant" from an unstated absence into a statement the migration will fail on. A new private column that skips it is the one failure mode this whole rule exists to catch.
- **Errors: throw, don't return tuples.** Convert at the boundary. The three real pieces are `src/shared/lib/http-error.ts › HttpError` (the class, and `toResponseBody()` is the ONE place the envelope shape is decided), `shared/api/parse-json.ts › parseJson`, and the shared catch-block helper `shared/api/http-error-response.ts › toHttpErrorResponse(source, err, mapDomainError?)` — imported by ~53 modules. Four feature wrappers delegate to it with their own domain mapper (`toKnowledgeErrorResponse`, `toChatErrorResponse`, `toSkillErrorResponse`, `channels/server/http-mapping.ts › toChannelErrorResponse`). Never a raw error string or a stack trace.
  - ⚠ **There is NO `withErrorHandler` and no `shared/api/error-handler.ts`** — that pairing has never existed in this repo. It is a docs-only fiction that lived in ENGINEERING.md for months and was copied into this file's first draft; `scripts/check-doc-refs.mjs` now resolves `path › symbol` anchors specifically so this class of claim cannot be written again. Conversion is a **catch block calling `toHttpErrorResponse`**, not a wrapper composed around the handler.
- **A NEW route uses the NESTED envelope — `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`** — because that is what `HttpError.toResponseBody()` returns and what every `toHttpErrorResponse` path emits. **The FLAT `{error, message, workspaces?}` shape in §4 is workspace RESOLUTION only**, surfaced verbatim by `@dopl/client`; it is a legacy surface with clients parsing it, not a second option to pick from. Two shapes exist; only one is choosable.
- **Never send `Cache-Control: no-transform`.** It forbids intermediaries applying a content coding — an instruction NOT to compress, not a stronger `no-cache`. What an SSE route needs is `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (`shared/api/sse-keep-alive.ts`).

Why/history: ENGINEERING.md §3, §8, §12.

## 3. Auth wrappers & caller-type gates

**The wrappers that EXIST** (`grep -rn "^export function with" src/shared/auth/`, verified 2026-08-11; `withMcpAccess` deleted 2026-09-23 — no route used it):

| Symbol | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `withUserAuth(handler)` | `shared/auth/with-auth.ts` | OAuth bearer (`dopl_at_*`) OR session cookie; injects `{userId, agentTokenId?, apiKeyWorkspaceId?, credentialSubjectUserId, params}` — the CONTAINER axis and the SUBJECT axis (§10, `credential-audience.ts`); logs 5xx |
| `withWorkspaceAuth(handler, opts)` | `shared/auth/with-workspace-auth.ts` | Composes `withUserAuth`; resolves workspace fail-closed, verifies membership + `meetsMinRole`. **Default for workspace-scoped content routes.** |
| `isAdmin(userId)` | `shared/auth/with-auth.ts` | Site-admin check vs `ADMIN_USER_ID` |
| `requireCronSecret(request)` | `shared/auth/require-cron-secret.ts` | Bearer gate for `/api/cron/*`; fail-closed 503 when unset |

⚠ **`withExternalAuth` and `withAdminAuth` DO NOT EXIST** — **zero hits in `src/` + `packages/`**, verified 2026-08-11. Not "zero hits repo-wide": four DOC mentions survive, and all four are correct in place — `ENGINEERING.md:500` (**corrected 2026-08-11 in this same batch**; it now names the fiction as a fiction and points here), `docs/CLEANUP.md` (a dated capture, describing the tree as it was), and this line. **ENGINEERING no longer asserts these wrappers exist; do not "fix" it again.** Do not import or "restore" them, and do not invent a `requireUser` either.

- ⚠ **THE RETURNED HANDLER'S SECOND PARAMETER IS REQUIRED, AND IT IS A TYPE CONTRACT WITH NEXT RATHER THAN A STYLE CHOICE (2026-08-25).** It is `shared/auth/with-auth.ts › RouteContextArg` (`{ params: Promise<…> }`, exported for that reason). Next generates, per route it compiles IN DEV, a `.next/dev/types/app/api/**/route.ts` asserting the exported handler's second arg extends its own `RouteContext`, and `tsconfig.json` INCLUDES that tree — so an OPTIONAL parameter (or one given a DEFAULT, which does not make a parameter required in the function type) infers `… | undefined` and reddens every wrapped route the dev server has served. **CI never sees it: a clean checkout has no `.next/`.** The gate was therefore red only on the machine running the mandated always-on dev stack, which is the machine doing the work. Pinned by `shared/auth/route-context-signature.test.ts`, which mirrors the generated shapes and goes red at `tsc` on either regression. `withMcpAccess` / `withWorkspaceAuth` inherit the signature.
- **Service-layer gates:** `features/workspaces/server/authz.ts › requireWorkspaceRole` (the one membership-fetch+role-check helper) and the pure hierarchy in `features/workspaces/member-policy.ts`, shared with the members UI.
- **Two caller-type options, orthogonal to `minRole`. Cookie/session callers authenticate AS the human and are NEVER gated by either — these only constrain OAuth tokens.**
  - **`writeScopeExempt` (default: gate ON).** OAuth bearer on any non-`GET` without `dopl.write` → 403 `WRITE_SCOPE_REQUIRED` + `WWW-Authenticate: insufficient_scope`. **TWO routes carry it, both MCP PLUMBING rather than content writes** (2026-08-11): `user/mcp-status` (the liveness ping) and `mcp/credits/consume` (the §10 credit charge — a READ-ONLY session still costs a credit per tool call, so gating it on `dopl.write` would make read-only agents free). **Neither is `sessionOnly`**: every MCP caller is an OAuth token, so a session gate would refuse the only caller there is. The pinned set is in `write-gate-coverage.test.ts`; adding a third is an edit there.

## 4. Workspace resolution — fail-closed

`features/workspaces/server/service.ts › resolveActiveWorkspace(userId, headerWorkspaceId)` is THE resolver behind `withWorkspaceAuth` and `GET /api/workspaces/me`:

1. 🔒 **CREDENTIAL WORKSPACE LOCK** (in `withWorkspaceAuth`, before the resolver) — a contradicting target → 403 `API_KEY_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH`, and the lock **OVERRIDES** rather than merely validating: a locked caller cannot fall through to step 3's auto-target either. ✅ **THIS STOPPED BEING "DEAD SCAFFOLDING; PRESERVED" ON 2026-08-26 — IT HAS A PRODUCER (Home Knowledge Panels M5, plan §4.4 B1; Samuel's RULING 4).** `mcp_tokens.container_id` (migration `mcp_token_credential_axes`, §12 — it supersedes `workspace_id`, which is dual-written and dual-read until B13) is read by `shared/auth/mcp-oauth.ts › validateAccessToken` and forwarded as `apiKeyWorkspaceId` by **both** wrapper families — `shared/auth/with-auth.ts` and `shared/auth/with-mcp-transport-auth.ts`. `shared/auth/mcp-container-token.ts › issueContainerToken` mints them: the desktop asks for one when it spawns a session into a `kind='link'` container that has a PEER in it, and revokes it at session end.
   - ⚠ **THE ENFORCEMENT CHAIN WAS INTACT AND THE PRODUCER WAS MISSING AT *THREE* LAYERS, WHICH IS WORSE THAN THIS BULLET USED TO SAY.** The `api_keys` table it was written for was dropped by `20260609000000_drop_api_key_auth.sql`; `with-auth.ts` never wrote the field in ANY of its three auth branches (its own docblock said *"always undefined"*); and `with-mcp-transport-auth.ts` passed a hardcoded `null`. So the 403 above, and every gate downstream, had been unreachable code rather than an unused feature. **Re-derive, never quote:** `grep -rn apiKeyWorkspaceId src/shared/auth`.
   - 🔒 **IT IS THE ONLY PART OF THE AUDIENCE CEILING THAT BINDS A PROCESS'S CHILDREN.** A `full` profile has Bash and the operator's 90-day device token is on disk, so an agent can issue any loopback HTTP the operator could — which is why the MCP directory lock (§10) and the desktop grant gate (§11) are TRIPWIRES. A lock on the TOKEN ROW is different in kind: everything the agent shells out to can only present the credential it was handed, and that credential names one workspace.
   - 🔒 ✅ **IT LIT UP EVERY M-10 GATE AT ONCE AND THAT WAS A DEFECT, NOT THE DESIGN — F-336/F-333, RULED BY SAMUEL AND FIXED 2026-08-27.** This bullet used to say the visibility gates biting was intended: `apiKeyWorkspaceId` non-null made `knowledge/server/service-shared.ts › canSeeBase` refuse a **PRIVATE** base outright — the caller's OWN included — and the mirrors in chats, skills and agent-identities, plus the `fromWorkspaceKey` branches in the three write services, did the same. **The lock answers WHICH WORKSPACE; visibility answers WHICH ROWS INSIDE IT.** Using one for the other made the operator's own private base unreadable by the operator's own agent *even when granted `agent_only`* (the visibility gate 404s before layer A's grant row is read), and made every `containerCopyDraft` identity invisible to the agents it was copied for. **The predicates now ask `shared/auth/credential-audience.ts › isSharedCredential`, never the lock.** ✅ **AND SINCE 2026-09-02 (wave B slice B3) THE ROW STATES THE ANSWER INSTEAD OF THE PREDICATE INFERRING IT.** `workspace_lock_kind` was a KIND read as evidence of a PERSON — the same inference in a smaller place — so `mcp_token_credential_axes` (§12) splits the row into two independent axes: `container_id` (WHICH container) and `subject_user_id` (WHOSE reach, `NULL` = nobody in particular). `isSharedCredential` is now ONE NULL CHECK on `credentialSubjectUserId`, and the axis is a REQUIRED field on every context that reaches a gate — this was the field whose ABSENCE used to widen, and the typechecker is now what enumerates its construction sites. **All four combinations are meaningful**: fenced+personal (a container session), fenced+anonymous (a shared container key — denied every private row), unfenced+personal (a device token), unfenced+anonymous. ⚠ **The 403 in step 1, and every other CONTAINER gate, is untouched.** Re-derive: `grep -rn 'isSharedCredential\|credentialSubjectUserId' src`.
   - 🔒 ✅ **AND THE LOCK IS ENFORCED IN *BOTH* AUTH FAMILIES SINCE 2026-08-26 — IT WAS ENFORCED IN ONE.** Step 1 above is `withWorkspaceAuth`'s. The OTHER family — `withUserAuth` + `workspaces/server/segment.ts › resolveApiWorkspace` / `resolveApiWorkspaceAccess`, i.e. everything under `/api/workspaces/[workspaceSlug]/**` — had **zero references to `apiKeyWorkspaceId`**, so `mcp-container-token.ts`'s claim that *"that credential cannot name another workspace"* was a property of ONE WRAPPER, not of the credential. **The reachable walk:** `POST /api/boot` with NO segment answers the caller's own container — its id AND its canonical segment — to any valid credential; ⚠ **the function it called then was `ensureDefaultWorkspace`, which no longer exists** (wave B B14 replaced it with `ensurePersonalContainer`, and the walk is the same walk whichever row is answered); that segment is then the argument the 19 `resolveApiWorkspace` route files take (access-matrix, members-with-emails, overview, overview-series, teams, invitations, join-link, my-access, member activity). **The comparison now lives ONCE, in `resolveWorkspaceSegmentForUser` (`› withinKeyLock`), beside the role floor the guest wave put there for exactly the same reason**, and boot's PROVISIONING branch refuses a locked caller outright before it reads anything.
     - ⚠ **IT IS THREADED BY EVERY CALLER, NOT DEFAULTED, AND THAT IS THE TRADE.** `ApiWorkspaceOpts.apiKeyWorkspaceId` has no fail-closed default available to it — the resolver cannot see a credential nobody handed it, and a request-scoped ambient would answer "no lock" on a scope miss, i.e. fail OPEN. So the resolver holds the COMPARISON and `workspaces/server/api-workspace-floor.test.ts` (its caller-scan block) holds the THREADING: every route file in the family must name the field, and every resolve call in them must pass it. **A pin on the fence is not a pin on its callers; here both are pins.**
     - ⚠ **A REFUSAL IS `null` → the caller's existing 404**, the same answer a non-member gets — so the lock cannot be used to learn that a workspace exists, and no route grows a new error shape. Blank-after-trim reads as NO lock on both doors.
   - **A CHILD CREDENTIAL IS NEVER MORE THAN ITS PARENT** — minted for the caller's own user id, under the caller's own proved membership, with the same scopes a device token carries, and then NARROWED. ## 4A. Home channels & workspace KINDS (2026-08-23, INVERTED 2026-08-24)

> A **HOME CHANNEL** is an account-level channel carried by a hidden **link container**: a `kind='link'` workspace holding exactly ONE channel and **ONE OR MORE** members. **CREATION IS FIRST-CLASS AND COMES FIRST** — "New channel" mints a SOLO container (one member, one PRIVATE NON-DIRECT channel) which the operator works in with their own agents, and which is a finished thing on its own. **PEERS JOIN AFTER THE FACT**, and by exactly one route: a link **BOUND** to that container (`channel_links.workspace_id`), whose claim inserts the claimer as a member. **THE ROSTER HAS NO CEILING (Samuel's ruling, 2026-08-26)** — it grows ONE PERSON AT A TIME, each by their own single-use link.

- 👥 **THE ROSTER IS A LIST ON THE PAYLOAD, AND `peer` IS ITS HEAD (2026-08-26, the ruling's second half — F-307 RESOLVED).** 🔒 **SINCE R-26 (2026-09-17) IT IS `channels/types-list.ts › ChannelRowExtras.peers: ChannelPeer[]`, READ BY `channels/server/repository-list-extras.ts › listChannelPeerIds`** — `HomeChannel.peers`, `HomePeer` and the whole second projection are DELETED, and the roster is now the CHANNEL's (`channel_members`) rather than the container's, which on a `kind='link'` container is the same set by construction. It carries EVERY other member, ordered `joined_at ASC, user_id ASC`. ⚠ **THE `user_id` TIEBREAKER IS LOAD-BEARING**: `joined_at` alone is not a TOTAL order, and two members admitted in the same millisecond (or legacy rows carrying NULL) would flip between loads — which was the bug. ⚠ **`peer` IS GONE, NOT KEPT** — it was a DERIVED back-compat projection of `peers[0]` for a cache entry written before `peers` existed, and both that payload and its cache entry left with the second projection; `home-rows.ts › channelPeople` is a plain `?? EMPTY_PEERS` now. The rule it bought survives: two fields that can disagree about who is in a room is what F-307 was.
  - 🔒 **KEEPING `peer` IS A §8 DECISION, NOT BACK-COMPAT SENTIMENT.** A cache entry written before this wave HAS `peer` and LACKS `peers`, so a client that knew only the list would fall back to `[]` and paint EVERY channel as solo on the first paint after the upgrade — "Just you", the agent glyph, no faces. **That is a FALSE sentence about who is in the room**, where degrading to one face is merely the old correct answer. The client's fallback is therefore a two-field MERGE, not a plain `?? EMPTY_PEERS`.
  - **ONE READ SITE, AND IT IS PINNED AS AN ABSENCE.** `pages/home/home-rows.ts › channelPeople` is the only thing on the home page that names `.peers`; `› channelTitle` (two names, then `+N`), `› channelSubline` ("Just you" / the address / `N people`) and every component go through it. ⚠ **It is an ACCESSOR, which §8 normally forbids** — the exemption is bought by `home-rows.test.ts`, which reads the directory's SOURCE and fails if any other file names `.peers` outside a comment. **Take the exemption only with the pin.**
  - **THE ROW DRAWS A STACK AT 2+** (`pages/home/relationship-list.tsx` → `shared/ui/avatar-stack.tsx › AvatarStack`, `size="sm"` `max={3}`; the Info-tab header does the same at `md`). `AvatarStack` GAINED a size (default `xs`, so its four older callers are byte-identical) rather than the home page forking a fifth stack. ⚠ **The stack's sizes are `avatar.tsx › SIZE`'s to the pixel**, or a row changes height the moment a second person joins. ⚠ **`+N` counts what is HIDDEN, not the total.**
  - ⚠ **THE INFO TAB'S EMAIL ROW IS A ONE-PERSON ROW AND IS DROPPED ABOVE ONE** (Samuel's call, 2026-08-26). It was already absent on a SOLO channel — a row answering a question nobody asked; with three members it answers about the WRONG person, since the header names two others. **Every member's address is one section down in the roster, beside their face.** Do not "fix" this by stacking N Email rows: the card is curated and capped, and the roster IS that list.
- 🔑 **THE PAYLOAD CARRIES THE CALLER'S OWN ROLE IN EACH CONTAINER, AND /home's ROLE-SHAPED CONTROLS GATE ON IT (2026-09-17, F-343 RESOLVED).** `home/types.ts › HomeChannel.role` is `workspace_members.role` for the caller, derived server-side by `channels/server/repository-list-extras.ts › listMyContainerRoles` — one bounded query in the tier that already reads peers, **never a client param**. ⚠ **THE SAME ROLE VOCABULARY AND THE SAME LADDER THE WORKSPACE USES** (`workspaces/types.ts › Role` through `meetsMinRole`), not a second predicate and not a `canManage` boolean: the floors it answers differ per control, and one flag could not say both. **`containerTarget.role` is no longer hardcoded `"owner"`** — that comment ("a home container is the caller's own") was true of the container the caller CREATED and false of every one they JOINED, where a bound claim seats them at the link's `granted_role`.

A channel-less call (Claude Desktop / Claude Code MCP connections, app clicks) charges the resource's container as before and is filed as **Desktop agent**; a SUB-AGENT is filed under the channel ITS OWN session lives in, which needs no rule because it sends its own slot key. ## 5. Channels — core model

> A **CHANNEL** (or DM) holds many **THREADS**.
> A **THREAD** is ONE exchange between two members about one thing — a single message or a long piece of work. It is SHARED: both members see the same thread, title, and status.
> A **SESSION** is ONE member's agent run working a thread, on THAT member's machine. Each side has its own. A session pauses and resumes; a thread does not. You never see the other member's session, only the messages it sends.

Inside a member's own window there is exactly ONE session, so it never needs a qualifier — **never write "agent session" or "channel session" in UI copy.**

- ⚠ **THERE IS EXACTLY ONE CHANNELS SURFACE, AND IT IS THE PORTED ONE (2026-08-18, wiring plan Phase 12 — the CUTOVER).** `/:workspaceSegment/channels` and `/:workspaceSegment/channels/:channelId` are two rows over ONE page component (`apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/channels/index.tsx`) over `channels/components/channels-core.tsx`. **The temporary `channels-v2` route, its page folder, its nav row and its deep-link key are GONE** — a re-added row would resolve to nothing — and the two-pane page went with them: `channels-view-core.tsx`, `channel-pane.tsx`, `channels-list-pane.tsx`, `rooms-sidebar.tsx`, `channel-transcript.tsx`, `message-composer.tsx`, plus `activity-event-row.tsx`, `address-picker.tsx`, `lib/agent-display.ts` and `hooks/use-channel-agents.ts`, orphaned by their removal.
  - ⚠ **THE SURFACE'S COMPONENTS ARE `src/features/channels/components/` AND NOTHING IS CALLED `v2` ANY MORE (Samuel, 2026-09-14: *"nothing should be named channels v2, it's just channels now"*).** The `channels-v2/` sub-folder was folded up into `channels/components/` on that date — the core is `channels/components/channels-core.tsx` and the selection hook `channels/components/use-channels-selection.ts` — and every `ChannelsV2*` symbol became `Channels*`. Every anchor in this file points into `channels/components/`. - **`task` == `thread` at the storage boundary, deliberately.** DOMAIN name is `thread` everywhere a human or agent reads (`ChannelThread`, `channels/components/threads-tab.tsx`, `useChannelThreads`, the MCP ops). STORAGE name stays `task`: the `channel_tasks` table, the `metadata.taskId`/`taskMode`/`taskCreatedBy`/`taskTitle`/`taskTarget` wire keys, the `task_*` kinds, the `TASK_*` codes, the `/tasks/**` route paths. A boundary comment marks the mapping in each crossing file.
- **`seq` IS NOT PER-CHANNEL.** The identity sequence lives on the TABLE, so one global counter serves every channel in every workspace: globally unique, strictly increasing per channel but **GAPPY**. **A seq RANGE is never a message count**, and **a cursor is only ever a number the server HANDED you** — never guessed.
- **THE TRANSCRIPT IS A KEYSET WINDOW, NEVER AN OFFSET, AND NEVER THE WHOLE CHANNEL (2026-09-01, F-053 resolved).** `schema-reads.ts › MessageReadQuerySchema` carries **both ends of one window** — `since` walks forward (the await/desktop incremental read), `before` walks backward (the UI's scroll-up page) — and `channels/server/repository-messages.ts › listMessages` is ONE builder with three modes. **What varies is which end the `limit` bites**, not which rows qualify: only the forward mode reads ascending, and a `before` page read ascending would return the channel's oldest `limit` rows every time, i.e. the same page forever. Both predicates ride `channel_messages_channel_seq_idx` on `(channel_id, seq)`, so page N costs what page 1 did. **A `before` page moves NO read watermark** (`service-reads.ts › readMessages`) — history cannot advance a monotonic cursor, and skipping the arithmetic says so.
  - 🔒 **THE SCROLL-BACK HISTORY IS NOT A QUERY-CACHE ENTRY, AND MUST NOT BECOME ONE.** `hooks/use-channel-messages.ts` keeps the newest page as the one `useApiQuery` entry (the entry every optimistic write patches, §8) and holds older pages beside it in `lib/message-window.ts`. A `?before=` sibling entry would sit under the SAME prefix key `use-thread-writes-shared.ts › messagesKey` patches — TanStack matches by array PREFIX — so every send would append its pending row into every loaded page of history, at a `nextSeq` derived from that page's own maximum. **The cost of the choice: a cache patch does not reach the window.** The one that matters is the thread DELETE, so `message-window.ts › dropThreadFromWindow` exists and `channel-surface.tsx` calls it on the delete's own exit callback. Anything added to that write family needs the same treatment or it is half-applied.
  - 🔒 **THE NEWEST PAGE CAN OUTRUN THE LOADED WINDOW, AND A `seq` GAP IS NOT EVIDENCE.** The newest page is refetched on every doorbell and always returns the newest page, so its minimum walks forward; land more than a page between two paints (a working agent posting `task_progress` will) and it steps past where history stopped, leaving rows neither half holds. **`seq` is table-wide (bullet above), so consecutive posts in one channel are never consecutive numbers** and no arithmetic over the rows on hand can detect the hole. `message-window.ts › isContiguous` checks a REMEMBERED boundary cursor instead, and the window is **dropped rather than concatenated** — a rendered hole is two adjacent rows minutes apart with nothing saying why.
  - 🔒 **THE UI TRANSCRIPT PAGES BY ESTIMATED RENDERED LINES, NOT BY ROWS (2026-09-08, Samuel: *"a message can be like 20 lines or it can be 2 lines … lets do 300 as the line chunk"*).** `constants.ts › CHANNEL_TRANSCRIPT_LINE_BUDGET` (300) sizes the page and `› CHANNEL_TRANSCRIPT_PAGE_MAX_ROWS` (= `MAX_MESSAGE_LIMIT`, 200) is the hard row cap under it; **`CHANNEL_TRANSCRIPT_PAGE_SIZE` (50 rows) IS DELETED — there is no alias**, so a caller still paging by rows is a compile error. The estimator is `lib/transcript-line-budget.ts › estimateMessageLines` (`sum over physical lines of max(1, ceil(chars/80))`, min 1 per message, fenced code counted verbatim) and it is an ESTIMATE FOR PAGING ONLY — never render from it. **The trim lives in the SERVICE** (`server/service-reads.ts › readMessagePage` calls `› takeLineBudget`): one keyset query for the row cap, trimmed to a SUFFIX so the caller's next `before` — the oldest returned `seq` — is exact, always at least one message. **`lineBudget` is an OPT-IN query param** (`schema-reads.ts › MessageReadQuerySchema`, refused together with `since`), so the MCP / desktop / await reads page by row exactly as before.
  - 🔒 **`hasMore` COMES FROM THE SERVER AND MAY NOT BE RE-DERIVED FROM `rows.length` ANYWHERE (2026-09-08).** A line-budgeted page is SHORT BY DESIGN, so the usual `rows.length === pageSize` test reports a channel of long messages as exhausted on its first screen and hides the rest of its history. The route puts it on the wire on every read; `hooks/use-channel-messages.ts › hasOlder` is `!window.exhausted && data.hasMore && …` and `lib/message-window.ts › appendOlderPage` takes the flag rather than a `limit`. **Both ends fall back to `true` ("maybe more") for a payload that predates the key** (§8) — failing toward one extra fetch, never toward hidden history — with an EMPTY page still latching `exhausted`, since nothing can exist below a page with no rows. ⚠ **A SMALLER FIRST PAGE IS A SMALLER DERIVATION WINDOW:** the channel view's thread cards, escalation cards and outbound send-box join are all derived from the messages ON SCREEN, so a thread quieter than a page has no card until the reader scrolls back. The Threads tab is the record of record for that question and has its own read.
- **Serialized append.** All inserts go through the `channel_message_insert` RPC (service-role EXECUTE only), which takes a per-channel `pg_advisory_xact_lock` **before** the insert, so `seq` commits in strict monotonic order — no committed-out-of-order hole a reader could poll past. Every writer uses it. ⚠ This bullet said "the cron sweep included" until 2026-08-18; **the stale-threads cron was deleted at wiring plan Phase 4** (§13) and the clause named a writer that no longer exists.
- **Channels RLS is stricter than the older tables:** INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE REVOKEd from `authenticated`+`anon`, write policies dropped — **every write is service-role-only through the feature service.** Member SELECT remains for reads and feeds the publication.
- **ADDRESSING IS REQUIRED, FULL STOP — an unaddressed ask triggers NOBODY, in any channel, at any member count.** ⚠ **STRENGTHENED 2026-08-18 (wiring plan Phase 3): the IMPLICIT TRIGGER and the DM AUTO-ADDRESS both RETIRED, in the same change.** The rule used to have two holes in it — `classify` fired on a **known-exact `memberCount === 2`** plus explicit membership, and `resolvePostMetadata` stamped a DM peer into `to_user_id` when the caller named nobody — so "unaddressed reaches nobody" was true only at 3+ and only outside a DM. Both are gone: `to_user_id` comes from the validated `toUserId` and nowhere else, and `classify` no longer reads the member count at all. **Fail-closed BY DESIGN, and now without exception. Never add a broadcast trigger and never re-add a count-keyed one** — the first converts the loop brake into a storm, the second makes the ROSTER a behaviour (below).
  - `GROUP_CHANNEL_MIN_MEMBERS = 3` in `features/channels/constants.ts` SURVIVES, deliberately duplicated in `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/channel-addressing.ts` (no shared source tree) and pinned together by `channel-addressing-rule.test.ts` — but it is **now a COPY threshold only.** Nothing branches on it; it decides whether the MCP roster line names a count or talks about "the other member". ⚠ **"Nothing branches on it" was FALSE in `src/**` until 2026-08-18 (wave-2 fix pass):** `components/invite-dialog.tsx › GroupChannelRoutingNote` both gated on `memberCount < GROUP_CHANNEL_MIN_MEMBERS - 1` and recited the threshold in its copy. **Its only reader in `src/**` is now the constant's own file.** ⚠ The command this bullet used to print (`grep -rn GROUP_CHANNEL_MIN_MEMBERS src/`) does NOT show that — it returns hits in three files, the extras being docblock prose that names the constant while explaining why nothing branches on it. **A verification command that contradicts the claim above it trains a reader to ignore both.** Count READERS, not mentions: `grep -rn 'GROUP_CHANNEL_MIN_MEMBERS' src/ | grep -v '^\s*\*'`.
  - ⚠ **THIS IS A SHIP-ORDERED PAIR (§13): WEB DEPLOYS BEFORE A DESKTOP BUILD.** An old desktop against a new server keeps firing its implicit trigger on 2-member channels until it updates — noisy and safe. A new desktop against an old server is the direction that breaks.
- **THE REQUEST FAN-OUT: N addressees, N threads, ONE card.** A thread stays one requester + one target, so the "New agent thread" panel's send loops `createTask` per addressee (`channels/server/service-tasks-broadcast.ts › createTaskFanOut`; `createTask` itself is unchanged and the fan-out is a CALLER). Two keys carry it and both are load-bearing:
  - **A per-addressee `client_msg_id`, `${base}:${toUserId}`** (`› addresseeClientMsgId`). ⚠ `channel_tasks` has a partial unique index on `(channel_id, client_msg_id, created_by)` (`20260913120000`), and a fan-out is ONE creator, so ONE key across N addressees does not fail — rows 2..N converge on row 1 through the idempotency short-circuit, every call returns a thread, and **the request silently reaches one person.** There is no error to catch: the ROW COUNT is the only witness, and `service-tasks-broadcast.test.ts` is what counts it.
  - **A DERIVED group id** (`› fanoutGroupId`, a hash of the creator plus the caller's base key), stamped as reserved `metadata.fanoutGroup` on each opening message. Derived rather than minted per attempt because a retry that re-mints splits one request across two cards; the creator is mixed in so no member can reproduce another's group. **An empty addressee list is a 400** (`schema.ts › TaskFanOutSchema`), not an empty success.
- **The web states the rule in exactly THREE places since 2026-09-08** (it was FOUR for part of that day, while the inline panel and its popup replacement were both mounted; the panel is deleted) — (`channels/components/composer-recipients.tsx › ComposerRecipients` — the CHANNEL COMPOSER's own, a standing `→ <who>` line under the draft that says `nobody` when it would wake nobody, added by v2 wave B slice B10 on Samuel's ruling that a guest *"doesn't know that there's a tagging function and that the tagging function is required for the agent to see the message"*; **`channels/components/new-thread-dialog.tsx › NO_ADDRESSEE_NOTE` — added 2026-09-08 with the new-thread POPUP**, a CREATE-time report on the form that raises the thread, carrying the deleted inline panel's wording exported rather than retyped, because two spellings of one fact is how one of them comes to sound optional. ⚠ **It began as a FOURTH place beside the composer's INLINE request panel and became a REPLACEMENT later the same day**, when that panel — and its last opener, the composer's `MessageSquarePlus` glyph — were deleted (Samuel: *"why wasn't that wired in"*); **`channels/components/invite-dialog.tsx › GroupChannelRoutingNote` — the CHANNELS one**, the standing explanation, shown UNCONDITIONALLY and stating the thread rule the composer never mentions); **the MCP lane in exactly one** (`channel-addressing.ts`). ⚠ **THE NEW ONE IS THE ONLY LIVE ONE — it restates itself on every keystroke** rather than standing as prose, which is what lets it obey the minimal-copy ruling while saying more than either of the others: it names the recipients, and it distinguishes an address the AUTHOR wrote from one the SERVER will repair (`default` for RR3, `thread` for RR1). Its rule is `channels/lib/draft-recipients.ts › draftReach`, a PREDICTION of `server/service-wake-verdict.ts › resolveWakeVerdict` over the same two parsers and the same `resolveDefaultResponder` — never a second opinion. ⚠ The composer half has moved TWICE and this bullet named the first move only: it was `channels/components/message-composer.tsx` until the 2026-08-18 cutover (deleted), then `channels/components/composer.tsx` until the 2026-08-22 split at the 500-line cap, which is where it lives now. **The doc said `composer.tsx` until 2026-08-26** — a bare-path reference, so `scripts/check-doc-refs.mjs` could not catch it; it is a symbol anchor now. ⚠ **The invite-dialog half was still count-keyed until the 2026-08-18 wave-2 fix pass** — gated below the group threshold and reciting it, so it taught the retired rule and said nothing in a two-member channel; it now takes no props. ⚠ **`invite-dialog.tsx` is an ambiguous basename: `members/components/invite-dialog.tsx` also exists and states nothing about addressing.** Anything else implying an unaddressed channel message reaches an agent is wrong — **"broadcast" is not a shape this product has.**
- **THE LOOP BRAKE is no longer a special case — it is the general rule.** An UNADDRESSED message can never trigger, whoever wrote it (`dopl-desktop-app/main/targeting.js › classify`). It used to be an agent-only branch sitting above the implicit 1:1 trigger, and the retirement of that trigger is what generalized it. Member-count-independent, as it always was.
- **THE `classify` VERDICT SET IS FOUR WORDS, AND ONE OF THEM CHANGED MEANING (2026-08-18, wiring plan Phase 7).** `trigger` (consent prompt, maybe a spawn) · `task-reply` (a passive notice, and the SUPPRESSION that stops a reply in my own thread looking like a fresh request) · **`fyi` — now "a message that @-TAGGED ME", not "a message I can see"** · `ignore`. Every `fyi` return in `classify` is conjoined with `targeting.js › mentionsMe`, so a post I am a member of and was not tagged in returns `ignore`. **The notification policy is §11; what belongs here is the verdict shape**, because a reader who still believes `fyi` means "visible" will reintroduce the notification storm by "fixing" a branch. `task-reply` is deliberately NOT gated — it is a routing statement, and the tag gates its NOTICE one layer up in `listener-messages.js`'s dispatch. ⚠ **WIDENED 2026-08-20 (the session-window retirement's pair, §11): the suppression now covers EVERY author kind and EVERY mode.** The branch reads only the server-stamped pair (`taskCreatedBy` = me, `taskTarget` = the author) plus the address — the old `authorKind === 'agent'` and `taskMode === 'interactive'` conjuncts existed so the requester's live session window could claim what fell through, and with that lane retired either conjunct failing turned the counterparty's reply IN MY OWN THREAD into a consent card against myself. Anybody OUTSIDE the pair (a third member in my thread, not-my-thread, unaddressed) still classifies as before. Pinned by `test/main-audit-targeting.test.mjs`.
- ⚠ **THE ROSTER IS NO LONGER A BEHAVIOUR, and the departure sweep's REASON changed with it.** A ghost `channel_members` row used to turn a live 1:1 into a "3-party" room and silently disable the implicit trigger — no error, no signal. With the count unread, that failure mode is gone. **The sweep stays and is still required:** a ghost row keeps a departed teammate ADDRESSABLE in the picker and in `op="members"`, keeps every displayed roster count wrong, and leaves a one-member DM that renders as a conversation with yourself. A workspace departure REMOVES the row (`workspaces/server/membership-admin.ts › removeMember` → `channels/server/service-workspace-departure.ts`), best-effort, always AFTER the membership delete.
- **TERMINATION IS A ROW DELETE, NOT A STATUS FLIP.** Nothing writes `workspace_members.status` to anything but `'active'`; no self-serve leave route, no deactivation. "No longer active" and "has no row" are the same statement. **Adding a deactivated state would silently break the departure sweep and its backfill, neither of which fails loudly.**
- **A thread is one requester + one target.** Reads are channel-visible (a third member CAN read a pair's thread; deliberate). Writes → **403 `TASK_FORBIDDEN`** unless the poster is `created_by` or `target_user_id` (`isThreadParticipant`, synchronous — a threaded post costs no participant query). A legacy `task-{channelId}-{seq}` id is validated against its opening message's `{author, to_user_id}` pair, and a non-participant's tag is **SILENTLY STRIPPED, never 403'd** (installed desktops post legacy ids for lifecycle events).
- **A thread may not be addressed to its own creator** — 400 `CHANNEL_TASK_SELF_TARGET`, checked AFTER the addressee-membership check and BEFORE the idempotency short-circuit (behind it, a retry returns the stored dead thread as a success).
- **Reserved metadata is STRIPPED from caller input and re-stamped only from validated fields**, at the single point `channels/server/service-writes-metadata.ts › resolvePostMetadata`. ⚠ **THE LIST LIVES IN CODE — read the `delete metadata.*` run in that function plus `service-writes-metadata-markers.ts` before trusting any prose copy, this one included.** As measured 2026-08-11 it is:
  - **Stripped, then re-stamped from a server or validated source:** `to_user_id`, `summary`, `runtime`, `appVersion`, `session_id`, `intent`, `handoff`, **`fanoutGroup`**, **`mentionedUserIds`**, and the four task keys (`taskMode`/`taskCreatedBy`/`taskTitle`/`taskTarget`). ⚠ **`fanoutGroup` is reserved on `handoff`'s terms and for a sharper reason:** the transcript renders every opening message sharing it as ONE card, so a settable value would draw your own thread inside somebody else's request. Like `handoff`, it stamps ONLY onto a post carrying a thread tag its poster is entitled to.

The atomicity above is unharmed: SET NULL neither blocks nor splits the one statement, and leaves no row still pointing at the deleted channel. **The migration was already right and was NOT edited.** The ruling lives in `schema-sql.test.ts` as a `CASCADE_EXEMPT` entry keyed to that exact `table.column` and carrying the argument, so the cascade case still FAILS for any other child that forgets — and a STALE exemption (column renamed or dropped) fails its own case rather than passing silently. ⚠ **Adding a name to that map is a RULING, not a fix.** It asserts the child is a RECORD OF SOMETHING THAT HAPPENED, whose truth does not depend on the room existing; anything that is a statement ABOUT a room (an arming row, an artifact, a direction) cascades. ⚠ Not to be confused with `channel_messages.artifact_id`, which is SET NULL into `channel_ARTIFACTS`, not into `channels`, and is ratified. **Do not add an RPC to "follow the pattern"**: the pattern is atomicity, and one statement has it.

So: every reader of a field added to an already-persisted payload type takes an explicit absent-fallback (`?? EMPTY_X`, matching what `{}` parses to server-side), and the change's tests include a STALE-CACHE case — the fixture WITHOUT the new field — or the tests are testing a cache state no user boots into. Measurement: `grep -n "CACHE-SHAPE FALLBACK" apps/desktop-ui/src` for the idiom.
