### THE OUTSIDE-SESSION ADDRESS — `@desktop` (2026-09-18, Samuel's ruling)

- 🔒 **`to="@desktop"` ADDRESSES THE CALLER'S OWN OPERATOR'S OUTSIDE SESSIONS, AND IT IS THE ONE ADDRESS ON THIS SURFACE THAT REACHES NO MACHINE.** An OUTSIDE SESSION is any MCP client on the operator's device token this product did not spawn — a Claude Code / Codex / Cursor run, a scheduled routine, a script. It has no handle, so an in-channel agent could previously only address the OPERATOR, and addressing a person is a request for that person's AGENTS: the operator's machine woke a responder for a question aimed at their laptop. The options paper is `docs/specs/external-session-handles.md`; what shipped is a variant of its **Option B**, so there is no presence row and no write on the read path.
  - **It resolves in `server/service-writes-metadata-recipient.ts › resolveToRecipient`, BEFORE any read**, to `ctx.userId`. Always resolvable, in every channel, with no setup — and therefore never stale. ⚠ **It is the CALLER'S own, never the room's**, so a room with two members holds two `@desktop`s that never contest; `@desktop` from Diana's agent means Diana's outside sessions.
  - 🔒 **THE RECIPIENT RIDES `metadata.to_desktop` AND IS DELIBERATELY IN NEITHER RECIPIENT COLUMN.** `recipient_user_ids` / `metadata.to_user_id` are what machines route on (`main/session-dispatch.js › serverNamesMember`, `main/targeting.js › classify`), so keeping this address out of both makes *"it wakes no desktop-run agent and does not notify the human as a person-address"* true **by construction** — for an OLD desktop exactly as for a new one. **No desktop change was needed, and a reader who "tidies" this into `recipient_user_ids` breaks the whole guarantee.** The key carries the OPERATOR ID (not `true`), which is what makes it indexable for `dopl_status` and readable from a second member's transcript.
  - **`delivery` is `posted`, and it may never become `held` or `woken`.** A hold is a long poll that registers nothing server-side, so no server can say whether an outside session is listening; `posted` states the only thing that is true either way. It is ranked ABOVE every machine outcome in `server/service-writes-delivery.ts › DELIVERY_RANK` and is excluded from `MachineDelivery`, so no receipt can arrive carrying it or overwrite it. See **F-740** — this is a recorded limitation of Option B, not a defect.
  - **`desktop` joins `addressed` in the verdict**, so the resilience arms cannot repair it: a deliberately-named lane is the opposite of a forgotten `@`, and RR3 was otherwise handing such posts to the room's default responder.
  - 🔒 **`desktop` IS RESERVED AT BOTH SERVER DOORS** (`liveAgentHandles` and `resolveAgentRecipients`, via `buildAgentMentionIndex`'s reserved set). The desktop's own `-1` suffixing (`main/agent-name-unique.js`) runs on ONE machine and cannot see a row written before the rule or a peer's agent, so **the server reservation is the half that actually holds**. In a BODY the handle is reserved-but-PLACED, so a mention in passing cannot stamp a false `unreachable`.
- **THE AUTHOR LABEL IS A PROJECTION, NOT A COLUMN VALUE.** `metadata.external_session` is stamped from ONE discriminator (`lib/desktop-handle.ts › isExternalSessionAuthor`: an `agent` author with no `desktop-session` runtime stamp) and projected by `› authorViewOf` as `external`. ⚠ **`MessageAuthorKind` IS NOT WIDENED**: `scripts/check-message-kind-drift.ts` reads the `author_kind` CHECK out of `20260725120000_channels.sql` ALONE and fails on any later migration carrying a CONSTRAINT clause on `channel_messages` that mentions `kind`. The projection is also the tolerant choice — an unstamped row is every pre-2026-09-18 row and every older server's, and it renders exactly as it did before. ⚠ The flag is stamped `true` or not at all, so readers test `=== true`; truthy junk is not a claim. ⚠ The discriminator's second mark is a caller-supplied header and is therefore forgeable in both directions — **F-741**; it LABELS and gates nothing.
- **THE READ MARKS, AND IT NEVER FILTERS** (Samuel's ruling (b): *"it's much worse if a message meant for an audience/agents is silently forgotten/dropped then like too many messages going to an agent"*). `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/channel-desktop-tag.ts › outsideRelevance` classifies a PAGE (class (ii) is positional, so it cannot be a per-line predicate) and `channel-render.ts › formatMessages` renders `⚠ FOR YOU` / `likely for you` as a SUFFIX on lines that were rendered anyway. **A hold returns on every new message exactly as before.** There is no opt-in "only tagged" mode in this wave, deliberately; the one-place seam is `OutsideRelevance`.

### THE DELIVERY KEYSTONE — the server resolves the recipient, the desktop executes it (2026-09-02, v2 wave A slice A9)

- 🔒 **WHO A MESSAGE IS FOR, AND WHETHER IT WOKE ANYBODY, IS DECIDED ONCE — ON THE SERVER, AT WRITE TIME.** `server/service-wake-verdict.ts › resolveWakeVerdict` runs on the post path after the metadata fold (so it reads the server's own `to_user_id` / `taskId` stamps, never the caller's claim) and stores four columns on `channel_messages` (`20260912120000_channel_delivery_verdict.sql`): `wake_verdict` (`none | member | agent | thread | thread_peer | reciprocal | responder | desktop` — the resilience three since `20260918120000`, see THE RESILIENCE ARMS below; `desktop` since `20260918140000`, see THE OUTSIDE-SESSION ADDRESS below), `recipient_user_ids`, `recipient_agent_ids`, and `delivery`. **Before this the server stored a message with NO delivery semantics at all** — every desktop re-derived addressing by parsing the BODY, so the addressing doctrine had to be written against the weakest build in the field (`packages/mcp-server/src/tools/channel-addressing.ts` says so in as many words) and "a message @-mentioning another agent is not addressed to you" was a request rather than a fact.
- 🔒 **THREE ANSWERS, AND COLLAPSING ANY TWO IS A REAL DEFECT.** `[]` is *resolved to nobody*; **`null` is *not resolved here*, and the desktop then falls back to its own body parse**; `"none"` is *addresses nobody*. A body naming an agent this server cannot see (a PEER's agent — ids are minted per machine and known to no server — or a session whose projection row has not been pushed) answers `null` and `delivery = "unreachable"`, so **nothing is silenced and nothing narrows**. `[]` there would stop a desktop feeding an agent it can see. ⚠ **`null` HAS A SECOND CAUSE AND THE TWO MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE (fixed 2026-09-02):** only `kind: 'message'` asks the agent half at all, so every LIFECYCLE and MILESTONE row also carries `null` — meaning *never asked*, not *reached nothing*. The `unreachable` arm is gated on the kind; without that term every `task_progress` / `task_finished` row was stamped `unreachable`, and a thread's own milestones read to an orchestrator as a room full of failed deliveries.
- 🔒 **THE SCOPE OF AN AGENT RESOLUTION IS THE CREDENTIAL'S, AND THAT IS SAMUEL'S SAME-ACCOUNT CARVE (2026-08-31) ENFORCED STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN AS A BRANCH.** Every agent posts under its operator's account, so "the author's own sessions" IS the set an AGENT-authored message may wake — the BODY parse (`service-wake-verdict-handles.ts › resolveAgentRecipients`) and the `to=` resolver (`service-writes-metadata-recipient.ts › liveAgentHandles`) are both own-scoped when the author is an agent, so a peer's agent is not in the index, cannot be resolved, and no stored verdict can name it. ⚠ **A PERSON MAY NAME ANY AGENT LIVE IN THE ROOM, AND SINCE 2026-09-04 THE BODY PARSE ACTUALLY DOES** — it read the AUTHOR'S OWN sessions for BOTH kinds of author until then, so a member's `@agent-<id>` for a peer's agent stored `recipient_agent_ids=NULL` and reached that agent only through the desktop's own body-parse fallback. It is not a widening: an unaddressed human post already reaches every machine's agents in the room through RR3, each machine feeding its own, and the Agents tab already shows a member every peer card — a typed handle asks for strictly less. ⚠ **THERE IS NO AMBIGUOUS HANDLE LEFT TO REFUSE (2026-09-15, corrected here 2026-09-16).** This bullet claimed *"ambiguity is now a REFUSAL, not a `null`"* via `ChannelAgentHandleAmbiguousError`; that throw site went on 2026-09-07 with the suffix mint, and the mint itself was withdrawn on 2026-09-15 in favour of Samuel's commit-time rule — no two ADDRESSABLE agents in a channel share a name, because the second is STORED as `Coder-1` (`main/agent-name-unique.js`; see §11). `AgentMentionIndex` is `ReadonlyMap<string, string>`, so the resolver has no value that could mean "two agents claim this". The class survives in `errors-recipient.ts` only because it is a wire-visible code older clients may name. ⚠ **THE ONE CASE THE COMMIT RULE CANNOT COVER IS CROSS-MACHINE** — names are minted on the machine that owns the id, so two MEMBERS can each run a "Main"; `buildAgentMentionIndex` names the FIRST CLAIMANT, which never re-points an address and never withdraws one. ⚠ **AND NEITHER BODY-PARSE READ IS FRESHNESS-BOUNDED (2026-09-05, corrected here 2026-09-16).** This bullet claimed both were. `isFresh` survives at exactly one site, `service-wake-verdict-handles.ts › ownLiveAgentIds`'s `projectionFresh`: **presence licenses RESOLUTION, freshness licenses only REFUSAL.** `channel_sessions` is a projection pushed on state CHANGE, so a quiet row means nobody spoke — filtering on it made an operator's own idle agent unaddressable. ⚠ **The body parse is skipped entirely unless the body carries an @-handle** — otherwise every post would pay for it.
- 🔒 **`to=` IS ONE **OR MORE** RECIPIENTS ACROSS TWO NAMESPACES (2026-09-02, v2 wave B slice B4 — Samuel's ruling B1; widened to a LIST 2026-09-18, and the resolver is `resolveToRecipients` — see ADDRESS IT OR IT IS A RECORD below).** `ChannelMessageCreateSchema.to` accepts a member (user id, or an email matched case-insensitively against THIS CHANNEL'S roster) **or** an agent (`@agent-<id>` / `@<handle>`, the `channel_sessions.name` grammar), resolved once at the door by `server/service-writes-metadata-recipient.ts › resolveToRecipient`. A member resolved there becomes the `toUserId` every existing fence already checks — one addressee path, one membership check — and an AGENT recipient stamps **no metadata key at all**: it rides `recipient_agent_ids`. ⚠ `metadata.to_agent_id` keeps its permanent strip and gains no writer; consent cards still key on `metadata.to_user_id`. ⚠ `to` and `toUserId` together are a 400: one recipient, one field.
- 🔒 **AN UNRESOLVED `to=` IS REFUSED — 400 `CHANNEL_RECIPIENT_UNRESOLVED`, LISTING THE LIVE HANDLES AND THE ROSTER — NEVER A SILENT `delivery=none`.** With the fan-out narrowing to the addressed recipient, a send whose `to` names nobody reaches nobody, and answering `ok` about it is the invisible-delivery failure in its purest form. ⚠ The lists are ROOM- and ROSTER-scoped so this cannot become a probe for whether an arbitrary address has an account here, and they name the `agent-<id>` form rather than a slug two agents may contest — a refusal must not teach a second refusal. ⚠ A handle in PROSE that resolves to nothing is still `delivery=unreachable`, not a refusal: prose is not an address.

#### THE RESILIENCE ARMS — a forgotten `@` must never stall a conversation (2026-09-02, v2 wave B slice B4, ruling B1)

- 🔒 **NARROWING THE FAN-OUT MEANS A MESSAGE THAT NAMED NOBODY REACHES NOBODY, SO THE SERVER REPAIRS THE ADDRESS — BY THREE RULES, AND IT STORES WHICH ONE FIRED.** They live in `server/service-wake-verdict-resilience.ts`, are applied by `resolveWakeVerdict`, and are reached ONLY when the author addressed nobody and only for `kind: 'message'`. **They are disjoint by (in a thread?) × (author kind), so exactly one fires**; none is a fallback for another.
  - **RR1 `thread_peer`** — a threaded reply with no `to` goes to the thread's OTHER party. Total, because a thread has exactly two parties and `isThreadParticipant` 403s a third. Read off the metadata fold's own `taskCreatedBy` / `taskTarget` stamps, so it costs no round trip. ⚠ A LEGACY `task-<channelId>-<seq>` tag stamps no pair and resolves to nobody — the post keeps the `thread` verdict, which is what those posts do today.
  - 🔴 **RR2 `reciprocal` IS DELETED (2026-09-18, Samuel's ruling: *"agree with stopping that. Agents should only be woken up when addressed (besides the logic for a user with no @ in their messsage)"*).** It resolved an unaddressed AGENT post in the MAIN room back to whoever last addressed that agent there, inside `RESILIENCE_WINDOW_MS`. **Its charter was a PERSON's problem** — *a forgotten `@` must never stall a conversation* — and an agent no longer forgets: it addresses somebody or files a record, and the send path refuses anything else. An ENDED agent reads `null` and its old posts wear the NEUTRAL accent (`channels/components/agent-box-rule.ts › AGENT_ACCENT_NEUTRAL`, `var(--border-strong)`), which is the reclaim rule made visible rather than a side effect.

"flex-row-reverse" : "flex-row"`, so right-aligned posts carry it right and left-aligned ones left). ⚠ **THE BAR'S TOP END IS SQUARE AND THAT IS A RULING** (Samuel, 2026-09-14: *"where it connects with the bar, it should be a straight, not rounded"*) — the top is the end the frame joins, so a cap there tapers to a point exactly where one colour has to continue into the other; only the far end is capped. ⚠ **THE 2026-09-13 BOX IS DELETED** — that message-box-agent component was a SECOND row shape that had to hard-code `items-start` and ignore `continuation`, and Samuel's restyle (*"instead of it being an entire box … a vertical bar … move the agent/user identification pill to the right again"*) makes an agent's post a person's post plus an accent, so the side rule (this section) and the run-grouping are answered once for every author. ⚠ **ONE POST, ONE BAR**: a run does not merge, and a CONTINUATION row drops the pill and the frame with it while keeping its own bar. ⚠ **THE PAINT IS RESOLVED IN ONE PLACE**, `agent-box-rule.ts › agentPostAccent`, beside the predicate that decides whether there is an accent at all — the filter's "People" option is that predicate's literal complement. ⚠ **THE POP-OUT'S "posted to channel" BANNER DID NOT FOLLOW** and keeps its own full-width geometry (`agent-stream-sent-box.tsx › AGENT_BAR`, which moved back into that file): it is a delivery record with no side, no author and no pill to frame. ⚠ **IT WAS A `ring` UNTIL 2026-09-16 AND SAMUEL READ THE RESULT AS THREE OBJECTS** (*"the borderline, the badge, and the vertical line, are 3 different components … the lines overlap and cause it to be darker. And also, since the shadow is attached to the badge, it gets covered behind the borderline."*): the ring was laid OVER the bar's full 3px, which composited on the translucent NEUTRAL face, and it covered the badge's own `--shadow-bento`. The pill now draws no stroke at all (`attribution-pill.tsx`'s `framed` drops `.bento` and `bits.tsx › agentAccent`), so there is ONE border path and the shadow sits on the outermost box. ⚠ **ITS HOVER IS THE BLACK BUTTON'S** — the 2px lift plus `--shadow-raised-hover`, which is `.auth-btn-3d:hover`'s ambient pair extracted to a token rather than copied. #### ADDRESS IT OR IT IS A RECORD — the structural half (2026-09-18, Samuel's ruling; branch `fix/channel-addressing`)

- 🔒 **AN AGENT-AUTHORED SEND ADDRESSES SOMEBODY OR IT IS A RECORD, AND A SEND THAT IS NEITHER IS REFUSED.** Samuel: *"agents posting in a channel should always be adding to or addressing another agent, or addressing someone … I don't think there should ever be messages that have no @ unless it really is purely just posting … we should bake this into the structure"*, and *"there are cases where maybe the agent just wants like needs to post something to channel to have a record of it, but it's like really not meant for agents and it might not be meant for like users."* The refusal is in the AGENT-FACING send path (`packages/mcp-server/src/tools/channel-ops-write.ts › unaddressedRefusal`, routed by `channel.ts`'s `op="send"` arm), names both choices in one line, and never reaches the wire. ⚠ **THREE CARVE-OUTS, EACH AN ADDRESS ALREADY**: a THREAD send (its two parties are the address — RR1), `kind="milestone"` and `kind="decision"`. ⚠ **PERSON-AUTHORED SENDS ARE UNTOUCHED** — the web composer does not go through this tool, and no server-side 400 was added, deliberately: a route-level refusal would break every installed desktop posting an agent's main-room result. That gap is recorded as **F-737**.
- 🔒 **THE RECORD IS `intent:"chat"` ON AN ORDINARY `message` ROW, SPELLED `kind="record"` ON THE MCP SURFACE.** The route's own field already meant *"this post is not work for anybody"* (`schema.ts › MessageIntentSchema`), `chat` + an address is already a 400 (`ChannelChatAddressedError`), and the row keeps its seq, its realtime event, its transcript line and its read watermark. **No migration, no new stored kind, no renderer arm.** ⚠ **WHAT THE WAVE ADDED IS THE ARMS GATE**: `resolveWakeVerdict`'s `repairable` now excludes a record, beside the stripped-thread-tag case and for the same reason — both LOOK unaddressed and neither is missing an address. A record resolves `verdict=none`, `delivery=none`, even inside a thread.
- 🔒 **AN AGENT'S PROSE NAMES NO AGENT.** `resolveWakeVerdict` does not ask `resolveAgentRecipients` at all when `authorKind === "agent"`; it answers `[]`, which is authoritative and stops the desktop's own parse. ⚠ **`[]` AND NEVER `null`** — `null` means "you decide" and would send the machine back to `main/session-dispatch.js › mentionedAgentIds`, resolving the very handle this gate makes inert. ⚠ **THE MACHINE CARRIES THE SAME FENCE ON THE OLD-SERVER FALLBACK**, where no verdict was stored (`planFor`'s `!agentAuthored` term) — the only lane the server cannot reach. ⚠ **THE PEOPLE HALF IS UNCHANGED**: `@diana` in an agent's body still lands in Diana's Tags inbox; that is `resolveBodyMentions`, a different fold over the human roster. ⚠ **THE OWN-SCOPED BRANCH INSIDE `resolveAgentRecipients` SURVIVES AS A BELT** and is driven directly by `service-wake-verdict-handles.test.ts`; it is unreachable from the verdict today and is kept so that re-opening the body door cannot silently re-open the same-account carve with it.
- 🔒 **AN AGENT SESSION TAKES A TURN ONLY WHEN IT IS ADDRESSED** (2026-09-18, Samuel's ruling on the two open questions). **THREE THINGS COUNT AS ADDRESSED AND THERE IS NO FOURTH**: named in `to` (`recipient_agent_ids`), the OTHER PARTY OF A TWO-PARTY THREAD (`thread_peer`, and `thread` for the sessions already working it — both thread-scoped by `liveOnThread`'s `<channel>:<task>:` key), and the structured ESCALATION-ANSWER field, which names the agent that ASKED. Everything else feeds nothing. ⚠ **SO AN AGENT ADDRESSING A PERSON REACHES THE PERSON AND NOT THEIR AGENTS**: `member` grants context only when a PERSON wrote the post (`main/session-dispatch.js › planFor`). The person is notified and an external held read still returns it; their channel agents get no turn. ⚠ **A PERSON'S `to=<me>` STILL FEEDS**, and the asymmetry is the ruling — that is the one case where my side is expected to decide what runs. ⚠ **`reciprocal` FALLS THROUGH TO FALSE** rather than being listed and excluded, which is what keeps the machine safe against a server predating the deletion.
  - ⚠ **WHAT THE CHAIN WAS, BOTH HALVES.** (a) unaddressed agent post → RR2 repaired to the operator → `reciprocal` counted as a member verdict → `context: true` → and a MAIN-ROOM post keys `liveOnThread` `<channelId>::`, so **every main-room session of that operator took a full model turn**; (b) writing `to=<me>` reached the same fan-out by a second route. Closing only (a) would have left (b). There is no passive-context lane — a windowless session floors at `auto_inbound` (`session-gate.js`) — so hearing it IS a turn.
  - 🔒 **THE ONE EXCEPTION IS RR3 AND IT IS UNTOUCHED**: *"besides the logic for a user with no @ in their messsage."* A PERSON who names nobody is still answered by the room's nominee, its one agent, else the agent they last addressed — all three arms pinned in `service-wake-verdict-addressing.test.ts`.
- 🔒 **`to=` IS A COMMA-SEPARATED LIST ACROSS BOTH NAMESPACES** (`server/service-writes-metadata-recipient.ts › resolveToRecipients`, cap `constants.ts › CHANNEL_SEND_MAX_RECIPIENTS` = 10). Samuel: *"we have to make sure agents might need to respond to multiple agents, not necessarily to only one agent. It could be multiple agents, and it could be multiple people on the channel."* ⚠ **THE LIST LIVES INSIDE THE EXISTING STRING FIELD AND THAT IS THE WHOLE WIRE CHANGE** — a `string | string[]` union publishes as `anyOf` on every MCP schema carrying the field, and a single-string `to` had to keep working byte-for-byte. ⚠ **EVERY TOKEN GOES THROUGH THE ONE RESOLVER**, so a list whose second name misses is refused WHOLE; **the membership fence loops over every member named**, or the multi form becomes the way around it. ⚠ **`metadata.to_user_id` IS THE FIRST NAMED MEMBER AND `recipient_user_ids` IS THE ADDRESS** — that key is the consent card's and thread inheritance's index and stays single. ⚠ **PRECEDENCE IS UNCHANGED**: a mixed send is `verdict=agent` over two full columns, because every machine routes on the COLUMNS and reads the word only to explain itself. ⚠ **THE DESKTOP NEEDED NO CHANGE FOR IT** — `serverAddressed` and `serverNamesMember` already read arrays — and `channel-render-identity.ts › addressTag` already joins them with `, `.
- 🔒 **`wake=` ON A SEND RESULT IS READ OFF THE STORED ROW, NOT OFF THE BODY** (`channel-ops-write.ts › wakeFact`). It counted the `@agent-…` handles the BODY named, which was honest while prose was an agent address and is a report of a wake that cannot happen now. ⚠ It renders the same column `addressed=` and the read's `→` arrow render, so the three cannot disagree.

## 5A. Agent identities — roles of the user ("agent templates" until 2026-09-22)

**Written and measured 2026-08-22** against the tree at authoring time — the whole section, not
bullet-by-bullet, so the file-header date above does not apply to it.

> ⚠ **THE SECTION IS LETTERED, NOT NUMBERED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.** §6…§14 are cited by number from
> `CLAUDE.md`, from other docs, and from docblocks across three trees; inserting a §6 to renumber nine
> sections would invalidate every one of those citations to buy a digit. **Do not renumber this file to
> "fix" it.**

> 🔒 **GLOSSARY (Samuel, 2026-09-22).** An **AGENT IDENTITY** is a ROLE OF THE USER — one piece of their
> digital twin (*"if you think about the coder agent, it's basically me as a coder"*): instructions, a
> default model, custom fields and attached knowledge. An **AGENT** is a running session in a channel,
> launched FROM an identity or blank. It was called an "agent template" until 2026-09-22; see the rename
> bullet below for what moved and what did not. **A SESSION IS EPHEMERAL; THE IDENTITY IS THE DURABLE THING** — that
> asymmetry is the whole feature, and it is why identities get a table while sessions get a projection.

- 🔒 **THE RENAME, AND ITS LIMIT (Samuel, 2026-09-22):** *"Agent templates will be called agent identities, but in the channel page, we're still calling things agents."* **What moved:** the workspace page (`apps/desktop-ui/src/routes.tsx › WORKSPACE_PAGES` — `identities`, label **Identities**; the old `agents` path REDIRECTS via `› RENAMED_PAGES`, mirrored for `dopl://` links by `dopl-desktop-app/main/deep-link-target.js › RENAMED_PAGES`, and the two are cross-pinned by `apps/desktop-ui/src/routes.test.tsx`, which requires the pure main module — P9-16, 2026-09-23), the sidebar row (`shared/layout/app-shell/app-sidebar-core.tsx › NAV`), the /home face (`features/home/tabs.ts › HOME_TABS` — key `identities`, label **Identities**, between Knowledge and Ontology), both create buttons (**+ Agent Identity**), the channel launch picker (label **Identity**), and every internal name: `src/features/agent-identities/`, `/api/agent-identities` (`{identity}` / `{identities, homeScopedIdentityIds}`), `AGENT_IDENTITY_*` codes, resource type `agent_identity`, refusal word `no-identity`, IPC word `identity-approval`, the desktop's `identity-resolve.js` / `identity-approval.js` / `prompt-framing-agent-identity.js`, session field `identityName`, the SDK's `agent-identities.ts`, and the MCP argument `identity`. **The schema half is `supabase/migrations/20261019120000_rename_agent_templates_to_agent_identities.sql` (renames only; WRITTEN — apply state is a measurement, §12).** **What did not move:** the channel page — its **Agents** tab, agent cards, agent view and every running-session noun (§5); the ONTOLOGY's object `template` (an object's default fields — `ontology_objects.template`, `set_template_field`); Electron menu/tray "templates" and template literals; migration FILE names and the dropped historical objects (`agent_template_teams`, `assert_agent_template_team_workspace`). ⚠ **NO BACK-COMPAT, by ruling ("I'm the only user anyway")**: a desktop built before the rename reads `template_*` directive columns, pushes `templateName`, writes `no-template` and calls `/api/agent-templates`, and each of those fails against a renamed server. ⚠ **EXCEPT MACHINE-LOCAL USER DATA (P3-10, accepted default 2026-09-23):** `identity-approval.js` reads the pre-rename `approvedAgentTemplates` store key as a fallback (`› LEGACY_APPROVAL_KEY`), and the park/boot/history readers take a record's `templateName` when `identityName` is absent (`session-park.js`, `session-boot.js › parkedSessionFromRecord`, `agent-history.js`) — read, never written. ⚠ **PRE-EXISTING `identity` WORDS ARE UNRELATED AND STAYED:** the caller's identity (`mcp-server/src/tools/identity.ts › CallerIdentity`), replica identity and `agent-identity-commit.js` (a running agent's display name/description). A running agent's OWN id line was renamed out of the word on 2026-09-23 (`prompt-framing-self.js › agentSelfFraming`, which was `agentIdentityFraming` in the old identity-framing module; the listener's identity module became `listener-people.js`, `resolveIdentity` → `resolveOperatorUserId`). `prompt-framing-agent-identity.js` (the identity's ROLE block) keeps its name for now. The channel view-model's roster record, which WAS named `AgentIdentity`, is `channels/components/view-model.ts › AgentRosterEntry` since the same change.

- **THREE TABLES, ALL SERVICE-ROLE-WRITE-ONLY** (`supabase/migrations/20260822200000_agent_templates.sql` — ✅ **APPLIED**, name `agent_identities`, history version `20260823091848`; **re-measured 2026-08-26**, and applied is a MEASUREMENT, not a claim: `supabase migration list` (or MCP `list_migrations`) **joined on the NAME**, never on the filename (§12, F-304's re-stamp). ⚠ **This bullet and the two below said "WRITTEN — applied is a measurement" until 2026-08-26** while §12 had already recorded all three as applied on 2026-08-24 — two sections of one file disagreeing about deploy state, which is what F-332's dev mock was still living behind): `agent_identities`, `agent_template_teams`, `agent_identity_knowledge_bases`. `INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` are REVOKEd from `authenticated`/`anon` and **no write policy exists on any of them**; the migration's trailing `DO $$` block RAISEs rather than trusting it. The service is the fence — and it must be, because the attach gate ("a KB the CALLER can currently read") is a predicate over ANOTHER table's visibility, which a `WITH CHECK` cannot express.
- **VISIBILITY IS ONE COLUMN WITH THREE VALUES — `private` | `team` | `workspace` — AND THIS IS THE ONE FEATURE WHERE THAT IS TRUE.** Skills, chats and KBs store the same three states as a PAIR (`visibility` 'public'|'private' × `access_mode` 'workspace'|'teams') because `access_mode` was added to a live table and its default was the BACKFILL; `src/features/skills/scope.ts › skillScope` is the helper that collapses the pair back. Nothing needed backfilling here, so the collapsed form is what is stored. **Porting a predicate across the boundary requires translating it**: `visibility='team'` here == `visibility='public' AND access_mode='teams'` there.
  - ⚠ **`workspace` IS THE VALUE; "Public" IS THE LABEL.** Never send `'public'` on this feature's wire, never render `'workspace'` to an operator.
- **TEAM LINKAGE IS A GRANT ROW, AND SINCE 2026-09-02 THERE IS EXACTLY ONE KIND OF GRANT ROW.** ⚠ **CORRECTED (Wave B slice B1, ruling B4).** It read: *"a join table, mirroring what the shipped features do — `team_resource_access` (`20260611020000_teams.sql`), extended per resource type by `20260707210000_chat_team_sharing.sql` and `20260708150001_skill_team_sharing.sql`"*. Both of those tables are now `resource_grants` at `scope_type='team'` (§12), and **team visibility is still MANY-teams** — a nullable `team_id` would still be a narrower model than the product ships. ⚠ **THE CAPABILITY DID NOT CHANGE; THE AXIS DID.** `agent_identities.visibility` still has three values, `'team'` still means "members of a linked team", the links are still a replace-set, and writes are still creator-or-workspace-admin.
  - ⚠ **IT WAS A DEDICATED JUNCTION (`agent_template_teams`) UNTIL 2026-09-02, AND F-277's TWO ARGUMENTS ARE ANSWERED RATHER THAN OVERRULED.** (1) *"a `level` this feature has no concept of"* — it is `'read'`, and `resource_grants_level_check` now says so, where the junction encoded the same fact by existing. (2) *"joining it means widening `src/features/teams/access-levels.ts › TeamResourceType`"*, a CONTRACT with four consumers outside the feature (`teams/server/repository-resources.ts › RESOURCE_TABLES`, `› listTeamsModeResources`, `members/components/member-bits.tsx › RESOURCE_META`, and the hand-copy in `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/members-render.ts`) — ⚠ **THAT UNION IS NOT WIDENED.** It names four types; `resource_grants` accepts five; every statement in each lane filters `resource_type`, so an identity row never reaches those consumers. **Do not unify them — F-463.**
- **THE VISIBILITY MATRIX IS WRITTEN TWICE AND THE TWO MUST MOVE TOGETHER**: `src/features/agent-identities/server/service-shared.ts › canSeeIdentity` and the `agent_identities_member_select` policy. Same arms, same ORDER — **SEVEN since 2026-09-02**, arm 4 being the grant (F-604), which moved on both sides in one change. `20260716150000_chats_team_aware_rls.sql` is the record of what a drift costs — RLS stayed permissive after the service tightened, and a team-scoped transcript leaked through PostgREST to every member until somebody compared them.
  - ⚠ **PRIVATE MEANS PRIVATE, ADMINS INCLUDED**, and the arm ORDER is what enforces it: the admin arm sits INSIDE the `team` branch, not above it. An admin administers SHARING; that is not a read of a teammate's private row. This is TIGHTER than `chats_member_select`, which leads with a blanket admin arm. `service-visibility.test.ts` enumerates 3 visibilities × 5 caller kinds so a reordering cannot be green.
  - **A workspace-scoped API key sees ONLY `workspace` identities** (M-10 — such a key may be shared between humans, so it inherits no individual's reach), including ones its own user id created.
- 🔒 **AN AGENT'S ONTOLOGY REACH IS ITS OPERATOR'S, RESOLVED SERVER-SIDE (2026-09-09, Samuel's home-ontology matrix; `docs/specs/home-ontology.md` §2/§4).** A member's or a guest's agent inherits **EXACTLY** that person's level on a shared ontology — no `min` is written for them, because the human's answer already IS the cap. **The OWNER is the one exception and gets two controls**: `ontology_clusters.agents_may_edit` (the SOLO toggle, default `edit`, and it only narrows) and `ontology_channel_shares.owner_agents_level` per channel. ⚠ **A SOLO ROOM THAT GAINS A PEER DROPS THE OWNER'S AGENTS TO `view`** until the owner states a level on the share row (Q2), and an unshared ontology reached from a shared room takes the same drop.
  - **THE FENCE IS `ontology/server/service-audience.ts › resolveOntologyAudience` + `› levelForCluster`**, one resolution per request (memoised on the context object in a `WeakMap`), and the `dopl_ontology` path inherits it because the MCP tools compose the same HTTP routes. **A prompt is not a fence**, and neither is the `dopl_ontology` description: an agent holds its operator's credential and has Bash. ⚠ **EVERY ARM OF `computeAudience` IS POSITIVE AND THE FALLBACK REACHES NOTHING (2026-09-09, F-683 RESOLVED)**: `standard` → `unrestricted` (one probe, no share fan — every board in the product today), `link`/`personal` → resolved from the share rows, **anything else — a kind nobody has designed yet, or a workspace row that vanished mid-request — → resolved with an EMPTY read scope**. The empty scope is what makes that "reaches nothing" rather than "reaches its own container": `› levelForCluster` answers `none` for it, because `service-shared.ts › inOwnContainer` asks about `ctx.workspaceId` and would otherwise admit the calling container to an audience resolved BECAUSE that container's kind could not be read. ⚠ **`agents_may_edit` IS REFUSED FROM AN AGENT SOURCE IN THE SERVICE** (`service.ts › updateCluster`, 403), not by a route field gate — a containment control a session could write is one call from re-widening itself, and the service refusal covers the MCP path a route-level rule would miss.
  - 🔒 **`guests_level` IS REACHABLE SINCE 2026-09-09 (Samuel's ruling; F-685 RESOLVED).** *"Guests of a home channel get their own level (none/view/edit) on a shared ontology, and their agents inherit it."* It had been a stored word nobody could exercise: every ontology route sat at `withWorkspaceAuth`'s `viewer` default while a home channel's peer is admitted at the role the LINK grants, which DEFAULTS to `guest` (`home/server/service-claim-bound.ts`). **SIX floors are now `minRole: "guest"`** and each is an entry in `src/app/api/channels/guest-route-floor.test.ts › GUEST_ALLOWED` — the two graph READS (`ontology/route.ts` GET, `ontology/anchor/route.ts` GET), the REACH read (`ontology/reach/route.ts` GET, next bullet), and the THREE object/relationship/membership WRITES (`ontology/objects/route.ts` POST, `ontology/objects/[objectId]/route.ts` PATCH and DELETE).
    - 🔒 **THE FLOOR GRANTS NOTHING. IT ONLY LETS A GUEST BE REFUSED BY THE FENCE.** `resolveOntologyAudience` is unchanged and still decides everything: a guest with `guests_level='none'`, or with no share row, reads an EMPTY snapshot and 404s on every write. Behaviourally pinned in `ontology/server/guest-lane.test.ts`; the census pins the floors.
    - ⚠ **WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT MOVE, and each absence is a decision**: the whole `ontology/clusters/[clusterId]/shares/**` lane (a guest lends nothing and re-levels nobody's share), cluster create / rename / delete, the **`agentsMayEdit` toggle** that rides the cluster PATCH (a CONTAINMENT control on the OWNER's own agents), and `objects/[objectId]/anchor` POST (workspace-scoped identity, R9). ⚠ The object DELETE keeps its **`sessionOnly`**: the floor changed WHICH ROLE may ask, never whether an agent token may.
  - **AN AGENT IS TOLD WHAT IT REACHES BY `GET /api/ontology/reach` (2026-09-09, F-681 RESOLVED).** `src/features/ontology/server/service-reach.ts › getReach` answers `[{ id, name, workspaceId, level }]` for the CALLING credential, composing `› service-audience.ts › levelForCluster` per cluster and dropping `none`. ⚠ **NO `?channelId=`, and that is not an omission**: the ceiling resolves per CONTAINER (every channel of it, at the wider rung — I5) and a home channel is the one channel in its `kind='link'` container, so a channel filter would answer NARROWER than the server enforces. ⚠ **THE DESKTOP PRESENTS THE SESSION'S AGENT BEARER, NOT THE OPERATOR'S COOKIE** — `service.ts › buildOntologyContext` derives `source` from an agent token, and the owner's own agent is the one matrix row that is not simply its human's; a cookie read would promise `EDIT` on a lane the server refuses. **No token ⇒ `[]`, never a cookie fallback.**
  - ⚠ **THE DESKTOP'S FRAMING BLOCK IS A COMPENSATING CONTROL, AND IT IS WIRED SINCE 2026-09-09.** `dopl-desktop-app/main/prompt-framing-ontology.js › ontologyReachLines` renders which ontologies a session reaches and at what level, spliced into both sides of `prompt-framing.js › buildFencedTurn` beside `PERSONAL_KNOWLEDGE_CONFIDENTIALITY`. It reads `ctx.ontologies`, and the PRODUCER is `main/ontology-reach.js › fetchOntologyReach` called from **the ONE spawn funnel** `main/session-launch.js › launch` — so the New Agent button, the directive spawn and the peer-triggered responder all carry it (the F-510 lesson). ⚠ **IT CANNOT REFUSE A LAUNCH**: every failure — timeout, dead socket, 5xx, an older deployment's 404, no credential — answers `[]` with one `diag` line. ⚠ **THIS MODULE IS NOW THE ONE CARRIER OF THAT RULE** — it was stated by the startup-context fetch on the same lane, and that fetch was deleted with knowledge pinning on 2026-09-18 (§10's removal bullet), so an ENRICHMENT read that degrades instead of refusing is spelled out here and nowhere else. ⚠ The key is merged onto `context` **only when non-empty**, so a lane reaching no ontology is byte-identical to what it was before the module existed — `context` staying `undefined` included. Nothing here narrows anything: the fence is `resolveOntologyAudience`.
- **AN AGENT SESSION'S KNOWLEDGE *AND ONTOLOGY* WRITES ARE ATTRIBUTED TO IT, AND THE CHANGELOG GROUPS BY THAT (2026-09-09; §9, §12).** Every write a session makes through `dopl_kb` records a revision whose `actor_kind` is `agent` and whose `agent_session_id` is the `X-Dopl-Session-Id` slot key VERBATIM, so several rows in a row wearing one session ARE one run of work and the base's Changelog renders them as such. ⚠ **IT IS AN ATTRIBUTION HINT AND NOTHING MORE** — the same forgeable, non-authorization signal `knowledge/types.ts › KnowledgeContext.sessionId` already carries (`shared/auth/session-header.ts`). Nothing grants on it, no policy reads it, and **a HUMAN on the desktop sends the same header and is never stamped with it**: `revisions/server/service.ts › deriveActor` records the column for agent callers only, or a person's edit would read as an agent's in every surface that groups by session. ⚠ **AND THE ONTOLOGY LANE JOINED ON THE SAME AXIS THE SAME DAY (part 2)**: `ontology/types.ts › OntologyContext.sessionId` carries the header verbatim and is read in exactly one place — that same `deriveActor` — so a `dopl_ontology` write shows in the object's **History** and the ontology's **Changelog** as its session's work. It is the only reader of that field in the feature, and no ontology gate asks it.

- **AN ATTACHMENT NAMES A BASE, A FOLDER, OR ONE ENTRY (2026-09-08, Samuel: *"right now, you can only select entire bases, but I want to be able to specific folders or entries/files"*).** `agent_identity_knowledge_bases` carries `scope_kind` ∈ `('base','folder','entry')` plus a nullable `folder_id`/`entry_id` (`supabase/migrations/20260930150000_agent_template_knowledge_scopes.sql` — ⚠ **WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED**; §12, and applied is a MEASUREMENT joined on the NAME `agent_template_knowledge_scopes`). The old composite PK could not survive it — three folders of one base share `(identity_id, knowledge_base_id)` — so the key is a surrogate `id` and the uniqueness is THREE PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEXES, one per shape.
  - **A FOLDER MEANS ITS SUBTREE, INCLUDING ENTRIES ADDED LATER.** One row names the folder; it is NEVER expanded into a row per child, because an expansion is a SNAPSHOT and an entry filed tomorrow would silently not be attached. Same rule the table already keeps one level up — an attachment is a REFERENCE, never a copy — held one level deeper.
  - 🔒 ⚠ **IT IS AN ATTACHMENT, NOT A PERMISSION, AND THE READ CEILING IS STILL BASE-KEYED (F-680).** `knowledge/server/service-audience.ts › resolveAgentAudience` / `audienceAdmits` resolve a BASE id, so an agent handed one folder of a base already in its audience can still `get_tree` the whole base. A folder scope narrows what the ROLE BLOCK POINTS AT and nothing else. Not a regression — it is exactly the pre-2026-09-08 reach — but do not read this column as access control.
  - **IDS ARE THE HANDLE; PATHS ARE DERIVED.** `knowledge_folders`/`knowledge_entries` carry no path column (`knowledge/server/path.ts › resolvePath` walks `parent_id`), so nothing stores one: the DTO derives `path` (DISPLAY, `Base / Folder / Entry`) and `toolPath` (base-relative, `/`-joined, what a `dopl_kb` call takes) on every read. **They are never interchangeable** — a base named "Ops / Legal" makes splitting one back into the other silently wrong.
  - **TWO WIRE SPELLINGS, MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE IN ONE REQUEST.** `knowledgeBaseIds` still means WHOLE BASES (older clients, and `dopl_agent`'s `knowledge_bases`); `knowledge` carries the scope. Both in one body is a **400**, never a merge: they are two REPLACE-SETs over one junction, so a body carrying both asks for two different final states. `agent-identities/schema.ts › knowledgeFieldsExclusive` is the refusal and `server/service-knowledge-scopes.ts › requestedKnowledgeScopes` is the one seam where they meet.
  - **THE DTO KEEPS BOTH KEYS, AND `knowledgeBases` IS THE BASE-LEVEL SLICE OF `knowledge`.** A folder scope contributes NOTHING to it — listing its base would tell an older reader the whole base is attached, a wider claim than the row makes. ⚠ On the LAUNCH payload the base list is load-bearing for §13: `main/identity-resolve.js › narrow` is an ALLOWLIST, so a desktop older than this release drops `knowledge` and would otherwise launch a role naming no knowledge at all. ⚠ §8: `AgentIdentity.knowledge` is OPTIONAL at every read (`lib/knowledge-scopes.ts › EMPTY_KNOWLEDGE`, spelled inline), because it was added to an IndexedDB-persisted payload.
- 🔒 **YOU MAY NOT ATTACH KNOWLEDGE YOU CANNOT READ.** Every scope in an attach set is resolved through `server/service-knowledge-scopes.ts › resolveVisibleKnowledgeScopes`, over `service-shared.ts › resolveVisibleKnowledgeBases` — the knowledge feature's `canSeeBase` rule MIRRORED, not imported (§1 forbids the cross-feature import). Without it an identity is a laundering channel: attach a teammate's private base by id, flip the identity to `workspace`, and every member's spawned agent gets a pointer to it. ⚠ **The refusal is 404-shaped, never a distinguishable 403** — the difference between the two codes would be an existence oracle for other people's private bases. ⚠ **SINCE 2026-09-08 THE GATE ALSO PROVES TENANCY AND LIVENESS ONE LEVEL DEEPER**, with the SAME 404: a folder or entry must live in the base its scope names and must not be trashed. **Three distinguishable shapes would be an oracle** — "that folder exists but is in another base" is a fact about somebody else's filing. The migration's trigger restates the tenancy half as a backstop; the service is the fence.
  - ⚠ **THE SAME PREDICATE FILTERS READS, so the attachment list is VIEWER-FILTERED: two people resolving the SAME identity can legitimately get different `knowledgeBases` arrays.** An attachment is a REFERENCE, never a copy — nothing about the base's content is denormalized — so a base that later goes private simply disappears from the payload rather than leaking its name.
- **WRITES ARE CREATOR-OR-WORKSPACE-ADMIN, FOR EVERY FIELD.** There is no "editable by the team it is shared with" level, deliberately: team `visibility` shares the ability to USE an identity, not to rewrite what it says. That is also why the team junction carries no `level` column. **An invisible identity 404s BEFORE the write gate can 403**, so a 403 never confirms a row exists.
- **`fields` IS SHAPE-IN-ZOD, SIZE-IN-SQL.** Element shape (`{key, value}` strings, unique keys, both halves charset-bounded as LABELS) is `src/features/agent-identities/schema.ts`; the DB CHECK asserts only `jsonb_typeof(fields) = 'array'` and `octet_length(fields::text) <= 8192`. ⚠ **Zod measures the same BYTES the CHECK measures** (`TextEncoder`, not `.length`) — a character count would pass a CJK payload here and fail it there as an opaque 500.
  - **A FIELD MAY CARRY `type` (`text`/`number`/`date`/`boolean`/`url`; absent = `text`) AND THE VALUE IS STILL A STRING.** The server never checks a value against its type. `dopl_agent` publishes the same vocabulary (`packages/mcp-server/src/tools/agent.ts › IDENTITY_FIELD_TYPES`, pinned against `types.ts › IDENTITY_FIELD_TYPES` by `schema-sql.test.ts`) and refuses, as `reason=invalid_field` naming field and type, a value the editor's control could not have produced (`agent-field-types.ts › fieldTypeRefusal`: decimal numeral, real `YYYY-MM-DD`, `yes`/`no`; `url` and `""` unchecked). An omitted `type` on update keeps the stored one, and an UNCHANGED field is never checked, so a read-modify-write cannot lose a field (DMP-009, 2026-09-23). Team visibility stays app-only: an agent credential is refused `team` by `assertTeamScopeIsHuman`.
- **HARD DELETE, NO TOMBSTONE.** No `deleted_at` column, no trash, no restore. Both junctions ride `ON DELETE CASCADE` — **the service writes no hand-rolled cascade**, and `service-writes.test.ts` asserts that ABSENCE, because a hand-written cascade is one that acquires a new child table and forgets it.
- **NOT PUBLISHED TO REALTIME, and the decision is recorded at the table** (§7's rule). An identity is edited by one person in a form and read at spawn by a desktop already making an HTTP request: no peer event, no live surface. Same answer `channel_mention_reads` got. It follows that no `workspace_id`-bearing replica identity is needed either — that requirement exists to make DELETE frames deliverable, and there are no frames.
- **THE REST SURFACE IS NOT `sessionOnly`, EXCEPT `DELETE`.** An orchestrator agent LISTING identities is the point of making them persistent, so GET/POST/PATCH stay reachable by an agent token; `DELETE /api/agent-identities/[identityId]` is session-gated because it is permanent and may destroy what a whole team spawns from. ⚠ **Per-METHOD** — `src/shared/auth/write-gate-coverage.test.ts` sees only that the FILE contains `sessionOnly: true`, so `[identityId]/route.test.ts › the per-method gate` is what pins WHICH method carries it.
- **`GET /api/agent-identities/[identityId]/resolve` IS THE LAUNCH CONTRACT** — a FLAT, unwrapped `{name, instructions, model, runtime, fields, knowledgeBases, knowledge, unreachableKnowledgeBaseCount, authoredByCaller}` (nine keys, re-read 2026-09-23 from `server/service-reads.ts › resolveIdentityForLaunch`; this bullet said six), and nothing else. It composes `› readIdentityById`, so it is gated by the same matrix as every other read and is not a second, weaker door. ⚠ **It is separate from the record endpoint on purpose:** the record grows fields as the product does, and the launcher must not re-decide which of them matter every time. A field added to `AgentIdentity` does not appear here unless somebody decides it belongs in a launch. `resolve/route.test.ts` pins the key set EXACTLY.
  - **`authoredByCaller` IS A SECURITY GATE RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE** (2026-08-22). The desktop's ROLE block wears the OPERATOR posture over an identity its operator wrote and the `UNTRUSTED_SKILL_BODY_HEADER`-shaped posture over another member's, and that gate cannot be built without it — the same authorship gating `narration.ts › isForeignAuthored` applies for the same reason (`knowledge-shared.ts`: *"noise is how a security header stops being read"*). ⚠ **A COMPUTED BOOLEAN, NEVER `createdBy`**: a raw creator id in a launch payload is ownership information the launcher has no use for, and the boolean discloses nothing the caller cannot already read off the list endpoint. ⚠ **It is AUTHORSHIP, not permission** — a workspace admin resolving someone else's identity gets `false`, and so does everyone once the author leaves the workspace (`created_by` is `SET NULL`), which is the fail-closed direction. `server/service-resolve.test.ts` pins the value per caller kind; the route test pins only the shape.
- 🔒 **AN IDENTITY WIDENS PROMPT CONTENT ONLY.** It never supplies, influences or relaxes a containment input: the tool profile, the permission axes, the working folder and the delivery lane are still the MACHINE's, resolved from the machine's own state. `dopl-desktop-app/main/session-launch-op.js` computes the tool profile from `targeting.resolveToolProfile(listener.watchedChannel(...))` BEFORE the identity is fetched at all, and `main/identity-resolve.js › narrow` is a literal whitelist of the six launch keys — a payload naming `toolProfile`, `startModes` or a `cwd` is DROPPED rather than refused. `prompt-profile-drift.test.mjs` fails any built turn that orders a hard-denied tool, identity-built turns included, which is the mechanical enforcement and needs no new test genus.
- **THE IDENTITY ENTERS THE PROMPT AS A FENCED ROLE BLOCK IN THE USER TURN, NEVER AS A `systemPrompt`** (`dopl-desktop-app/main/prompt-framing-agent-identity.js › identityRoleFraming`, spliced into the REQUESTER branch of `main/prompt-framing.js › buildFencedTurn`, last of the framing blocks and adjacent to the goal). ⚠ **A system prompt would sit structurally ABOVE the containment framing** — LANE_EXCLUSIVITY, the SECURITY RULES, the counterparty framing and the identity block all live in the user turn — and for a `team`/`workspace` identity that is ANOTHER MEMBER's text, which is exactly backwards. It would also survive `options.resume` uncorrectably. **PRECEDENCE, stated once:** tool-profile deny lists and `canUseTool` (CODE) > the framing's own rules (main's voice, OUTSIDE the fence) > the identity's instructions and fields (INSIDE `BEGIN-ROLE-<nonce>`) > the launch goal (INSIDE `BEGIN-REQUEST-<nonce>`). **ROLE FIRST, GOAL LAST**: an identity never replaces the goal and a goal never suppresses the identity.
  - **BOTH FENCE VOCABULARIES ARE STRIPPED LINE-EXACT** from an identity's instructions — the ROLE one so the body cannot close its own container, and the REQUEST one so it cannot forge a goal in main's voice. Same rule and same reason as `main/session-seed.js › frameOperatorTurn`. The name and both halves of every field pass a neutralizer belt at render as well (`main/prompt-sanitize.js › sanitizeText`), even though `SAFE_LABEL_RE` already bounded them at write.
    - ⚠ **THE BELT'S LENGTH BOUND IS THE FIELD'S OWN, AND EVERY REUSE OF A DISPLAY DEFAULT IS A BUG** (2026-08-23, F-287). **The neutralization is the security part** — the whitespace collapse and the fence-token strip, neither of which depends on the bound; **the length is a BUDGET and belongs to the field.** `main/prompt-sanitize.js › sanitizeName` is `sanitizeText(value, 80)` and 80 is correct for exactly one caller: a counterparty `display_name`, which has no server bound of its own. Reused for identity text it clipped a field VALUE (bounded 1000 by `schema.ts › IdentityFieldSchema`) to 80 and the identity NAME (bounded 120) to 80 in the role line, while every operator-facing surface kept showing the whole thing. The live numbers: **name 120, field key 80, field value 1000**, applied at BOTH the boundary (`main/identity-resolve.js › narrow`, per field) and the render (`main/prompt-framing-agent-identity.js › fieldLines`). **A BOUNDARY BOUND MUST MATCH THE WRITER'S, NEVER UNDERCUT IT** — a smaller one is a limit the operator can neither see nor satisfy, and the disagreement is silent and always resolves against them. The same parameterization now applies to `main/session-store.js › durableName` and `main/agent-history.js › historyName`, which persist `identityName` at 120.
  - **UNDER `read_only` THE ATTACHED BASES ARE NAMED AND NO TOOL CALL IS ORDERED.** That profile hard-denies `mcp__dopl__dopl_kb`, and a turn that ordered it would fail `prompt-profile-drift.test.mjs`. ⚠ **Named, not dropped** — §11's UNKNOWN-is-not-EMPTY rule: a silently missing section would be the prompt claiming the identity has no knowledge attached.
- **A SESSION REPORTS ITS IDENTITY BY NAME, AS A SNAPSHOT, AND ONLY TO ITS OPERATOR** (2026-08-23, Samuel's OQ-5 ruling; `supabase/migrations/20260823130000_channel_sessions_template_name.sql` — ✅ **APPLIED**, name `channel_sessions_template_name`, history version `20260823092005`, re-measured 2026-08-26 by the command above, joined on the NAME). `channel_sessions.identity_name` is an additive nullable TEXT column, and every word of that is load-bearing.
  - **A SESSION KEEPS ITS SPAWN-TIME IDENTITY CONTENT, AND THAT FALLS OUT OF THE ARCHITECTURE RATHER THAN BEING ENFORCED.** The resolve happens ONCE, in `main/session-launch-op.js`, and the answer is stashed on `context.identity`; the role block is built at WAKE from what was captured then (`main/session-seed.js › takeFraming` is a one-shot). An identity edited between spawn and wake does not change the session, an identity DELETED after spawn does not stop it, and a PARK/RESUME carries it for free because `main/session-park.js › resumeParked` works IN PLACE and never rewrites `s.context`.
    - ⚠ **A CRASH RESUME IS THE OTHER LANE AND IT DID *NOT* CARRY IT — CORRECTED 2026-08-23 (F-288).** This bullet named `resumeParked` as if it covered both, which is exactly the shape of a doc that wins the next argument: `main/session-park.js › startResume` is a full re-`startSession` off a DURABLE RECORD, and the durable projection is a literal whitelist that did not name the identity. So after a desktop crash the rebuilt session reported `identityName: null`, `identityName` is in `main/session-telemetry.js › STATE_FIELDS` (so the null BYPASSED the cadence floor), and the next push ERASED `channel_sessions.identity_name` under a still-running agent — the value an orchestrator reads in `read_sessions` to tell six agents apart. **THE FIX IS THE NAME, PERSISTED AND REHYDRATED, NOT THE IDENTITY**: `main/session-io.js › baseRecord` projects it, `main/session-store.js › durableSessionRecord` whitelists it (at the column's own 120, not `durableName`'s 80 display default), and `main/session-park.js › contextFromRecord` rebuilds it as a NAME-ONLY STUB. ⚠ **THE STUB IS SUFFICIENT AND THE BODY IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT**: `instructions` / `fields` / `knowledgeBases` have exactly one consumer, `main/prompt-framing-agent-identity.js › identityRoleFraming` through the one-shot `takeFraming`, which a resume never runs (`freshFraming` is false whenever `resumeSdkId` is set) — the SDK's own resume carries the original ROLE block. **A consumer that later reads `identity.instructions` off a LIVE session must not assume it is there.**
  - ⚠ **A DENORMALIZED SNAPSHOT, NOT AN FK, AND NOTHING MAY "FIX" THAT LATER.** A session captures its identity's content ONCE, at spawn, and keeps it for its whole life — so it must go on reporting what it **ran as** after the identity is renamed or deleted. An FK would rename a running agent under its operator, or (`ON DELETE SET NULL`) erase the only record of what it is executing. **A stale name here is correct, not drift.** The mappers resolve nothing: `src/features/channels/server/session-state-service.ts › toUpsert` stores what the desktop reported and `src/features/channels/server/collab-dto.ts › mapOwnSessionStateRow` passes it through.

  - **THE FENCE IS THE MAPPER; THE COLUMN GRANT IS THE BELT.** `identity_name` joins `OPERATOR_ONLY_SESSION_COLUMNS` / `OPERATOR_ONLY_SESSION_FIELDS` (`src/features/channels/server/collab-dto.ts`, parallel by construction, now EIGHT) and is mapped in `mapOwnSessionStateRow` only — `src/features/channels/server/collab-dto.ts › mapPeerSessionStateRow` BUILDS a narrow object, so it fails closed. `src/features/channels/server/session-visibility.test.ts` is a PROPERTY test over those arrays and **covers the new field with no new case, which is that suite's whole point**. The migration excludes the column from the `GRANT SELECT (…)` list for the PostgREST door only; `src/features/channels/schema-sql.test.ts` pins that exclusion.
  - **THE WIRE FIELD IS `identityName`, AND THE SERVER ACCEPTS IT BEFORE ANY DESKTOP SENDS IT.** `src/features/channels/schema-sessions.ts` bounds it `safeLabel(…, 120)` — character for character `agent_identities_name_charset_check`, so a name legal on an identity is never refusable into this projection. ⚠ **The rule that survives is ADDITIVE: a new push field is optional AND nullable** (§11, §13). (Corrected 2026-09-23: this said one unknown key would 400 a newer desktop's whole push — false, `SessionStateEntrySchema` is a zod 4 `z.object`, which STRIPS unknown keys; what does 400 the whole array is a KNOWN field with a value that fails its schema, since `retryable(400)` is false.)
  - **WHERE THE OPERATOR SEES IT:** `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/channel-session-render.ts › telemetryClauses` renders it as the FIRST clause, immediately before the model (`` `Code Auditor` · `opus-5` ``) — ⚠ and the MODEL half of that pair is guaranteed to be ONE token since F-293, so a name carrying a space is an identity and never a model — on own-scoped lines only — `read_sessions` and the `sessionBlockLines` block every `await` hold returns. A peer's line is unchanged: a handle and a state.
  - **AND ON THE AGENTS TAB'S OWN-AGENT CARD** (2026-08-22): `channels/components/agents-tab-cards.tsx › AgentCard` prints it in the existing detail line, **before** the model clause and with the same `·` separator the MCP surface uses — WHO the agent is reads ahead of WHAT it runs on. No pill and no `Identity:` label (INVARIANTS §5, minimal copy). ⚠ **ABSENT AND `null` BOTH RENDER NOTHING** — a blank agent has no identity and an older main omits the field, and neither is a reason to print a word. ⚠ **OPERATOR-ONLY HERE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A CHECK:** the field is on `spa-bridge-shapes.ts › DesktopSessionSummary` (this machine's own registry) and NOT on `hooks/use-channel-agent-sessions.ts › ChannelPeerSession`, so `› PeerCards` has nothing to render and nothing to be careful with. **Do not plumb it there.**
- ⚠ **IDENTITIES ARE ADDRESSED BY UUID AND HAVE NO SLUG AND NO NAME UNIQUENESS**, which is a MIRROR of `skills` (unique on `(workspace_id, slug)`, nothing on `name`) rather than of `teams` (unique on `(workspace_id, lower(name))`). Uniqueness across a visibility boundary would leak the existence of a private row through a conflict error, and two people may each keep a private "Researcher".
- **AN ORCHESTRATOR NAMES AN IDENTITY BY ID **OR** BY EXACT NAME, IN ONE PARAM, AND AN AMBIGUOUS NAME IS REFUSED WITH THE LIST** (2026-08-23). `dopl_channel(op="manage", action="launch")` gains `identity` (1–120), and the resolution happens SERVER-SIDE in `src/features/channels/server/service-launch-identity.ts › resolveIdentityForDirective`, over `src/features/agent-identities/server/service-resolve-ref.ts › resolveIdentityRef`. ⚠ **ONE PARAM FOR BOTH IS THE TREE'S OWN IDIOM**, not a new convention — `dopl_kb`'s `base` already takes either. The rule, in order: a UUID is an ID (and never falls back to a name lookup, or the two misses answer through each other); otherwise a CASE-INSENSITIVE EXACT name over the CALLER-VISIBLE set; **more than one match ⇒ REFUSE, listing each match's id and visibility; zero ⇒ the same `AGENT_IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND` shape `/resolve` answers.**
- 🔒 **AN ID RESOLVES ITS OWN CONTAINER, AND A `workspace=` THAT CONTRADICTS ONE IS IGNORED** (2026-09-02, A12 + B2 — supersedes the 2026-09-01 T35 rule below it). `src/shared/tenancy/resolve-resource.ts › resolveResource` answers WHERE an id lives; `src/shared/tenancy/read-resource.ts › readResourceById` is the ONE composition that follows that answer — it re-runs **the caller's own visibility-checked read** in the container the id named, with the caller's REAL role there. ⚠ **FOUR TYPES SINCE B2, NOT ONE**: `agent_identity`, `knowledge_base`, `skill`, `chat`, each a row in `resolve-resource.ts › RESOURCE_TABLES`. Adding a fifth is a row and a read path, never a second resolver. ⚠ **AN ENTRY IS NOT ONE OF THEM AND MUST NOT BECOME ONE**: `knowledge_entries` has no `visibility` column, so clause 4 below would have no arm to apply — `knowledge/server/service-entries.ts › readEntry` follows its BASE's id through `readBaseById` instead, which is what carries the audience ceiling along.
  - 🔓 **WRITES FOLLOW THE ID TOO — SAMUEL'S RULING, 2026-09-06** (supersedes "READS FOLLOW THE ID; WRITES STAY KEYED TO `ctx.workspaceId`", 2026-09-02, which recorded the ruling as OWED). ⚠ **THE RULING WAS FORCED BY THE SHAPE THE HALF-MIGRATION LEFT**: with the personal shelf a CONTAINER and `personal-reach.ts` default-on, a session could OPEN a base or an identity on its operator's shelf from any channel and then could not EDIT the row it had just rendered — `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_MISMATCH` / `AGENT_IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND`, one call apart, on the same id. A fence that opens the read and closes the write on the SAME row is a half-migration, not a fence. ⚠ **A WRITE GATE HANDS BACK THE CONTAINER, NOT JUST THE ROW** — `knowledge/server/service-bases.ts › getBaseForWrite` and `agent-identities/server/service-reads.ts › getIdentityForWrite` both return `ContainerRead`, and **every workspace-keyed call after them takes THAT context**: slug scans, team grants, both identity junctions, `hardDelete*`, the storage gate, the path walk, and the response re-read. Gating in one container and writing in another is worse than the refusal it replaces, and it is the only way this change can go wrong. ⚠ **THE ROLE COMES FROM THE RESOLVER, NOT THE ROOM**: `meetsMinRole(baseCtx.role, "admin")` and `assertMayWrite(tplCtx, …)` weigh the caller's standing where the ROW lives. ⚠ **NOTHING ELSE MOVED**: both fences still run in order, `assertBaseWritable` / `assertMayWrite` / `agent_write_enabled` / the shared-credential and team-scope guards are untouched, and a row that clears the resolver but not the matrix is the same single 404. ⚠ **A FEATURE OPTS IN BY MIGRATING ITS CALL SITES.** Migrated: the base PATCH and DELETE, `write_file`, `create_folder`, `delete`, `move`, and the identity PATCH and DELETE. **Not yet migrated, and still correctly refusing a cross-container id**: `service-stars.ts` and the `channel-grants` route — each needs the re-based context threaded through its own follow-up calls, never just the first half. (⚠ **A THIRD SITE LEFT THIS LIST BY BEING DELETED, NOT MIGRATED** — knowledge pinning's write service went with the feature on 2026-09-18; see §10's pinning-removal bullet.) Pinned in `knowledge/server/service-bases-resolve.test.ts › 🔓 the by-id WRITE doors name the id's own container` and `agent-identities/server/service-writes-tenancy.test.ts › 🔓 update and delete name the id's own container` (⚠ **this line named `service-writes.test.ts` until 2026-09-07** — that file exists, so the citation resolved and pointed at a suite holding no such block; the tenancy cases live in their own file), both of which assert the CONTAINER the repository was called with.
  - ⚠ **A SLUG DOES NOT FOLLOW, AND NEITHER DOES A NAME.** `skills` is unique on `(workspace_id, slug)` — per CONTAINER — and `agent_identities` has no name uniqueness at all, so both can legitimately match in several containers and every tie-break resolves one the caller did not choose. An id is a primary key and has no such question, which is exactly why `workspace=` is redundant on it and not on the others.
  - ⚠ **A FOLLOWED READ CARRIES ITS WHOLE CONTEXT.** `readResourceById` returns the CONTEXT the read succeeded in, because a row is rarely one query: a skill's body and KB references, a chat's messages, and a chat's RETENTION WINDOW (a billing plan — `chats/server/retention.ts › resolveChatsWindow`) are all keyed to the container the row lives in, not the one the caller was authorised in.
  ⚠ **RESOLUTION IS NOT AUTHORISATION**: the resolver is strictly NARROWER than each feature's matrix (it cannot see a team-scoped row an admin can), so it is an ADDRESS and the matrix is the fence, in that order. ⚠ **THE FENCE IS FOUR CLAUSES IN ONE PLACE**: a SHARED credential resolves nothing; the container must be one the caller is an ACTIVE member of at the `viewer` floor (so a `guest` container is excluded, matching every resource route's own floor); the credential's own `apiKeyWorkspaceId` lock NARROWS the candidate set (§4 layer B1 — a locked credential resolves inside its lock and nowhere else); and the row must be one the caller could already list — the owner column is the caller, or the row is shared with every member of its container. Another member's `private`/`team` row matches nothing anywhere, so a probed id answers exactly as a nonexistent one does. ⚠ **"SHARED WITH EVERY MEMBER" IS ONE COLUMN ON IDENTITIES AND TWO EVERYWHERE ELSE** — `visibility='workspace'` there, `visibility='public' AND access_mode='workspace'` on bases, skills and chats, because a `public` row in `access_mode='teams'` is visible to the GRANTED TEAMS and not to the container. ⚠ **AND A SOFT-DELETED ROW IS NOT NAMEABLE**: the three tables that have `deleted_at` filter it, or an id would resolve a container for a row every read then skips. Pinned un-mocked against the query builder in `src/shared/tenancy/resolve-resource.test.ts`, the follow in `src/shared/tenancy/read-resource.test.ts`, and one composition test per feature (`*-resolve.test.ts`); every service suite above them mocks the module.

The **RESOLVE** fence is the OPERATOR's, on their desktop, at claim time (§11). Both are required and neither substitutes. The consequences are fail-closed and are written down rather than debugged: a `workspace` identity works; a `team` identity the orchestrator is in and the operator is not is CREATED and then refused `no-identity` on the machine; the orchestrator's own PRIVATE identity is unusable over this lane unless the orchestrator IS the operator (the common case, not the only one); and a KB the OPERATOR cannot read is simply OMITTED from their resolve payload, so a shared identity cannot launder access to a private base.

### The surface (measured 2026-08-22)

- **ONE PAGE, ONE ROUTE, ONE NAV ROW: `/:workspaceSegment/agents`.** Seam at `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/identities/index.tsx`, surface at `src/features/agent-identities/components/agent-identities-core.tsx` — Next-free and ROUTER-FREE by construction, like every shared page core. ⚠ **The label and the segment are both `Agents`/`agents`, NOT "agent identities"**: the operator's noun for the thing they author is the AGENT, and §5's noun rule ("the noun on both is the **AGENT**") is a copy rule with tests behind it, not a style preference.
  - ⚠ **NO `agents/:identityId` DETAIL ROW, and the absence is load-bearing.** An identity is edited in a MODAL, not at a URL, so the hand copy in `dopl-desktop-app/main/deep-link-target.js › WORKSPACE_PAGES` carries **`agents: false`** — a `true` there hands the renderer a third segment matching no route. **All FOUR places the route table's docblock demands are written**: the route row, the `NavSection` member + `NAV` row in `src/shared/layout/app-shell/app-sidebar-core.tsx`, and that hand copy. `apps/desktop-ui/src/routes.test.tsx › registers the agents page` and `› gives the agents page its sidebar nav row` pin the first three against each other; `dopl-desktop-app/test/deep-link-target.test.mjs › the page table matches the SPA's route table` DERIVES the fourth from `routes.tsx` and fails on any drift — so a future detail row is a two-file change or the desktop suite goes red.
- 🚫 **NOTHING ON THIS PAGE IS PRESSED IN (Samuel's ruling, 2026-08-22).** No `FIELD_WELL`, no `.concave-field`, no `.concave-track`, no `SECTION_BOX_INSET`, no `SectionBox` — RAISED, ELEVATED and FLAT faces only. The three scope panels are the flat `bg-card-surface-subtle` face on a hairline (deliberately **not** `SectionBox`, whose BODY is `bg-bg-inset` plus the concave inset shadow); cards are `.bento`; a text control that is NOT a popup-form field wears the kit's RAISED well — `shared/ui/wells.ts › RAISED_INPUT`, which is `RAISED_WELL` plus type/placeholder/focus and which **was promoted OUT of this feature on 2026-08-27** (see the standard-dialog bullet below) — `identity-approval.tsx` imports it from there directly (the `identity-editor-rows.tsx` re-exports were deleted 2026-09-23, P7-20). ⚠ **THE POPUP FORM'S OWN FIELDS ARE THE UNDERLINE SINCE 2026-09-08** (the `FormDialog` bullet below) — `RAISED_INPUT` is what the editor's inline key/value LIST still wears, and neither face is pressed in, which is the ruling both halves keep. ⚠ **Pinned as a SOURCE READ, not a render** — `components/identity-editor-surface.test.tsx › no concave surfaces` sweeps the feature's UI directories for those class names, because jsdom loads no stylesheet and a rendered assertion would pass against a concave field and prove nothing. ⚠ **The sweep moved file on 2026-09-08** (it was `components/identity-editor.test.tsx`), for the §1 line cap and nothing else.
- **THREE PANELS, ONE READ.** `GET /api/agent-identities` answers everything the caller may see and `lib/visibility.ts › groupByVisibility` splits it into Private / Team / Public. The server does not group (see the route's own docblock), and the client does not FILTER — a second "is this mine?" test would either duplicate the visibility matrix above or hide a row the server deliberately sent. ⚠ **A row whose `visibility` this build does not know is DROPPED from the sections rather than filed under one** (§11 — UNKNOWN is not EMPTY, and it is not a guess either). ⚠ **KNOWLEDGE IS DECORATED PER ROW CONTAINER (P7-02, 2026-09-23)** (`server/service-reads.ts › listIdentities` → `› decorateByContainer`): an unfiltered or `home` list spans the calling container and the caller's personal one, and junction rows are filed under the row's container — decorating the whole list against the calling container showed personal identities with no knowledge, and a save from the editor then REPLACED the hidden set.
  - 🚫 **THERE IS NO FIXTURE FALLBACK ON THIS READ, AND ONE MUST NOT COME BACK (2026-08-26, F-332 ✅ RESOLVED).** `hooks/use-agent-identities.ts` returns `query.data ?? []` and the error, full stop: a FAILED read renders the plain error state and nothing else, in every build. A dev-only fallback (`client/mock.ts` + `› isMockFallback`, gated on `process.env.NODE_ENV`) existed from 2026-08-23 while the migration above was unapplied; it is applied, and — the reason this is a rule rather than a cleanup — **the same hook now reads a link CONTAINER, where a 403/404 is an ORDINARY answer** (roster change, stale header, a guest opening the tab), so the branch had become a dev build painting fabricated identities under a channel that has none. UNKNOWN is not EMPTY and it is not a GUESS either (§11). `hooks/use-agent-identities.test.ts` is the rewritten-to-survivors pin.
  - **An empty panel keeps its header and says one quiet line.** A section that vanished when empty would make "you have no team identities" and "this workspace has no teams" the same picture.

Same discipline as `channels/components/new-thread-dialog.test.tsx › the payload is the panel's, field for field`.

The Model row offers the identity runtime's live catalog (`agent-identities/lib/identity-runtime.ts › identityModelOptions`; the channels-side `AGENT_MODEL_OPTIONS` list it used to read was deleted 2026-09-23), and without the Default option the `SelectMenu` rendered BLANK on every new identity and could never be put back once a model was chosen. A pill row needs one option selected and the honest one is the value the draft holds — a back-filled "Sonnet" would claim a pin the row does not have (§11).

- 🔒 **AN IDENTITY HAS A RUNTIME (Samuel, rulings 4–6, 2026-09-23: *"Identity gets a runtime"* / *"Identity's, unless picked"* / *"From their model"*).** `agent_identities.runtime` is nullable; NULL = no preference, the channel decides (`20261021120000_agent_identities_runtime.sql`, §12, WRITTEN NOT APPLIED). It rides the DTO (`types.ts › AgentIdentity.runtime`, `string | null`), the create/update schema (`schema.ts`, the runtime-id GRAMMAR only, never an enum — the roster is the desktop's), the resolve payload above, and `dopl_agent` (create/update take `runtime`, `null` clears; get/list render it — `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/agent-ops-write.ts`, `agent-ops-read.ts`). No Claude-frozen fallback on this surface (review F11/P7-12). Switching runtime drops a model the new READY catalog positively lacks (`› modelAfterRuntimeChange`); **Any** clears the model.

The model row, native summary and sign-in note follow the LAUNCH runtime, and the model row drops an identity model the launch runtime's READY roster positively lacks (the desktop's `identityModelFor` rule, mirrored for display).

The /home SPA cards pass none yet (re-verified 2026-09-23).

Pinned by `shared/ui/standard-dialog.test.tsx`.

The two faces are alternatives, not layers (`shared/ui/select-menu.tsx › TRIGGER_FACE`); the flat one's `hover:bg-surface-raised-2` would flatten the raised gradient.

The old note argued a second surface puts the operator two Escapes from their draft; what settled it is that a field is about to be more than a key and a value, and a row that grows four controls wide is a form pretending to be a list. **Editing and removing stay INLINE.** ⚠ The dialog's confirm reads **"Add", not "Add field"** — the title already names the thing, and two buttons with one accessible name is ambiguous for the operator and for `getByRole`. ⚠ `cleanFields` is still the save-time backstop, pinned in `lib/identity-draft.test.ts`, not in the modal's suite.

ONE component for create and edit; the only differences are the heading, the Save verb, and whether Delete exists. **It stays OPEN until the write settles** and closes only on success (`create-channel-dialog.tsx`'s idiom): the writes are optimistic, so a modal that closed on the click would leave a failed save with nowhere to report — the row silently rolls back and the operator's edit is gone with no sentence saying why.

- **NO LAUNCH UI ON THIS PAGE.** Choosing an identity AT LAUNCH is a later phase, and `agent-identities-core.test.tsx › what this page deliberately leaves out` refuses one — a beachhead here would be a second surface deciding what starting an agent means, which is what `resolve` exists to keep singular.

### The /home face — identities inside a link container (2026-08-26, `docs/specs/home-agents-tab.plan.md` M2)

- **THE SAME `visibility` COLUMN ANSWERS SHARING INSIDE A CONTAINER, AND NOTHING NEW WAS BUILT TO ASK IT (Samuel's ruling Q1).** A `kind='link'` container has no teams (§4A), so the three values collapse to TWO live ones: `workspace` = **shared with the other person in this relationship**, `private` = the creator's alone. `agent_only` has no identity referent (an identity has ONE consumer — main, at spawn — where a KB has two, which is why Knowledge shares by GRANT and this shares by VISIBILITY). ⚠ **A `channel_resource_grants` row for identities would be a THIRD copy of the visibility matrix** (this section already keeps two, and they must move together); widening was correct only for a MULTI-CHANNEL standard workspace and was filed as **F-334**, not built. 🔒 **F-334 IS CLOSED-BY-RULING (2026-09-17) AND THE RULING IS THE OPPOSITE OF BUILDING IT**: Samuel — *"In workspaces, resource access is not scoped by channels. It's instead scoped by teams."* (§4A). The gap that entry costed is not a gap: a standard workspace HAS its sub-workspace scope, and it is the team. **Do not re-open it as a widening.**
- **THREE SCOPES, TWO SECTIONS, TWO WORKSPACES** (`apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/home/identity-panels.tsx`): **A** container + `workspace`; **B** container + `private` + the caller's own; **C** the caller's HOME workspace + `private` + their own. B and C share a `SelectMenu` pill because they are the same shelf at two ranges; A is its own section because it is a different QUESTION — who else can wear this identity.
  - ⚠ **THE SECTION-A HEADING IS "Shared in this channel", NEVER "Public"**, and both container label sets live in `agent-identities/lib/visibility.ts › SECTIONS_CONTAINER` / `› SECTION_PRIVATE_EVERYWHERE` — beside `› SECTIONS`, never hand-typed in a component. **Two arrays in one module cannot drift the way two components can.** `team` is a DEAD value here, so `SECTIONS_CONTAINER` has exactly two entries and a `team` row is **DROPPED** by `› groupByVisibility`, never re-filed under a live scope (§11: UNKNOWN is not a guess).

Scope C's workspace id rides `POST /api/boot`'s `workspace`, which is **NULL until the caller is onboarded** — that scope then reads UNAVAILABLE, never EMPTY. **No new endpoint and no channel-scoped key**: the workspace element already separates the two entries, unlike Knowledge's (§9). This is exactly the surface F-331's entry-key rule exists for (§8).

Four distinct sentences (A, B, C, and "no home workspace"), each against its own resolved read — the container and home reads move independently.
