Re-measure rather than quoting — the command is in the FOUR NARRATION DEFECTS bullet above.

- 🔒 **`manage(action="direct")` / `status` — THE PRIVATE DIRECT LANE (Samuel's ruling, 2026-08-31; renamed by B8, 2026-09-02).** An operator's EXTERNAL agent may send a private message into one of that operator's OWN running desktop sessions, and read that turn's final text back. The write half is `manage`, gated whole in `gating.ts › WRITE_OPS.dopl_channel`; the READ half folded into `op="status"`, which returns the session table AND the direction mailbox in one answer — "what is running" and "what is queued for it" are the two halves of one question, and an orchestrator that asked only the first read a machine with nothing running and no sign that three directions were waiting. ⚠ **THE SPEC'S §2.3 ROW SAID `direct_agent` FOLDS INTO `send(to=@agent)`, AND IT DID NOT (F-576).** That mapping presupposes a server that FILES a `channel_agent_directions` row for an idle agent recipient; wave B batch 1 stamps `recipient_agent_ids` and predicts a verdict but files nothing, so folding it would have deleted the private lane rather than moving it.
  - 🔒 **IT REACHES THE CALLER'S OWN OPERATOR AND NOBODY ELSE, AND THE ABSENCE OF AN ARGUMENT IS THE WHOLE AUTHORIZATION STORY.** No schema on this path accepts an operator id and none may ever get one — the server stamps `ctx.userId`, written LAST in `repository-directions.ts › insertAgentDirection` so no payload key can shadow it, and every read and write carries it as a SQL predicate on the admin client. A peer can neither be directed nor direct you, and there is no spelling of the API that says otherwise. Asserted, not reviewed: `server/service-directions.test.ts`.

This one names an INSTANCE ID on the caller's own machine and addresses nobody in the channel, which is exactly the distinction that guard keeps. It accepts the `@agent-<id>` handle `read_sessions` prints as well as the bare id, because refusing the printed form would be a 400 for doing what the neighbouring op taught.

The op's copy, its five refusal words and its hold are unchanged.

It is safe to DISCLOSE because sender and recipient are the same operator's agents by construction. **`null` is the ORDINARY case** — an external orchestrator sends no session stamp — and renders as the sentence the surface already showed, never as a raw id.

- 🔒 **THE PING LANE IS DELETED (Samuel's ruling B8, 2026-09-02; retired at slice B8, deleted at B16).** The op names, the `@dopl/client` methods, the contracts types, the ping service and repository modules, the `/api/pings` routes, the desktop's ping module and its realtime binding are all gone; the never-applied `channel_pings` migration (version `20260907130000`) was deleted a wave earlier, so the lane never had storage in any environment. **A directed `send` IS the delivery record** — it names one recipient, the server resolves it, and the result's `delivery=` is the acknowledgement the mailbox row existed to be, which is why the lane could retire rather than be renamed.

The card distinguishes an ESCALATION (option buttons, waiting on a press) from an ordinary request, which is a fact about the message rather than a self-report. **`check-message-kind-drift.ts` still holds the wave-A set**; nothing was added to the `CHECK`.

- 🔒 **`to`'s HANDLE PROMISE IS TRUE ON `op="send"` AND CANNOT BE KEPT ON `op="manage"` (2026-09-18, S51).** The describe offered *"an agent (`@agent-<id>` or its handle)"* in its HEADLINE, over every op. On a send that is honest — `channels/server/service-writes-metadata-recipient.ts › resolveToRecipients` resolves a NAME. On the manage lane nothing does: `channel-agent-id.ts › bareAgentId` strips `@` and `agent-` **without validating** (deliberately — the pasted form is what `op="status"` prints), so `to="@my-agent"` reached `AgentDirectiveCreateSchema.agentId`'s anchored eight-character grammar and died as a bare `VALIDATION_FAILED`. ⚠ **REFUSE, DO NOT RESOLVE, AND THE REASON IS THAT THERE IS NOTHING TO RESOLVE WITH**: no `@dopl/client` method maps a name to an instance id, and `channel_sessions.name` IS the id on any current desktop (the `channel-session-handle.ts` bullet above), so a local resolver would be inventing a lookup rather than restating one. **`channel-agent-target.ts › agentTarget` refuses `field=to reason=not_an_agent_id retry=dopl_channel(op="status")` before the call**, on all four manage verbs — `end`, `rename`, `posture`, `direct` — which share the strip and now share the check. ⚠ **EVERY PASTED FORM STILL PASSES** (`@agent-<id>`, `agent-<id>`, `@<id>`, bare): the refusal is only for a value that is not an id at all. ⚠ **`opReadDirections` KEEPS THE BARE STRIP**, deliberately — its `agent` is a FILTER over rows the caller already owns, not an address, so an unmatchable value answers an empty list and there is nothing to refuse. ⚠ The describe is corrected in the same change and is **net −7**: the forms moved DOWN into the per-op clauses, where they differ, rather than being reworded.
- **`send(kind="decision")` — A STRUCTURED QUESTION TO A HUMAN, AND IT IS A SEND (Samuel's ruling, 2026-08-31; folded by B8, 2026-09-02).** Four validated fields, of which TWO are now the fields every send already has — `summary` is the issue (one line, the card's title), `body` the context (bounded at `escalation.ts › ESCALATION_CONTEXT_MAX`, refused pre-call by `channel-ops-write.ts › decisionRefusal` so an over-long one is not an opaque VALIDATION_FAILED about a field the caller never named), plus `options` (2–6, each a `label` and a one-line `consequence`) and `recommendation` (`{index, why}`) — that the channels surface renders as a CARD WITH OPTION BUTTONS. In `gating.ts › WRITE_OPS.dopl_channel`, because it writes a real message row.

It is a HAND COPY of `src/features/channels/escalation.ts › escalationBody`, paired the way `main/agent-handles.js` is paired with `lib/mentions.ts`: **one fixture table (`ESCALATION_BODY_PARITY_CASES`), driven from both sides**, so either tree changing the render alone fails a suite.

The @-tag in the body is the inbox mechanism and it starts nobody, so the op's prose and its result both send the agent to one.

- **`create_thread` NOW RUNS FROM A WINDOWLESS DESKTOP SESSION, UNDER THE OPERATOR'S OUTBOUND POSTURE (2026-08-24, Samuel's ruling).** It rides AXIS B's own-channel OUTBOUND lane exactly like `post` and `milestone` — §11 carries the rule and the argument. **What this section owes the reader is the CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TOOL SURFACE:** the op the `THE PROTOCOL` paragraph tells an agent to open with was previously auto-refused on every windowless session in every posture, so an agent taught to start with it could not, and the refusal named a permission prompt rather than anything it could act on. It is now the operator's own MESSAGES POSTURE that decides — an open outbound half sends it, `ask` raises a consent row with the title, the body and the addressee on it. ⚠ **THIS SENTENCE SAID "the operator's auto-send setting" UNTIL 2026-09-07; auto-send was deleted on 2026-09-06** (§6) and the axis it duplicated is the one that decides. ⚠ **A slug-addressed `create_thread` still gates** (the ID scope, §11), which is why `prompt-framing.js › channelScopeFraming` interpolates the channel UUID.
- **`launch_agent` NOW RUNS FROM A WINDOWLESS DESKTOP SESSION TOO, UNDER BOTH POSTURES AND A RECURSION BOUND (2026-08-25, Samuel's ruling; F-320).** §11 carries the rule, the two-axis conjunction, the depth bound and the refusal vocabulary. **What THIS section owes the reader is the CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TOOL SURFACE:** an agent running on an operator's own machine can now ASK that machine for another agent — the op's whole point, and previously unreachable from a desktop session in every posture — while everything the op's own result copy says is unchanged, because **nothing about the DIRECTIVE lane moved**.   | **B1** — the credential lock | `mcp_tokens.container_id` → `apiKeyWorkspaceId` → `withWorkspaceAuth`'s 403 (§4) | 🔒 **FENCE** — rides the credential, so it binds the process AND its children. ⚠ **CONTAINER AXIS ONLY** — the row's `subject_user_id` is a separate column on a separate axis, read by `credential-audience.ts › isSharedCredential` and never by a container gate (F-336). ⚠ `workspace_id` is dual-written beside `container_id` for one release and read as the fallback; B13 drops the pair |
  | **B3** — the directory lock | `factory.ts › bootServer` → `workspace-directory.ts`'s `lockedTo` | ⚠ **TRIPWIRE** — one MCP connection's view |
  | **B2** — the desktop belt | `main/session-audience.js`, `grantDecision` step 1.5 (§11) | ⚠ **TRIPWIRE** — one machine's permission gate |

  - **LAYER A'S DECISION TABLE, AND THREE OF ITS FOUR BRANCHES CHANGE NOTHING.** `source !== "agent"` → unrestricted (humans unaffected); **channel scope not allowed in this container → unrestricted**; **not a shared room → unrestricted (SOLO, today's behaviour)**; else reachable **iff** a grant row at EITHER level (`agent_only` OR `visible`) on one of the container's channels, and everything else is the same 404 an invisible base throws. **It can only ever CLOSE.**
    - 🔒 **THE TWO MIDDLE ARMS ARE THE TWO SHARED PREDICATES SINCE 2026-09-18 (Samuel's fail-closed ruling; F-718 RESOLVED) — NOT A CONJUNCTION SPELLED HERE.** `shared/tenancy/channel-scope.ts › channelScopeAllowedForKind`, then `shared/tenancy/shared-room.ts › isSharedRoom`. What they replace — `kind !== 'link'` followed by `memberCount <= 1` — was the LAST site answering "is this room shared" its own way, and it failed OPEN twice: a real `0` (a roster race, a `status` flip mid-request) took the unrestricted arm, and every kind added to `WorkspaceKind` after `link` inherited it (F-295/F-564). `shared-room-parity.test.ts`'s `DEVIATIONS` list is now EMPTY.
    - 🔒 **A SHARED STANDARD WORKSPACE IS `unrestricted`, AND THE AGENT SEES EXACTLY WHAT A MEMBER SEES.** Per the 2026-09-17 scope ruling a channel-scoped grant is REFUSED in a standard container, so the `granted` arm there could only ever answer with an EMPTY set. The audience is the member's — WORKSPACE-WIDE + TEAMS, applied by `service-shared.ts › canSeeBase` / `› filterTeamVisibleBases` one layer out. ⚠ **This is the ceiling declining to add a bound, never a second grant path**: nothing in this arm can make a base reachable that the human gate refused.
    - ⚠ **A `null` KIND (the row vanished mid-request) ANSWERS `unrestricted`**, which is `channelScopeAllowedForKind`'s own reading and the same one the WRITE door takes; `withWorkspaceAuth` proved an active membership one fence earlier. ⚠ The SOLO carve-out is deliberate at every layer: a one-member container is the operator's primary agent surface (§4A's traffic-profile bullet), and there is no second audience in it to bound. ⚠ **CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS RULING 2 AND NOT AN ACCIDENT:** a scope-B base (private, in the container, ungranted) is INVISIBLE to the operator's own agent there.
  - 🔒 ✅ **AND THE REMEDY RULING 2 NAMES WORKS — F-336 RESOLVED 2026-08-27 (Samuel: "option B"). A scope-B base is invisible to the operator's own agent UNTIL IT IS GRANTED `agent_only` (or `visible`) ON ONE OF THIS CONTAINER'S CHANNELS**, and then it is readable. ⚠ **IT DID NOT WORK BETWEEN 2026-08-26 AND THAT RULING, AND THE MECHANISM IS WORTH KEEPING:** `service-bases.ts › getBaseById` runs `assertBaseVisible` **BEFORE** `assertWithinAudience`, and `canSeeBase` answered false for ANY non-public base once `apiKeyWorkspaceId` was set — so the grant row was never consulted and the `agent_only` level was decoration. **THE FIX WAS NOT A FENCE WIDENING.** B1 was trespassing on layer A's axis: a locked credential is a WORKSPACE fence, and `canSeeBase` was reading it as a VISIBILITY fence. The predicate now asks `shared/auth/credential-audience.ts › isSharedCredential` — a container SESSION carries its operator's id and reads that human's private rows; a credential that may be passed between humans still reads none. ✅ **SINCE 2026-09-02 THAT IS A NULL CHECK ON `mcp_tokens.subject_user_id`, NOT AN INFERENCE FROM A LOCK KIND** (§4, `mcp_token_credential_axes`): an absent subject is the refusal, so a future producer inherits the narrow rule by forgetting rather than by opting in. **Three refusals, three different fences, one 404:** ungranted → layer A; another workspace → B1's 403 / the service's workspace check; a PEER's private base → `canSeeBase` itself. Pinned by `knowledge/server/service-container-credential.test.ts`.
  - 🔒 **F-327-PROOFING, AND THE SENTENCE THAT LICENSES IT.** The ceiling takes the **SET** of the container's channels, because nothing enforces one-channel-per-container. `X-Dopl-Session-Id` parsed `<channelId>:<tail>` may then NARROW that set to one channel **iff the id is already in it**; anything else is ignored ENTIRELY. **A forgeable input used only to narrow inside an already-fenced set is safe** — the set is computed from DB facts BEFORE the header is read, every id the header can select was already in it, and selecting one only REMOVES grants. The worst a forged value achieves is fencing the forger out. ⚠ **Do not "improve" it into a lookup**: resolving the named channel against the database would make the header an ADDRESSING input, which is the one power it must not have.
  - **B3, PLAINLY: `getWorkspaceList()` answers `[container]` and `resolveWorkspaceRef` answers `null` for every other id and slug**, and the INSTRUCTIONS table is empty (a locked session is already bound to that one container). ⚠ **Bash can open a SECOND, unpinned MCP connection or hit the loopback directly; neither passes through that object.** Pinned by `packages/mcp-server/src/container-lock.test.ts`, whose header says the same thing so a green run cannot be read as containment.
  - 🔒 ⚠ **`memberCount` IS NEW ON `WorkspaceListItem` AND FAILS CLOSED — §8's STALE-FIELD RULE, INVERTED, IN THREE PLACES.** **ZERO IS NOT SOLO**, in `packages/mcp-server/src/shared-room.ts › isSharedRoom` (which `factory.ts › bootServer` calls since 2026-09-17; it spelled the `?? 0` inline until then), `main/session-credential.js › shouldLockSession` and `main/session-audience.js › audienceFor`. The reflex fallback (unknown ⇒ the permissive case) would silently unlock every container for exactly the release window in which a client runs against a server predating the field. ⚠ It is **HAND-MIRRORED** between `src/features/workspaces/types.ts › WorkspaceWithRole` and `packages/dopl-client/src/types.ts › WorkspaceListItem` (plus the tracked `dist/`), and since 2026-08-26 `scripts/check-role-drift.ts › checkWorkspaceMirror` guards that pair — a SECOND family in the same CI step, carrying one recorded pre-existing asymmetry (`iconUrl`, **F-335**) whose allow-list **may only ever shrink**.
  - **THE RESIDUAL, STATED HONESTLY — AND IT IS THREE THINGS, NOT TWO (corrected 2026-08-26).** (1) A session whose B1 mint FAILED (the desktop fails OPEN and logs — a credential endpoint being down must not stop the operator's agent). (2) Anything using the operator's device token OUTSIDE a desktop-spawned session, which the ceiling never claimed to cover. Layer A still refuses the knowledge read in both. (3) 🔴 **AN UNLOCKED CREDENTIAL REACHABLE FROM INSIDE THE LOCKED SESSION.** `mcp-config.js` wrote the operator's unlocked 90-day device token in PLAINTEXT to `userData/mcp-spawn.json`, and `runtime/claude/loader.js › buildSecretPathDenyRules` fences that path for `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` only — **`Bash` is not on that list and cannot be**, because Claude Code `Bash(...)` rules match COMMAND patterns, not path globs. One `cat` voids B1 for the session, and layer A with it (the ceiling only fires on `apiKeyWorkspaceId`). ⚠ **The real mitigation is that `Bash` is an ESCALATION tool** (§11), so the read gates at every posture except `bypass` — **B1 is therefore a STRONG TRIPWIRE, not the fence F-329 declared it.** ✅ The file is no longer written and is deleted on the next signed-in launch; the encrypted store under the same directory is not, so the CLASS is open. **F-329 is REOPENED with this as residual #3.**
- **`packages/*/dist` is what the app loads at runtime.** After editing either package's `src/`, run `npm run build:packages` or the old surface ships.
- **MCP tool output carries NO web URLs (2026-08-11).** The knowledge/skill file-write results dropped their `webUrl` field and the `View in Dopl: <url>` trailer — the website those URLs named is retired and 302s to `/get-started`. `src/shared/lib/url/resource-url.ts` is deleted; the onboarding bootstrap prompt no longer teaches the trailer or a `{{URL}}` card slot. (Shipped pre-1.10.3 bundles still carry the old prompt text until they auto-update — a cosmetic mismatch, not a contract.)
- **THE PLAYGROUND IS A SECOND DOOR TO THE SAME MCP TRANSPORT, NEVER A SECOND SERVER (2026-08-17).** The public `/playground` page demos a REAL guest workspace: `POST /api/playground/session` (anonymous, per-IP limited) provisions a throwaway `auth.users` row stamped `user_metadata.playground_guest: true`, a workspace through `features/workspaces/server/service.ts › createWorkspaceForUser` (so the starter corpus seeds it), and a 24h full-scope bearer under the reserved `dopl_client_playground` client (`features/playground/server/token.ts`, hash/rand/prefix primitives imported from `shared/auth/mcp-oauth.ts` so the row stays `validateAccessToken`-compatible). `app/api/playground/mcp/[token]/route.ts` exists because desktop MCP clients accept a URL and no headers — it moves the path token into `Authorization` and DELEGATES to `/api/mcp`'s exported handlers, so auth/gating/credits cannot drift; keep its function config identical to `/api/mcp` (nodejs, 300s). The page's panes poll ordinary workspace GETs with the same bearer (`features/playground/session.tsx`). Guests bill as the FREE plan — the credit allowance is the abuse cap, no playground carve-out. Deletion is the reaper cron (`app/api/cron/playground-reaper`, vercel.json): it double-gates on the playground client id AND the guest metadata marker, and skips+logs on any mismatch — never delete on one signal. Both routes are reasoned EXEMPT entries in `shared/auth/write-gate-coverage.test.ts`; `/api/playground` is in `SELF_AUTH_ROUTES` and the `/playground` page in `PUBLIC_ROUTES` (`src/shared/auth/public-routes.ts` — §3, not `proxy.ts`, since 2026-08-23).

- 🔒 **EVERY `dopl_kb` REFUSAL NAMES THE FIELD, THE LIMIT, THE REASON AND THE RETRY (2026-09-18, Round 1 batch B — S52, S41, S43, S40).** The grammar was already there (`tools/tool-errors.ts › refusal`, the bullet above); what was missing is that the ungoverned refusals never reached it. **The codes are declared once, in `tool-errors.ts`, and are EMIT-ONLY** — `fieldTooLong(field, limit)`, `KB_INVALID_FIELD`, `KB_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND`, `KB_TARGET_VANISHED`, `SESSION_REQUIRED` — **and none of them may be added to `KB_ERRORS`**: `renderErrors` pushes the first THREE, so a fourth row silently drops `ambiguous_slug`, and `dopl_kb`'s composed description sits ~112 characters under `HARD_DESCRIPTION_CEILING`, which THROWS at import and takes the server down with it. ⚠ **ALL OF IT IS PER-CALL TEXT** (`write-result-budget.test.ts`), so the served total is untouched — putting words in the refusal rather than in a `.describe()` is this surface's own instruction.
  - ⚠ **A BRANCH NAMES ITS OWN FIELD'S RULE AND NO OTHER FIELD'S (S52).** A 301-character `excerpt` was answered *"Titles can't contain '/'"* — the field named, the wrong rule printed — so an agent that shortened its TITLE got the identical refusal again. `tools/knowledge-validation.ts` (split out of `knowledge-shared.ts` at the §1 cap) now carries one arm per field, and `opCreateFolder` has a mapper at all: the folder half rethrew a raw `VALIDATION_FAILED` with no field, no number and no remedy. ⚠ The two 300s and the 1 MB are HAND-MIRRORED there from `src/config/index.ts › DESCRIPTION_MAX` and the files route's `MAX_BODY_BYTES`; a quoted number that UNDERCUT the real bound would refuse a legal write.
  - ⚠ **A MISSING PATH IS A REFUSAL THAT SAYS THE ENTRY MAY HAVE MOVED (S41).** `EntryNotFoundError` → 404 `KNOWLEDGE_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND` and `PathTraversalError` → 404 `KNOWLEDGE_PATH_NOT_FOUND` were mapped by NOTHING, so both rethrew past the registrar as an unhandled transport error. `knowledge-shared.ts › entryNotFound` answers both on `op="read_file"` and `op="outline"` with `reason=entry_not_found · retry=op="list_dir"`. ⚠ **"May have moved" is not a hedge**: a path is a POSITION, `move_file` and a retitle both vacate one, and `write_file` is an UPSERT — so an agent told only "not found" writes a DUPLICATE at the old path. The refusal names the entry id as the handle that survives a move. ⚠ `KB_ERRORS`' docblock asserted *"no code path emits that literal"*; that described the absent mapper, and is corrected in the same change.
  - 🔒 **`force=true` NO LONGER DISARMS THE SERVER'S ANTI-DUPLICATE GUARD (S40).** `service-paths.ts` refused the vanished-target case only when a precondition was present — and `force` sends NONE (`packages/dopl-client › writeKbFileByPath`, `expectedVersion === null`), so the call most likely to be a retry-after-timeout was the ONE arm that skipped the guard and upserted a second entry at a path a move had emptied. **Unrecoverable: deletion is app-only.** The client now sends `X-Expect-Existing: 1` beside the absent precondition, `WriteFileByPathInput.expectExisting` carries the BELIEF (it compares nothing and cannot 412), and the refusal is the new `KnowledgeTargetVanishedError` → **409 `KNOWLEDGE_TARGET_VANISHED`, not a 412**: no version mismatched, the row is gone, and a 412 sent callers to `read_file` for a version that cannot exist. ⚠ The MCP arm is discriminated on the CODE and sits BEFORE the status-only arms, which would read that 409 as "an entry with that title already exists" — the opposite fact. ⚠ The 412's own text now names the move and the duplicate risk too.
  - ⚠ **AN APP-ONLY ROUTE ANSWERS `reason=session_required retry=no` (S43).** Both pin routes are `sessionOnly`, so `with-auth.ts` refuses EVERY MCP caller — every one is an OAuth bearer — and `opPin` mapped none of it. `respond.ts › sessionRequired` is cross-cutting by design (the delete routes and `channel-grants` carry the same wrapper option). ⚠ It is not a permission anyone can grant a session, which is why `retry=no`; making the published OP LIST itself honest about the refusal is a separate question, PENDING Samuel (fix-list Q2).
- 🔒 **KB WRITES TAKE AN IDEMPOTENCY KEY, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES A TIMED-OUT WRITE SAFE TO RE-ISSUE (2026-09-18, S53).** `client_write_id` on `op="write_file"` and `op="create_base"`, mirroring the contract `channel_messages.client_msg_id` has carried since `20260725120000`. Before it, a write an agent could not confirm left `force=true` as the only recovery on offer — a blind overwrite aimed by the caller least able to verify the row. **A re-send converges: the probe returns the FIRST write and the result leads with `reason=converged · … · retry=none, it landed`**, which is not an `isError` (the write happened; a retrying client must not retry it) and must SAY the call wrote nothing, or an agent believes its second, different body is stored.
  - 🔒 **AUTHOR-SCOPED, AND THAT IS A VULNERABILITY FIX RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE** — the argument `repository-artifacts.ts › findOwnArtifactByClientId` holds. Scoped to the base alone, idempotency would be a contract with everyone who can write there, and a member reusing another member's key would be handed back THEIR row. The partial unique indexes are `knowledge_entries (knowledge_base_id, client_write_id, client_write_by)` and `knowledge_bases (workspace_id, client_write_id, client_write_by)`, both `WHERE client_write_id IS NOT NULL` (`supabase/migrations/20261014120000_knowledge_client_write_id.sql`, **WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED**). ⚠ **The database agrees with the probe and has to**: scoping only the read turns a convergence into a 23505 the caller sees as a 500 — `createBase` has an explicit race arm re-probing on that code.
  - ⚠ **THE PROBE RUNS BEFORE THE PATH IS RESOLVED**, deliberately: a converging retry must not depend on the path still meaning what it meant, which is exactly what a move between the two calls breaks. ⚠ **A ROW HOLDS ONLY ITS MOST RECENT KEY** — the guarantee protects ONE in-flight call, not the history of the row. ⚠ **`converged` is additive and omitted when false** (§8): an older server sends no such key and absent must read as "this call wrote".
  - ⚠ **THE ONE PUSHED COST OF THE BATCH, AND THE CEILINGS MOVED WITH THE ARGUMENT IN CODE**: `SCHEMA_CEILINGS.dopl_kb` 5,726 → 6,040 and `SERVED_TOTAL_CEILING` → 49,115 (+314 each, all of it `dopl_kb`'s schema — the new param plus `force`'s MOVED refusal). A PARAMETER cannot move into a pulled doctrine, which is why this one is served while eight refusals in the same batch are not. ⚠ **RE-DERIVE, NEVER QUOTE** (`tool-budget.test.ts`, through the real `listTools()`).
- **A MARKDOWN HEADING IS AN ADDRESSABLE UNIT, AND IT IS SPLIT AT READ TIME (Samuel's ruling 2026-09-03).** `dopl_kb` gains `op="outline"` (an entry's `#`/`##`/`###` headings and what each costs to read, with NO body) and `section=` / `offset=` on `op="read_file"`; `write_file` takes `section=` to replace one. **The split is `src/shared/knowledge/markdown-sections.ts` — pure, import-free, and the ONE implementation.** A fenced code block never yields a heading (a runbook full of `# comment` lines would otherwise be all sections), setext headings do, YAML frontmatter is skipped whole, `####` and deeper stay inside their `###` parent, and every offset indexes the ORIGINAL body — CRLF and missing trailing newlines included. **No migration: nothing about a section is stored.**
  - 🔒 **A SECTION WRITE PRESERVES THE BLANK LINE UNDER THE HEADING (2026-09-18, S29).** The heading line and the gap below it are the DOCUMENT's formatting, not the section's content, and `replaceSection` stopped at the heading's EOL — so every write that kept its heading ate the blank line and glued the new prose to the `##`. It re-rendered a document the author had not written, once per edit, with nothing on the result saying so. The gap is measured from the ORIGINAL body and re-emitted VERBATIM (CRLF and a two-line gap both survive; rebuilding it as `"\n"` would reformat an entry nobody asked to reformat). ⚠ **NOT ADDED WHEN THE CALLER SUPPLIED ONE** — content that already opens on a blank line, and content that brings its own heading back, are the caller's shape; doubling it would grow the entry once per write. **Idempotent, and pinned as such.**
  - 🔒 **THE SPLIT RUNS SERVER-SIDE, WHICH IS THE ONE PLACE THIS DEPARTS FROM `response-size.ts`'s RULE.** Those three knobs (`response_format`, `fields`, `max_chars`) are applied in the RENDERER because they PROJECT a payload the loopback already paid for. A `section` SELECTS which part of a document to fetch, the way `path` selects a document — so it is a query parameter (`GET .../files?path=&section=&outline=1`), and the body that never matched never crosses the wire. ⚠ The practical half of the same argument: **`packages/mcp-server` cannot import `src/`** (tsconfig `rootDir`), so a renderer-side split would have meant a hand-copied markdown parser — a second opinion about what a heading is. `offset` DID stay in the renderer, because it is a window over a payload already fetched, exactly like `max_chars`.
  - ⚠ **AN UNKNOWN HEADING IS A 200 CARRYING THE OUTLINE, NEVER A 404**, and the MCP result is `ok` rather than `isError`: the entry resolved and the heading did not, so the retry needs no second call and a client that retries on error would retry a call that can only answer the same way. **An AMBIGUOUS heading refuses on the WRITE path** (409 `KNOWLEDGE_SECTION_AMBIGUOUS`, both line numbers in `details`) because picking the first would overwrite a section nobody named and there is no trash to recover it from.
  - 🔒 **THE WRITE HALF IS A NUDGE FOR A PERSON AND, FOR AN AGENT, TWO REFUSALS AND TWO NUDGES — AND THIS BULLET SAID "A NUDGE AND MAY NEVER BECOME A REFUSAL" UNTIL 2026-09-18, WHEN SAMUEL RULED THE OTHER WAY** (fix-list Q1, option A: *"are you saying that saves should be blocked if there's no description? I think I agree with A"*). What changed is the EVIDENCE, not the taste: Wave 4 measured a base that had been nudged eight times and still cost 18,000 characters read to extract 900, and the trial's only reproducible wrong turn came from one-word excerpts. **An AGENT save through `dopl_kb(op="write_file")` is REFUSED, before anything is written, when (a) the entry would end up with no real summary — absent, one word, or a restatement of the title — or (b) a WHOLE-BODY write is over `src/shared/knowledge/caps.ts › KB_SECTION_NUDGE_CHARS` (1,500) with no `##` at all.** Rules and refusals are `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/knowledge-write-rules.ts`; each refusal is one line in the surface's own `reason=` / `retry=` shape and names exactly what to add. ⚠ **A HUMAN TYPING IN THE APP IS NEVER BLOCKED** — that half of the ruling is the editor's, and nothing in `packages/mcp-server` can reach a person, which is why the refusals live on the agent surface and nowhere else.
    - ⚠ **THE `section=` PATH STILL NUDGES, AND THAT IS NOT A LOOPHOLE.** With `section=`, `body` is one section's new content and the real body is the SERVER's merge of it — a document the MCP process never sees — so a pre-write length test would measure the wrong thing. That path keeps `knowledge-sections.ts › unsectionedNudge`, measured on what actually landed, and a caller passing `section=` has by construction addressed a heading.
    - ⚠ **AN OMITTED `excerpt` PRESERVES THE STORED ONE**, so the rule is tested against the value the entry will HAVE, not the argument: when `excerpt` is absent `opWriteFile` reads the row first (one extra round trip, and only on the omission — the behaviour the rule exists to discourage). 🔒 **THE PROBE FAILS OPEN**: a 404 is a create and the refusal stands, and any other failure means "unknown", where blocking a user's content on our own transport error is the worse error. A rule this process could not measure is not a rule it may assert.
    - ⚠ **THE TWO NUDGED RULES ARE POINTERS AND SUPERSESSION**, both on a write that LANDED. A body carrying "see the…" / "documented elsewhere" / "not reproduced here" / "follows the" and naming no `base/path` anywhere gets `reason=POINTER_WITHOUT_TARGET` (Wave 4: hit all four runs; one agent recovered by explicit luck). A body whose supersession marker sits below its FIRST line gets `reason=SUPERSESSION_BURIED` — position is the whole rule, because the marker is what let both Poor agents skip the decoy with no metadata help at all. **Every write result still ends with a one-line outline** (` · `-joined, ~200 chars) so the next read has the addresses without a call.
    - 🔒 **THE TWO AUDIENCES ASK ONE QUESTION AND THE PREDICATE IS ONE IMPLEMENTATION, HAND-COPIED AND PINNED BYTE-FOR-BYTE** (`src/shared/knowledge/write-rules.ts`, copy at `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/knowledge-write-predicates.ts`, join in `src/shared/knowledge/write-rules.test.ts` — the same boundary and the same construction as `./caps.ts` and its test, because `packages/mcp-server` cannot import `src/`). **A person warned about a page an agent would have been refused for is two rules wearing one ruling**, so the pin is byte-for-byte over a marked region rather than an expression check: a cap is one number a reader can compare by eye, a predicate is three branches and a regex. ⚠ **THE WORDING IS DELIBERATELY NOT SHARED** — the agent gets `reason=` / `retry=` naming what to add, the person gets a label. ⚠ **THE HEADING DETECTOR IS A SECOND OPINION AND IS TUNED TO FALSE NEGATIVES**: `markdown-sections.ts` is unreachable from the package, so the shared regex reads a code-fence `#` AS a heading — the write goes through and no warning shows, because the opposite error nags about a body that really is sectioned.
    - **THE HUMAN HALF IS IN THE ONE KB ENTRY EDITOR, WHICH BOTH KNOWLEDGE SURFACES SHARE** — `knowledge/components/doc-pane.tsx`, reached by the web channels-v2 workspace pages and by the desktop Home pane through the same `knowledge-v2` detail view, so there is no second editor to keep in step. The labels are derived and worded in `doc-pane-chrome.tsx › writeRuleLabels` ("No summary", "Long page, no headings") and rendered by `› WriteRuleWarnings` in the Overview header row beside the save indicator: **label only, `role="note"`, no explainer, no control, no dismiss** (Samuel's minimal-UI ruling), on the `text-caption text-warning` + `AlertTriangle` recipe this feature already uses. ⚠ **IT READS THE DRAFT, WHICH IS WHAT "at save time" MEANS ON AN AUTOSAVING EDITOR** — there is no Save button, and `title`/`description`/`body` ARE the next write's payload. ⚠ **A BODYLESS ENTRY IS SILENT**, or every new page would greet its author with a complaint about itself. ⚠ **"NEVER BLOCKED" IS A PROPERTY OF WHERE THE VALUE IS USED**, so `doc-pane-chrome.test.tsx` pins the label list at exactly ONE consumer — the render.
  - 🔒 **`get_tree` AND `read_file` CARRY THE HEADING LIST SINCE 2026-09-18 (Wave 4 a1), AND THIS BULLET SAID THEY WERE UNCHANGED.** It read *"a `sections=N` COLUMN WAS MEASURED AND NOT BUILT"* and priced the body fetch (~1 MB against ~80 kB of metadata) against *"~12 rendered characters a row"*. ⚠ **THE PRICE WAS RIGHT AND THE BENEFIT WAS UNDERCOUNTED**: Wave 4 measured heading names as the TOP ASK in three of four runs — three spent calls guessing them, and one spent three `outline` calls whose only purpose was learning names it should already have been handed. What ships is neither of the two shapes that bullet weighed: **no stored column** (its drift seam stands — SQL and the TS parser would have to agree about code fences) and **no unconditional fetch**. `service-folders.ts › getBaseTree` takes a `headings` FLAG; `GET .../tree?headings=1` sets it, it is the only thing that turns `includeBody: false` off, **the bodies are dropped before the snapshot returns**, and the names ride their own `entryHeadings` key so `entries` keeps the shape `scripts/check-knowledge-type-drift.ts` pins. **The app's tree pane does not send it; the agent surface always does** — paged at 400, called rarely. ⚠ **THE SAME TRADE, INVERTED, ON `read_file`**: `?headings=1` keeps the WHOLE body and adds the outline beside it, where `?outline=1` returns the map INSTEAD of the document. Both are opt-in and additive, so a client that sends neither gets byte-for-byte what it always got (§8). ⚠ **AND `read_file` NOW SAYS WHEN THERE ARE NONE** — *"No headings; 3,299 chars whole"* with the paging knobs named (S32 / Wave 4 a4) — **but only when the payload carried an outline**: no outline is a server that did not MEASURE, and "no headings" would be a claim about the document rather than about the response.
  - 🔒 **A CURATED EXCERPT IS BODY-CLASS CONTENT, FENCED — NOT A NEUTRALIZED VALUE (2026-09-18, S36 / Wave 4 a3+b2).** `knowledge-ops-read.ts › descSuffix` ran `narration.ts › inlineOr`, which clipped at `INLINE_TEXT_MAX` (160) **mid-clause** and **stripped backticks**; Wave 4 recorded both as routing failures — an excerpt quoted dying at `"...the $5..."` before naming its heading, and the authoring rule *"quote the heading name in backticks"* that the renderer made unfollowable. It now renders the field's own 300 (`DESCRIPTION_MAX`), markdown intact, clipped at the last clause boundary in the budget. ⚠ **`INLINE_TEXT_MAX` WAS NOT RAISED AND MUST NOT BE** — it guards every name, label and error echo on the surface, none of which is curated; what changed is the CLASS of this one value. ⚠ **THE FENCE IS WHAT PAYS FOR IT**: `untrusted-fence.ts › fenceLines` wraps the whole ROW BLOCK of `get_tree` / `list_dir` in one `<body_HEX>` per response, and this server's own narration — the header, the paging notice, the scope line — stays OUTSIDE it. One header per response, never per row. ⚠ **NEWLINES ARE STILL FLATTENED**: a row is a LINE, and a fence says where a BLOCK ends, never where a row does.
  - 🔒 **A SEARCH HIT CARRIES THE ADDRESS A READ ACTUALLY TAKES, AND `dopl_search` DISCLOSES ITS RECALL CAP (2026-09-18, S15/S49).** `SearchHit` gains `baseSlug` and `path` (`folder/sub/Title`), derived from rows `searchKnowledgeEntries` already read — one folder list per DISTINCT base in the result set, never per hit — so a hit stops ending one lookup short of `read_file(base, path)`. ⚠ Both keys are absent from an older server's payload and every renderer treats them so (§8); the entry id stays on the row as the durable handle. ⚠ **THE CAP RIDES `search.ts › scopeNote`, NOT THE DESCRIPTION** — `dopl_search` is held to `READ_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS` (450), the tightest budget on the surface, and a per-call footer is in no served total at all. `dopl_kb`'s own search has disclosed it for months (`knowledge-ops-search.ts › SEARCH_SCOPE_NOTE`); this one never did, so *"2 matches"* read as a census. The `concise` footer keeps it in one clause, because `concise` drops what the DESCRIPTION carries and the description cannot afford to carry this. ⚠ **ONE PER-SCOPE READ SINCE 2026-09-23 (P8-10)**: `snippet`, `entryAddress`, `more`, `SEARCH_GROUP_COUNT` and the per-scope read itself live in `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/search-scope.ts › searchScope`, which BOTH `dopl_search` paths use — so the everywhere legs now carry the entry address, the capped-group counts and the ontology clip note too (they did not). Identity hits render `seen by <audience>` (`agent-shared.ts › identityAudience`), never the raw visibility column.
  - 🚫 **TWO THINGS WERE LEFT ALONE, EXPLICITLY (Wave 4 a5/a7).** The missed-section fallback still answers with the OUTLINE for ~600 characters — all three agents who hit it praised it — and **the outline-before-read nudge was NOT strengthened**: both Good agents skipped `outline` CORRECTLY once the excerpt named the heading, so a stronger nudge would have bought a call per question. The fix was to make the data support the skip, not to instruct harder.
  - ⚠ **`op="search"` ALREADY RETURNED SNIPPETS AND STILL DOES** — verified 2026-09-03, unchanged. `search_knowledge_hybrid` builds them in SQL: a keyword hit is `ts_headline(… MaxWords=20, MaxFragments=2)` and a semantic hit is `left(<nearest chunk> || body, 240)`, so a hit is ~240–250 characters and a body has never reached the wire. Nothing was capped because nothing needed capping.
  - ⚠ **THE BUDGETS ROSE AND ARE RECORDED WHERE THEY ARE TAKEN** (`tool-budget.test.ts`): `dopl_kb` description 1,937 → 1,986 (one op, two routing sentences, after a trim of 233 in the same string), its schema 5,138 → 5,707 (`section`, `offset`, one op name), the served total 46,846 → 47,464, and `DOCTRINE_CEILING` 8,960 → 9,446 → 9,923 for the new `dopl://doctrine/knowledge` (477 chars, budgeted on its own by `knowledge-doctrine-budget.test.ts`). **Every one of those is per CONNECTION and the saving is per READ**: a 2,559-char sectioned entry renders whole at 2,760 characters, its outline at 319 and one section at 839.
  - ⚠ **AND THEY ROSE AGAIN ON 2026-09-18, ON THE PULLED SIDE ONLY.** `knowledge-doctrine.ts` 500 → 744 measured (`knowledge-doctrine-budget.test.ts › KNOWLEDGE_DOCTRINE_MAX` 500 → 750) and `tool-budget.test.ts › DOCTRINE_CEILING` 12,120 → 12,387, for the four write rules — two of which now REFUSE. 🔒 **A BLOCKING RULE AN AGENT CAN ONLY LEARN FROM THE BLOCK COSTS A WRITE TO DISCOVER**, which is why it had to be readable in advance. ⚠ **IT COULD NOT HAVE GONE PUSHED**: `dopl_kb` measures ~1,888 against `tool-style.ts › HARD_DESCRIPTION_CEILING` (2,000), which THROWS AT IMPORT — the same characters on that side would not boot the server. The refusal TEXT is per-call (`write-result-budget.test.ts`) and is in no served total. **Nothing pushed moved in this change; re-derive every number rather than quoting these.**

Why/history: ENGINEERING.md §7 (MCP surface hardening), §8 (MCP narration, MCP identity, F-100/F-104/F-145), and the 2026-09-03 entry on headings as addresses.

## 11. Desktop session rules

### 11.-1 Where an OPEN lands (2026-09-09)

- 🔒 **AN EXPLICIT "OPEN THE APP" PUTS THE WINDOW BACK ON `/`, WHICH IS THE LAUNCH DECISION** (`main/shell-mode.js › openMainWindow`). Three doors go through it and only three: `second-instance` (when the second launch carries NO deep link), the tray's **Open Dopl**, and macOS `activate` (the dock icon) — all wired in `main/index.js`. It reveals the window and, **only when one already existed**, pushes `/`; a window main had to BUILD is already loading the index at `/`, and a route pushed at a renderer that has not subscribed yet is dropped on the floor (`main/deep-link.js › pushRoute` carries that trap in full).
- ⚠ **A DEEP LINK AND A CLICKED CHANNEL NOTIFICATION MUST NOT GO THROUGH IT.** Both reveal the window too, and both NAME a destination — routing them to `/` first is a race their own push would have to win. They call `showMainWindow` / `navigateToChannels` directly, and `second-instance` returns early when the argv carries a `dopl://` link.
- **WHY IT EXISTS.** Samuel, 2026-09-09: *"every time i go to the desktop app/open it, it auto has it on my original workspace. The user should be auto at the Home space."* A COLD process launch already landed on `/home` — `spa-window.js` loads the index with no hash, the hash router resolves `/` to `pages/boot`, and boot navigates to `/home` for a `kind='personal'` boot answer (`c37e4942`, §4A). **Nothing persists a route on either side**: main stores none, and the SPA's IndexedDB query cache cannot drive the navigation (boot is `refetchOnMount: "always"` and gates on `isFetchedAfterMount`). What was NOT a cold launch is the common case — Dopl lives in the tray, so every "open" revealed the SAME window on the workspace route it was left on.

### 11.0 The runtime seam (2026-08-31 — the adapter port, behaviour-preserving half)

- 🔒 **"BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING" IS THE CLAIM. "BYTE-IDENTICAL" IS NOT, AND WAS RETRACTED 2026-09-01.** An independent review diffed the four moved sites against `git show HEAD:` and found the Claude lane observably different from HEAD. **The correct sentence for this whole section is: behaviour-preserving, with SEVEN declared observable differences and THREE narration changes** — enumerated in 11.0g, which is the list to read before assuming an existing Claude session behaves as it did. ⚠ **THE PHRASE MATTERED BECAUSE IT WAS LOAD-BEARING**: "byte-identical" is the reason a reviewer skips re-testing the Claude lane, and it was asserted in a file header (`runtime/claude/launch-spec.js`) that is itself one of the drifted files. ⚠ **WHAT REALLY WAS PRESERVED IS MOST OF THE SURFACE AND IT WAS VERIFIED**: `grantDecision`'s order, verdicts, reason codes and all five Axis-B lanes; `buildSessionToolConfig`'s three profile branches; `main/session-outbound-tag.js` byte-unchanged (`git diff` empty); `triageOptions`' whole body; the `result`-then-`context` ordering; the subagent skip; and the delta clamps. **The drift is in the SEAMS AROUND the moved code, plus two features that rode inside a change described as a move.**
- 🔒 **CORE MAY NOT NAME A RUNTIME. `dopl-desktop-app/main/runtime/` IS THE ONLY PLACE AN ADAPTER IS NAMED, AND `main/runtime/index.js` IS THE ONLY DOOR.** Core asks it for a frozen `descriptor` (pure data) or for one of the methods in `main/runtime/contract.js › RUNTIME_METHODS` (SEVENTEEN @ 2026-09-23, since `rosterKey` and `modelArg` joined — re-count the object, never this number), and nothing else. ⚠ **This is `main/`'s FIRST SUBDIRECTORY** — **143** flat modules beside it @ 2026-09-01 (`ls dopl-desktop-app/main/*.js | wc -l`), against **137** at the last commit (`git show HEAD:dopl-desktop-app/main | grep -c '\.js$'`). ⚠ **THIS SAID "it said 139 before" AND THAT NUMBER NEVER EXISTED IN A COMMITTED STATE** (corrected 2026-09-01): the wave is uncommitted, so the only two measurable states are 137 at HEAD and 143 in the working tree. **Re-measure both; a delta quoted from memory is how a count becomes fiction.** Core keeps the flat convention. **Every file under `main/runtime/**` must be `.js`**: the 500-line cap's glob is `main/**/*.js`, so a `.mjs`/`.ts` file there would match NO eslint block and be UNCAPPED, in the one tree whose stated invariant is that the cap has no exemptions (`test/eslint-config-coverage.test.mjs` walks it).
- **What MOVED to the adapter, and the one test that keeps it there.** `test/core-vocabulary.test.mjs` scans core's CODE LINES (comments are allowed — this repo's comments carry the argument) for `claude` / `anthropic` / `codex` / Cursor's vendor spellings / `sdk.query` / `canUseTool` / `permissionMode` / `app-server`. It carries a DATED `DEFERRED` census naming the files whose extraction belongs to a later step, and **every row must still have a hit**, so the list shrinks and can never grow quietly.
  | Was | Is | Why it could not stay |

See 11.0b |
