- **What STAYED, and it is most of the system.** `grantDecision`'s ORDER, the four verdicts, the 23 reason codes, `UNIVERSAL_HARD_DENY`, every Axis-B lane, `floorWindowlessMessage`, the private-turn withdrawal, the grant keys, the reducer, the state machine, the effect table, the timers, the store, targeting, the wake tiers, the narration ring and the whole listener spine. **`mcp__dopl__*` names are runtime-independent** and live in `main/session-dopl-tools.js` (§2 split, so both sides of the seam read them without a cycle); each adapter's `tools.js` COMPOSES them rather than re-deriving them.
- ⚠ **`main/runtime/index.js` IS ELECTRON-FREE AT LOAD, BY CONTRACT** — and **the mechanism is `claude/index.js`'s THREE LAZY REQUIRES, not a discipline the leaf files keep.** `session-profiles.js` is a PURE module two suites slice and evaluate standalone, and it asks the registry for every gate decision, so `runtime/claude/index.js` defers `./loader`, `./launch-spec` and `./normalize` behind arrow functions (`const platform = () => require('./loader')`, and the two beside it). **The leaves themselves require core at TOP LEVEL**: `claude/normalize.js` requires `../../session-io`, `claude/launch-spec.js` requires `../../session-auth`. ⚠ **THIS SAID THE OPPOSITE UNTIL 2026-09-01 — "`normalize.js` / `launch-spec.js` / `axis-b.js` lazy-require anything that reaches back through `session-io` or `session-auth`" — and TWO OF THE FOUR DO THE REVERSE.** The OUTCOME was true; the stated mechanism was not, and that is the dangerous kind of wrong doc: **an edit making `claude/index.js` eager would break the invariant while every file still satisfied the old sentence.** => require('../../session-auth')` — which is presumably where the generalisation came from.) **A top-level require of `runtime/claude/index.js`'s deferred three closes a cycle and hands the gate a half-initialised module at exactly the moment it asks for a deny list.**
- **A session is STAMPED with its runtime at spawn (`s.runtimeId`, `session-engine.js › startSession`) and never re-reads it.** The conversation handle, the tool vocabulary and the Axis-A modes all belong to ONE runtime, so a park or crash resume must not land on another. **An unknown id resolves to the DEFAULT rather than refusing** — a different kind of fail-closed from a gate's: an unknown id is a record written by a build that knew a runtime this one does not, and refusing would strand the session with no way to end it. Nothing is GRANTED by it; every posture and profile is re-derived per call.
- 🔒 **FOUR DECLARATIONS REFUSE INSTEAD OF HIDING** (`main/runtime/contract.js › LAUNCH_BLOCKING`, driven by `test/runtime-contract.test.mjs` + `test/session-engine-slot.test.mjs`, which assert BOTH that the shipped descriptors satisfy each and that one which does not is really rejected). Everywhere else `null` means HIDE the control, never gray it. ⚠ **AND THE FOUR REFUSE FOUR DIFFERENT-SIZED THINGS, EACH ENFORCED WHERE THAT THING HAPPENS** — read the verb in each bullet, because "launch-blocking" is the family name, not the mechanism.
  - **`axisB.enforcementPoint: null` ⇒ the adapter does not register.** Axis B needs an in-process tool boundary OR a held callback and there is nothing else: the Dopl MCP server is remote HTTP (`runtime/claude/loader.js › buildMcpServers`), so main is not in the call path of a channel call, and **no posture field crosses the wire**, so the server cannot refuse the post either. With neither, an agent posts with **no outbound consent card at all** — the gate coming off, not a capability degraded.
  - **`containment.profiles.<p>.denyList: null` ⇒ THE ADAPTER DOES NOT REGISTER.** ⚠ **THIS SAID "that profile is refused at LAUNCH" UNTIL 2026-09-01 AND IT IS WRONG — confirmed by mutation.** The check is in `contract.js › descriptorProblems`, which `sealAdapter` THROWS on at module load; the launch-time predicate that used to shadow it (`canLaunchProfile`) was deleted 2026-09-23 (RC-08), so `descriptorProblems` is the only enforcement. (§11.0e states it correctly; `contract.js`'s own comment made the same error and was corrected in the same change.) `grantDecision` step 1 reads the list as the gate's OWN first check — the verdict no task grant and no widest mode can open — so a restricted profile with no list in that runtime's vocabulary has NO enforcement at all. A native sandbox bounds the filesystem; it does not deny the delegation, exfil and persistence built-ins those lists exist for. **This is the one place absent does not mean hide, because the control here IS containment.**
    - 🔒 **AN EMPTY LIST IS REFUSED THE SAME WAY, ON EVERY PROFILE BUT `full` (2026-09-01).** `denyList: []` SAYS "this profile denies nothing", which is the identical condition — the gate's first check with nothing to check — and both checks asked only `Array.isArray`, so it registered cleanly. `full` is exempt because its supervision IS Axis A rather than a list (`contract.js › UNRESTRICTED_PROFILE`); every other profile exists *because* it denies something.
    - 🔒 **AND `sealAdapter` NOW READS THE ENFORCED STRUCTURE, NOT ONLY THE DECLARATION** (`contract.js › mirrorProblems`). `grantDecision` step 1 has always read `runtime.toolConfigFor(p).disallowedTools` — the runtime METHOD — and NEVER `descriptor.containment.profiles.<p>.denyList`. **The descriptor field is a MIRROR**, so every rule above validated a mirror of the thing it claims to protect: an adapter hand-writing a plausible descriptor over a `toolConfigFor` that returns `[]` sealed cleanly, the launch-time predicate called the profile enforced, the UI rendered containment, and the gate denied nothing. **MEASURED: hardcoding `denyList: []` across every Claude profile failed 0 of 2786 tests; emptying the ENFORCEMENT list fired 16 pins.** All three shipped adapters DERIVE the mirror (`index.js › profileEntry`: `denyList: cfg.disallowedTools.slice()`) — the seal now asserts that derivation as a SET comparison rather than trusting it.
  - **`session.usageResetsOnResume: 'unverified'` ⇒ RESUME is refused (`capability.js › canResume` / `› resumeRefusal`); a cold launch is unaffected.** `session-park.js › resumeParked` zeroes both delta baselines; a runtime that CONTINUES the cumulative total makes every delta negative and `session-io.js › applyCoreEvents` clamps it to 0 — the spend meter silently under-reports. (There is no turn/cost cap any more; the argument is about the meter.) Codex declares `false` (measured: it continues), so it resumes (re-read 2026-09-23).
  - 🔒 **`toolMode.windowlessFloor: null` ⇒ THE WINDOWLESS LAUNCH IS REFUSED (added 2026-09-01).** A windowless session has NO GATE SURFACE — `session-windowless.js › claimGate` answers a permission request with a DENY — so Axis A must be floored to a mode that allows the reads the prompt ORDERS the agent to make. With no floor there is nothing to raise to and the session runs at its STORED mode, which STARTS at the narrowest member and RESETS to it on park: **every tool call denied, silently, with the agent reporting it cannot read files it was told to read.** ⚠ **THE RULE WAS WRITTEN IN `capability.js › floorWindowlessTool`'S HEADER FROM THE START AND NOTHING REFUSED IT** — the predicate returned the session's own un-floored mode instead. It now answers `null`, `› windowlessFloorRefusal` carries the sentence, and `session-launch.js › launch` refuses AFTER `acquireRuntime` and BEFORE `startSession`, so nothing is registered and there is no rollback. ⚠ **A FLOOR NAMED BUT ABSENT FROM `toolMode.options` REFUSES IDENTICALLY** — neither is orderable, and picking for either is the guess this refuses. ⚠ **THE REFUSAL RIDES `{skipped:'disabled'}`, NOT A NEW WIRE WORD**: `launch-directive-vocab.js › REFUSAL_REASONS` is the same closed set as `schema-launch-modes.ts › LAUNCH_REFUSAL_REASONS` and the column CHECK (eleven words @ 2026-09-23), so minting one here would be a refusal the database refuses to record. The specific sentence rides the diag, which is the only surface allowed to name a runtime.
- ⚠ **AND ONE DECLARATION *WARNS* RATHER THAN REFUSING: `axisB.opScoped` (2026-09-01).** `false` or `'unverified'` collapses Axis B from op-scoped to whole-tool — every channel call gates, READS INCLUDED. **It is a WARNING because the direction of failure is CLOSED and that was traced end to end:** input the gate cannot read fails `› postFieldsOk`, `grantDecision` answers `'gate'`, and a windowless gate DENIES. The agent is broken; the boundary is not. `capability.js › axisBOpScopedWarning` is the sentence and `session-launch.js` logs it at the spawn. ⚠ **THE PREDICATE HAD ZERO CONSUMERS UNTIL THIS** — declared, documented in the strongest terms, and read by nothing in `main/` or `src/`, so the operator got no warning and the launch was not refused. All three shipped adapters declare `opScoped: true` (re-read 2026-09-23), so it fires on no shipped runtime today.
- ⚠ **AND THE LIVE-MODEL-SWITCH DECLARATION NOW REFUSES SOMETHING (2026-09-21, U10 — F-753).** `main/runtime/runtime-copy.js › liveModelSwitchRefusal` ASKS `capability.js › canSwitchModelLive` (one reading of `descriptor.session.liveModelSwitch`, since 2026-09-22), and `main/session-reopen.js › setModelByTask` is what calls it. ⚠ **IT REFUSES A CONTROL, NOT A LAUNCH** — the boundary `interruptRefusal` draws; a runtime that cannot hot-swap a model is perfectly launchable on any model it offers. **What it closed is a RECORDED SWITCH THAT NEVER HAPPENED**: the `setModel` call was guarded by a `typeof` test, so on a runtime whose live handle has no model verb nothing was applied and the function still stamped `s.model` and answered `{ok:true}` — the value the NEXT assembly reads, so the session came back on a model the operator had been told it was already using, wearing one runtime's ALIAS on another runtime's session. ⚠ **REFUSED WITH A SENTENCE, NEVER SILENTLY**, and `'unverified'` and `false` are worded apart because the operator can act on the difference. ⚠ **A LIVE HANDLE WHOSE QUERY HAS NO `setModel` IS A SECOND REFUSAL RATHER THAN A NO-OP** — the declaration is the runtime's promise, and the handle in hand is allowed to disagree with it. ⚠ A session with NO query at all (spawn-idle or parked) is untouched: nothing is running to disagree, and the recorded pick is what its first turn will spend.

#### 11.0a The normalizer is the seam, and it owns ALL THREE raw-message consumers

- The consume loop called **three** things on every platform message and each read the platform's schema directly: the auth-sentinel hold (which SHORT-CIRCUITS the loop), the render mapping, and the per-message usage watcher. It now calls **one**: `rt.normalize(msg, ctx)` → `CoreEvent[]`, applied by `session-io.js › applyCoreEvents`. **A boundary owning only the render mapping would have left two platform-shaped parsers in core and made the golden fixtures cover a third of the surface.**
- ⚠ **`normalize` IS PURE — no I/O, no dispatch, no session mutation.** That is what makes a later adapter testable from a recorded transcript with nothing installed, which is the only honest answer to "no live installs". So the state it used to write travels on events and CORE writes it: the conversation handle and the durable record on `launched`; the **cumulative** cost/token totals on `result`, with the DELTA arithmetic staying in core beside the resume baselines it is the twin of; and the meter's last reading as a `context` event, which core REMEMBERS on the session and never dispatches (`session-io.js › applyCoreEvents` → `s.promptTokens` / `s.promptWindow` / `s.liveModel`; P4-11, 2026-09-23 — the turn-end context dispatch and its swallowed-failure line are deleted). `session-metrics.js › metrics` is the one reader. ⚠ **`result`'s `sessionTokens` is `null` for a turn with NO measurement, never `0`** (`runtime/events.js › result`), and core then moves neither `tokensSpent` nor `lastTotalTokens` — the turn is still counted and dispatched; a zero there re-billed the whole running total on the next turn (CX-02/P4-04).
- **The event vocabulary is the reducer's, unchanged** (`main/runtime/events.js`). Not one of its names is a vendor's; the reducer was platform-neutral all along and only looked coupled because the thing producing the events read SDK messages directly.
- A REJECTION goes through the same normalizer as a message, as a synthetic `{type:'error', text}` (`runtime/events.js › ERROR_FRAME` is the shared spelling): **the runtime decides what is auth-shaped**, because a rejection string is as platform-specific as a message. The hold BOOKKEEPING (`session-auth.js › holdIfAuthFailure`, `resumeAfterSignIn`, the release path) is core, and 🔒 **it TRUSTS the adapter's `auth_hold` verdict and never re-tests the text** (P4-03, 2026-09-23 — core re-running Claude's regexes dropped or mis-filed six of seven Codex auth messages). The consume loop (`session-query.js`) hands it only an `auth_hold` event or an `auth_hold` its normalizer made from a rejection; core no longer requires `main/session-auth-detect.js`, whose regexes remain for the Claude normalizer and the operator copy. `holdIfAuthMessage` is deleted (no production caller).

#### 11.0b Axis A is the runtime's; Axis B is Dopl's — and the split IS the argument

- **Axis A's modes and lists are one runtime's built-in tool vocabulary.** A runtime storing Axis A as its own words would resolve every call to the most restrictive mode → `false` → `gate` → and, on a windowless session, **DENY**. So `descriptor.toolMode.options` declares the modes **narrowest FIRST** — `[0]` is where every unknown value fail-closes and the LAST entry is the widest, which is how the windowless floor stays widen-only and how "is this tool classified at all" is asked without core holding a copy of any list (`session-profiles.js › isClassifiedTool`).
- **Axis B did NOT move.** `ask | auto_inbound | auto_outbound | auto_both` names no platform tool and no platform mode. **So the two windowless floors are now in different files, and that asymmetry is the point:** `floorWindowlessMessage` stays in `session-profiles.js` (it moves between members of an enum every runtime shares) while `floorWindowlessTool` is `descriptor.toolMode.windowlessFloor`, applied by `main/runtime/capability.js › floorWindowlessTool`. **Each half still carries the other's argument in prose** — pinned by `test/session-tool-floor.test.mjs`, which asserts the cross-reference rather than the old adjacency.
- 🔒 **AXIS A IS IN THE SESSION RUNTIME'S OWN WORDS, END TO END (Samuel's ruling 2, 2026-09-23: *"Each runtime's own words"*; X-01).** `session-engine.js › startSession` copies the launch runtime's Axis-A list (narrowest first; `session-profiles.js › toolModesFor(runtimeId)`) into `state.toolModes`, and `session-boot.js › parkedSessionFromRecord` does the same from `rec.runtimeId`. `session-state.js › initialSessionState` and the reducer's `set_tool_mode` arm coerce against THAT list (`› toolModesOf`), so a Codex session keeps `never` / `on-request` / `granular` / `untrusted` and `runtime/codex/launch-spec.js › nativePair` really sends the deliberate `never` → `granular` policy. A word from another runtime resolves to THIS runtime's narrowest, never a translation. `session-state.js › TOOL_MODES` is only the fallback for a caller that names no runtime. The same words ride every lane: the Settings record (`byRuntime[id].tools`), the live picker (`sessions:setMode`), the summaries wire (`DesktopSessionSummary.toolMode` is `string | null`), the directive wire and its column CHECKs (the UNION of every registered runtime's words, validated against the RESOLVED runtime — §11 directive lane, §12 `20261020120000`) and MCP (`dopl_channel` `posture.tools` lists the words per runtime). Pinned engine-level through `initialSessionState` (no hand-built state).
  - The auth hold resets both STAMPED axes to the session runtime's narrowest word (`› toolModesOf(state)[0]`) and `ask` (`session-reducer.js`'s `auth_hold` arm); a per-agent pick survives it. (The park's "Tools and Messages reset to Manual / Ask" notice and the `modes` echo had no receiver and were deleted 2026-09-23.)
  - `session-grant-keys.js › makeGrantKeyFor` takes `editToolsFor`, and `grantKeyFor(toolName, input, channelId, runtimeId)` asks the SESSION runtime's edit-scoped names (`session-profiles.js` / `session-gate-reason.js` pass `a.runtime`, `session-gate-bridge.js` passes `s.runtimeId`) — never the default runtime's list read at load.
- **`grantDecision` gained ONE argument and it decides nothing.** `a.runtime` names WHICH vocabulary steps 1 and 4 are asked in; the order, the verdicts and every Axis-B lane are identical on every runtime, and absent resolves to the default.
- **The SPA/desktop posture parity pin now has TWO winners.** `settings-agent-posture.test.tsx` reads Axis A off `runtime/claude/index.js › descriptor.toolMode` and Axis B off `session-profiles.js`, and derives the declaring files **per axis**. The invariant is unchanged and is not about literals: **the SPA must never offer a mode the desktop would coerce away**, because such a mode is written, acknowledged, re-rendered as the operator's choice, and applied as the most restrictive value on every launch.

#### 11.0c The vendor is a SECOND header dimension, never a fourth runtime value

- 🔒 **`X-Dopl-Runtime` IS CUSTODY; `X-Dopl-Vendor` IS VENDOR.** A Dopl-driven Codex or Cursor session is still a session the desktop app spawned, so it stamps `desktop-session` like every other. ⚠ **Three live sites read the custody word by strict equality or array membership** — `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/identity.ts › runtimeWord`, `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/channel-wake-guidance.ts`, `dopl-desktop-app/main/targeting.js › DESKTOP_RUNTIMES` — so **adding a vendor word there would not widen the set; it would drop every non-Claude session OUT of it**, silently changing the wake guidance those sessions are taught and whether a requester window opens.
- `src/shared/auth/runtime-header.ts` owns both readers (`readVendorHeader` / `narrowVendor`, recognized values only, exact match). ⚠ **THE MCP SERVER HAS ONE VENDOR READER, AND IT IS PRESENTATION ONLY (2026-09-23, P8-03/X-09):** `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/identity.ts › toolLoaderFor` names the caller's own deferred-tool loader in pushed text (Claude `ToolSearch`, Codex `tool_search`, unknown/Cursor "your client's tool search"); nothing gates on the vendor. The mcp-server copy keeps `CLAUDE_VENDOR` / `CODEX_VENDOR` only. **Absent stays absent** — an older desktop build stamps custody and no vendor, and reading `desktop-session` as "therefore Claude" is the conflation the second header exists to prevent. `dopl-desktop-app/test/runtime-stamp-literals.test.mjs` pins both literals against the server's constants across a join with no shared module, and asserts the custody enum did not grow a vendor word; `channel-wake-runtime.test.ts` carries the regression that a non-Claude desktop session still lands in the desktop branch.

#### 11.0d The SECOND adapter (2026-08-31) — `main/runtime/codex/`, and what it declares it cannot do

- **It cost one `register(require('./codex'))` line in `main/runtime/index.js` and a directory.** No core module gained a branch, and every case in `test/runtime-contract.test.mjs` applied to it at registration. **`registry.ids()` → `['claude','codex','cursor']` @ 2026-09-01** (⚠ this read `['claude','codex']` until then — the THIRD adapter landed in the same wave; §11.0e carries the measurement command). **Registration ORDER is load-bearing** — `DEFAULT_ID` is the first registered, so a session record carrying no runtime id still resolves to the runtime it ran on.
- **The target is `codex app-server` over stdio, not the SDK and not `codex exec`.** Both of those fix policy at LAUNCH and have no mid-turn approval handshake, so on either one Dopl's gate would be a pre-flight list and the outbound consent card would have no mechanism. **`main/runtime/codex/client.js` is the only module that frames JSON-RPC** — ⚠ **it is NOT the only one that spawns a child, corrected 2026-09-01**: `codex/credential.js` runs `execFile('codex', ['login','status'])` as its credential probe. The JSON-RPC half of the old sentence was the load-bearing half and is unchanged; the spawn half was simply false, and "one module spawns children" is exactly the kind of claim a reviewer relies on when auditing where a binary can be invoked (`grep -rn "execFile\|spawn(" dopl-desktop-app/main/runtime/codex/`).
- 🔒 **AXIS A'S FOUR MODES ARE `approval_policy`'S OWN VALUES, ORDERED NARROWEST FIRST: `untrusted` / `granular` / `on-request` / `never`.** ⚠ **`granular` sits SECOND, not last, and the design's §1.4 table was wrong about this.** That array is an ORDERING — `[0]` is the fail-closed member and the LAST entry is the widest — so listing `granular` last would declare it the widest mode and make a tightly-configured granular session immune to the windowless floor. Dopl's own gate treats `granular` as no wider than `untrusted`, because its five categories are configured on Codex's side and this process cannot read them. `on-failure` is not offered: documented as deprecated.
- **The gate is asked about CODEX'S OWN WORDS, and there are only three kinds.** `commandExecution` and `fileChange` (the app-server's approval-request item names), the five `granular` category names, and MCP tool names. `main/runtime/codex/server-requests.js › answer` is the ONE place a server request becomes a gate name (`› REQUEST_NAMES`: `commandExecution`, `fileChange`, `request_permissions`; a tool-call elicitation from Dopl's own server via `› doplElicitation`) and the one place a verdict becomes that method's reply (`› decisionReply` for the `{decision}` methods). An approval method this build does not know is answered JSON-RPC `-32601` and never reaches the gate — a reply in the wrong shape would hang the turn (CX-05, 2026-09-23; `approval.js` is deleted). `client.js › connect` answers a request with NO handler, or whose handler throws, with a JSON-RPC error (`-32603`, or the handler's own `rpcCode`) — never a guessed `{decision}` (CX-25).
- 🔒 **A RESTRICTED PROFILE SHIPS BOTH LAYERS: the native pair AND a deny list.** `read_only` / `dopl_only` pin `sandbox_mode='read-only'` + `approval_policy='untrusted'` (the operator's Axis-A pick does not move them) **and** deny `commandExecution`, `fileChange`, `sandbox_approval`, `request_permissions`, `skill_approval` plus the Dopl surface. `full` is `UNIVERSAL_HARD_DENY` and pins no native pair. **Nothing is pre-approved on any profile** — Codex raises no approval request for a read, so there is no name to pre-approve and listing one would only create a shadow past the gate.
  - 🔒 **DELEGATION IS OFF ON EVERY PROFILE (2026-09-22, C25 closed, measured on codex-cli 0.155.1).** Matching Claude's `Agent` removal on all profiles: on Dopl an agent delegates by launching a visible Dopl agent (`dopl_channel(op="manage", action="launch")`). Two levers, because one is not enough: `features.multi_agent = false` on every profile (`runtime/codex/tools.js › ACCOUNT_FENCE`) is what a model with no catalog `multi_agent_version` obeys (gpt-5.5); every `code_mode_only` model's catalog `multi_agent_version` OVERRIDES every `[features]` key, so `runtime/codex/catalog.js › writeDelegationFreeCatalog` writes Codex's OWN catalog (the private home's `models_cache.json`, else `debug models --bundled`, else `debug models`) with `multi_agent_version: null` and `launch-spec.js › start` passes it as `-c model_catalog_json=…` — PROCESS config; the same key in `thread/start.config` is ignored. A forced `spawn_agent` then answers `unsupported call` with no child thread. 🔒 **NO CATALOG → THE LAUNCH THROWS.** ⚠ **THE CATALOG READ IS ASYNC (CX-09, 2026-09-23)** — `execFile`, never `execFileSync` on the Electron main thread (a cache miss froze the UI for up to ~20s); `start()` still returns its handle synchronously and spawns the app-server only after the catalog resolves, so a `close()` first means no child at all.
  - 🔒 **PERSISTENCE / SCHEDULING IS OFF ON EVERY PROFILE TOO (2026-09-22, C26 closed, measured on codex-cli 0.155.1 with a scripted model — `dopl-desktop-app/test/codex-persistence-fence-live.test.mjs`).** The twin of Claude's `CronCreate`/`ScheduleWakeup`/`Monitor` removal: later work on Dopl is a VISIBLE Dopl agent, and waiting is a hold on `dopl_channel read(wait_ms)`. `runtime/codex/tools.js › PERSISTENCE_FENCE` rides every `thread/start.config.features` beside the account fence: **`goals = false`** (`get_goal`/`create_goal`/`update_goal` were offered on every profile, and one forced `create_goal` made the app-server start ~500 turns BY ITSELF in 8s, the goal stored in the shared private home's `goals_1.sqlite`), **`sleep_tool = false`** (`clock.sleep`, 1ms–12h, on every code-mode model), **`memories = false`** (off by default today; ON, a hidden "Memory Writing Agent" model request with a shell wrote `$CODEX_HOME/memories/` — the home EVERY Dopl Codex session shares, i.e. cross-channel state), **`hooks = false`** (not agent-reachable — a planted private-home `hooks.json` loads `untrusted` and never fires, and trust arrives only through config — but it fired once trusted, so it is off like Claude's `settingSources: []`; ⚠ Dopl's own `PreToolUse` stamp, C18, must turn it back on deliberately). And `launch-spec.js › buildLaunchSpec` pins **`thread/start.config.notify = []`** (`tools.js › NOTIFY_FENCE`): `notify` fired from the home `config.toml`, from `-c` argv AND from thread config, and a thread `[]` silenced a home-layer one. ⚠ **NO AGENT VERB EXISTS FOR AUTOMATIONS OR THE THREAD QUEUE**: no automation tool is offered signed in or not, with `in_app_local_automation` on or off, and `thread/queue/*`, `thread/goal/set` and `memory/*` are client methods Dopl never sends; plugin `scheduled_tasks` need `plugin/install`, behind `plugins = false`. The shell stays a shell (`crontab`, `launchd`, `codex queue`), exactly as Claude's `Bash` is — its fence is `commandExecution` + the sandbox, not this one.
  - ⚠ **`dopl_only` IS STRICTLY NARROWER HERE THAN ON CLAUDE**: it reaches the web there (`WEB_TOOLS`) and cannot here, because network is a property of the sandbox rather than a named tool and the escalation that would open it is on this profile's deny list.
  - **`channel_agent` (2026-09-02, ruling B7) IS `full` PLUS `ESCALATION_ITEMS` ON THE DENY LIST** — `commandExecution` and `sandbox_approval`, the shell and the one documented way out of the sandbox that bounds it. ⚠ **`native` STAYS `full`'S `null`**: the ruling removes the shell, not the operator's Axis-A pick, and pinning a `sandbox_mode` / `approval_policy` pair here would be a second, unasked posture decision. `fileChange` is NOT denied — this is `full` minus the shell, not a sandbox. Delegation is fenced for it exactly as for every profile (above).
- 🔒 **THE OPERATOR'S `never` IS NOT SENT AS CODEX'S `never` (2026-09-22, the Claude `permissionMode: 'default'` pattern).** Native `never` raised no request for `dopl_channel` and the call FAILED, so a Codex agent on `never` could not read or post. `runtime/codex/policy.js › NEVER_NATIVE` sends `granular` with `sandbox_approval`/`rules`/`skill_approval`/`request_permissions` **false (Codex auto-REJECTS those, `never`'s own answer)** and `mcp_elicitations` **true**, so the channel call reaches Dopl's gate and Axis A/B answer it (no human card where the Messaging row says none). Measured identical to native `never` for in-sandbox shell, in-workspace patches, escalation, out-of-root writes and network (`test/codex-parity-fences-live.test.mjs`). The mode's stored value, label and meaning are unchanged — no migration. ⚠ **AN OBJECT POLICY RIDES `thread/start.config.approval_policy`, NEVER THE TYPED FIELD** (`policy.js › placePolicy`): the field refuses `granular` without the experimental API (`-32600`), which had also made the operator's own `granular` unlaunchable. `› assertPolicyTook` compares the object echo per schema key.
- 🔒 **NO SKILL CATALOGUE REACHES A CODEX AGENT, PERSONAL OR BUNDLED (2026-09-22, the Claude `Skill`-removal twin).** Codex read `~/.agents/skills`, `$CODEX_HOME/skills/.system`, `<cwd>/.codex/skills` and `.agents/skills` from the project root down, whatever `CODEX_HOME` is, and a `$name` mention injected a skill's whole body. `runtime/codex/skills-fence.js › skillsFence` rides every `thread/start.config.skills`: `include_instructions = false`, `bundled.enabled = false`, and a `{path|name, enabled = false}` entry per SKILL.md found under a SUPERSET of those roots — only the per-skill selector stops a `$mention`; a root path does nothing. ⚠ A skill added to a root after launch is not covered.
- 🔒 **AXIS B'S PIN IS PER-MCP-TOOL AND INDEPENDENT OF AXIS A.** `tools.dopl_channel.approval_mode = 'prompt'` is what guarantees a channel post reaches the gate however wide the operator's `approval_policy` is — because **no tool posture can send a message**, on any runtime. The server default is `default_tools_approval_mode = 'approve'` (`codex/mcp.js › DEFAULT_TOOL_APPROVAL_MODE`, the only never-ask mode — `auto` asks, measured), so `dopl_channel` is the SOLE asker: an elicitation names no tool, and a second asker would make every ask un-nameable. (Corrected 2026-09-23: this read `'writes'`.) ⚠ **NON-CHANNEL DOPL TOOLS RAISE NO APPROVAL REQUEST ON CODEX AT ALL** (CX-23): only `dopl_channel` and the item/category names reach the gate on this runtime, and `enabled_tools` (the offer bound) is ABSENT on `full` / `channel_agent`, so the whole Dopl surface is offered there — the profile narrows it through `X-Dopl-Tool-Profile` (below).
- 🔒 **THE DOPL ENTRY CARRIES `X-Dopl-Tool-Profile` (CX-12, 2026-09-23, R5 default: parity).** `codex/mcp.js › buildDoplServerEntry(policy, profile)` stamps `normalizeProfile(profile)` exactly as `claude/loader.js › withToolProfileStamp` does, so the server offers each profile the same surface on both runtimes: a `read_only` Codex agent is offered NO Dopl tool and a `dopl_only` one no `dopl_channel` (both could reach `dopl_channel` through the gate before).
- ⚠ **THE HELD CALLBACK ANSWERS IN CORE'S VERDICT VOCABULARY (`{behavior, message}`), AND THE WIRE TRANSLATION HAPPENS IN `server-requests.js › answer`** (`launch-spec.js › makeApprovalHandler` wires the gate to it). The callback itself is the shared `main/runtime/held-gate.js › makeHeldGate` on all three runtimes, with `› settledVerdict` the one allow/deny shape (CX-16, 2026-09-23). `session-permissions.js` (the operator's own click) and `session-outbound-tag.js` mint or read that shape, and `session-gate-bridge.js` reads `verdict.behavior`; an adapter answering in its platform word upstream of core hands core a verdict it cannot read. **That contract is undeclared — F-382.** (The `wrapGate` wrapper and its module were deleted 2026-09-23: nothing received the quiet emit they served.)
- **CODEX HAS NO INPUT-REWRITE ROUTE, SO THE FORCED THREAD TAG IS NOT APPLIED ON THIS RUNTIME** (`codex/axis-b.js › descriptor.inputRewrite: null`; `runtime.stampOutbound` answers `null`; CX-15, 2026-09-23 — the tests-only `PreToolUse` stamp path is deleted). The approval reply has no slot for rewritten arguments and no hook is configured (`tools.js › PERSISTENCE_FENCE` keeps `hooks = false`). Self-echo is still filtered by the server's `session_id` stamp.
- **The bearer NEVER touches argv.** `-c` overrides appear in the child's command line, so the token rides the child's ENV and only its variable NAME is passed: `bearer_token_env_var` + `env_http_headers` for the workspace and session pins. No token → no `mcp_servers.dopl` entry at all, and the session still launches.
  - 🔒 **AND THE BEARER NEVER REACHES A SHELL (CX-03, 2026-09-23).** It rides the app-server env as `DOPL_MCP_TOKEN` (`codex/mcp.js › BEARER_ENV`; it was `DOPL_MCP_BEARER`), and Codex builds every shell command's env from its own, so every launch pins `thread/start.config.shell_environment_policy = { exclude: ['DOPL_MCP_*'] }` (`codex/mcp.js › shellEnvironmentPolicy`). ⚠ **MEASURED on codex-cli 0.155.1 with no model turn** (`thread/shellCommand` running `env | grep DOPL_`): with no policy every var was visible, INCLUDING `*TOKEN*` names — Codex's KEY/TOKEN/SECRET default exclude is OFF by default (`ignore_default_excludes` defaults true), so a direct `curl` with the printed bearer would have bypassed the desktop gate. The `exclude` hides the whole `DOPL_MCP_*` set; the `_TOKEN` rename is belt only. Pinned by `test/codex-launch-stamps.test.mjs`.
- 🔒 **AMBIENT CONFIG IS FENCED BY AN APP-OWNED `CODEX_HOME`, NOT BY A FLAG — AND THE FLAG THIS BULLET USED TO NAME DOES NOT EXIST (corrected 2026-09-22).** It read *"`--ignore-user-config` is the fence, first in argv"*, and **`codex app-server` has no such flag at all** — `--help` shows `-c key=value`, `--enable/--disable <FEATURE>` and `--strict-config`. So it was not a fence that had weakened; it was an argument the CLI rejects, and every spawn carrying it died at argument parsing before `initialize`. ⚠ **AND TWO SITES SENT IT, SO THE MODEL PICKER BROKE INDEPENDENTLY OF THE LAUNCH** (`launch-spec.js` and `models.js`). **`main/runtime/codex/config-home.js › isolatedEnv` IS THE FENCE NOW:** it points `CODEX_HOME` and `CODEX_SQLITE_HOME` at a `0o700` directory under the app's own `userData` (`› PRIVATE_HOME`) and exposes ONLY the operator's existing `auth.json`, through a symlink — so `~/.codex/config.toml`, its profiles, its MCP servers and its permission defaults cannot widen a session Dopl launched, and the credential is shared without copying a bearer or putting one on argv. 🔒 **IT REFUSES TO LAUNCH IF A `config.toml` APPEARS IN THAT PRIVATE HOME** (`› hasAmbientConfig` — the app puts none there, so one that exists was put there by something else), **and an `auth.json` there that is not a SYMLINK is the same refusal**: an app-owned link may be repointed, a real file may not. ⚠ **BOTH SPAWNERS GO THROUGH IT** (`grep -rn 'isolatedEnv' dopl-desktop-app/main/` → `launch-spec.js`, `models.js` and the module itself @ 2026-09-22); `models.js` passes `args: []`, a session passes exactly the delegation catalog (`-c model_catalog_json=…`, a path, never a secret); approval policy, sandbox, model, skills and MCP configuration ride `thread/start`, and reasoning effort rides `turn/start`. `test/codex-gate.test.mjs` asserts the dead flag is never sent again.
- 🔒 **ONE HONEST REFUSAL LEFT, A DECLARATION RATHER THAN A GAP (re-derived 2026-09-23 — this said THREE).** The `meter` block left every descriptor (RC-07 — there is no cost cap to hide), and `session.usageResetsOnResume` is `false`, MEASURED on codex-cli 0.155.1 (the cumulative total continues across `thread/resume`), so a Codex session RESUMES (`capability.js › canResume` is true; `› resumeZeroesBaseline` carries the baseline forward). **Re-derive from the sub-bullets, and a declaration that leaves takes its row with it.**
  - **`credential.interactiveSignIn: null`** — `codex login` opens a browser and `--device-auth` needs a terminal; neither is driveable in-window. `signIn()` answers `null` and the UI shows a pointer, not a button that opens nothing (C20).
- **`packaging.delivery: 'bundled'`, `versionPin: '@openai/codex@0.155.1'`** (`runtime/codex/packaging.js`; re-read 2026-09-23 — this said `'path'` / `null`). The `@openai/codex*` platform package ships inside the app, re-signed with it (`asarUnpack` globs test-pinned); the pin equals `protocol.js › SUPPORTED_CLI.measuredFrom` and the exact `package.json` dependency. `resolve-bin.js` still falls back to an operator-installed binary when the optional platform package is absent. `available()` is still a real probe with an operator-readable refusal.
  - ⚠ **IT IS NOT "FOUND ON `PATH`", AND THIS BULLET SAID `PATH` UNTIL 2026-09-22.** A Finder-launched app gets `launchd`'s environment — roughly `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` — not the `PATH` the operator's shell builds, so every prefix Codex actually installs into is invisible to `spawn('codex')` and a machine with a working `codex` in Terminal reported *"not on this Mac's PATH"* the moment Dopl was opened from the Dock. `main/runtime/codex/resolve-bin.js › resolveCodexBin` is the ONE answer the probe, the credential check, the roster read and the spawn all ask for: the `DOPL_CODEX_BIN` override (⚠ **one that does not resolve is an ERROR, never a fallback** — naming a file and silently running a different one is how a diagnostic measures the wrong binary), then the bundled package, then `PATH`, then the well-known macOS prefixes, then the directory beside the running Node (`› nodeNeighbours(process.execPath)` — which only helps under plain node, scripts and tests; in Electron main `execPath` is the Dopl binary). It caches a HIT for the process and re-walks a miss, so a Codex installed with Dopl open is found (CX-08). An npm install that resolves to the `@openai/codex` package's `bin` node launcher script is mapped to the vendor binary it would spawn (`› launcherVendor`), the launcher staying the answer when no vendor binary is beside it (CX-07). 🔒 **A FILE NAMED `codex` IS NOT A REASON TO RUN IT** — a candidate must be a regular file this user may execute, and neither it nor any directory resolving its candidate OR canonical path may be writable by other users, because anything that can replace the target chooses what Dopl runs. ⚠ **"WRITABLE BY OTHERS" IS NOT `& 0o022`** (`› writableByOthers`): world-writable is always refused, group-writable only when the owner is neither this user nor root — the flat reading refused Homebrew's own directories, whose group bit is by design. **A REFUSED candidate is reported with its reason and never as "not installed"**, and the answer carries `source` and `path`, because a version report that cannot name its binary cannot settle a support question.
  - 🔒 **THE MEASURED CLI FLOOR IS ENFORCED AT `available()` (CX-06, 2026-09-23).** `main/runtime/codex/client.js › probe` runs `protocol.js › versionGate` over `codex --version`; a CLI below `protocol.js › SUPPORTED_CLI.min` (`0.155.1` @ 2026-09-23 — `grep -n 'const SUPPORTED_CLI' dopl-desktop-app/main/runtime/codex/protocol.js`; re-measure with `cd dopl-desktop-app && npm run codex:schema`, never by hand) or with no readable version is refused with the gate's own operator sentence, on `available()` and the roster read alike. A NEWER CLI is not refused: the release gate (`npm run test:codex-compat`) checks the installed CLI declares every `› REQUIRED_METHODS` method (the methods this adapter actually sends — one added to the adapter belongs on that list in the same change; the fixture's `doplRequires.methods` mirrors it). ⚠ **The earlier protocol-state gate (`checkProtocol`, `PROTOCOL_STATE`, `REQUIRED_FACTS`, `catalogGate`, the `max`/`unpinned` arms) is DELETED** — it had no caller in the connected-state path. What survives of its argument: below the floor is a protocol nobody measured, above it is the future, and refusing the future would strand operators the day Codex ships a compatible release.
- **`mcp.toolNamePrefix` IS `'<tool>'`, MEASURED** (re-read 2026-09-23 — this said `null`, "the highest-stake unknown"): `mcpToolCall` carries `{ server, tool }` with the tool name BARE, no `mcp__` prefix. `main/mcp-tool-names.js` handles the bare form and `mcp__<server>__`; ⚠ **a third shape would miss every list in the gate at once — Axis B, the pre-approvals, both Axis-A lists and hard-deny — which is F-139 reproduced.**
- **MEASURED SPELLINGS ONLY (CX-40, 2026-09-23).** The Codex normalizer, launch spec and roster read the 0.155.1 schema's spellings only (`item.type`/`item.id`, `agentMessage.text`, `reasoning.summary|content`, `commandExecution.command|aggregatedOutput`, `mcpToolCall.tool|arguments`, `TokenUsageBreakdown.inputTokens|outputTokens|totalTokens`, `model/list`'s `{ data, nextCursor }` with `id`/`displayName`/`isDefault`/`supportedReasoningEfforts[].reasoningEffort`). Drift is the release gate's to catch (`npm run test:codex-compat`), not a tolerant reader's to hide.
- 🔒 **HANDSHAKE AND TRANSPORT (CX-01/10/14, 2026-09-23).** `initialize` is followed by the `initialized` client notification (launch and roster). A fresh `thread/start` answering no `thread.id` fails the stream. `client.js › connect` reports the child's end ONCE, on `close` (stdout drained; bounded 2s after `exit`), as `onExit(code, signal, spawnError)` — a spawn failure (`error` + `close`, no `exit`) rejects with its own errno. A `stdin.write` returning `false` is BACKPRESSURE, not closure (a ≥64 KiB request used to reject while still being delivered).
- 🔒 **A FAILED TURN IS A LINE, NEVER SILENCE (CX-04, R7 default, 2026-09-23).** An app-server `error` notification with `willRetry !== true`, or a `turn/completed` with `turn.status: 'failed'`, becomes ONE synthetic `{ type: 'error', text, codexErrorInfo, turnFailed }` frame per turn (`launch-spec.js`). `codex/normalize.js`: auth-shaped text, or `codexErrorInfo` `unauthorized` / HTTP 401/403 → `auth_hold`; any other failed turn → ONE `assistant` line `Codex could not finish this turn: <message>` in the agent's lane (no reducer change). Core's own rejection frame (no `turnFailed`) still renders nothing (crash path). An expired sign-in or a usage limit used to leave the agent silently saying nothing.
- **TOKEN BASELINE ACROSS AN INTERRUPT (CX-02).** The adapter carries the thread's last cumulative `total` onto an interrupted `turn/completed` (which gets no `thread/tokenUsage/updated`); with no measurement at all the `result` is unmeasured (`null`, §11.0a).
- **Fixtures, not installs.** `test/codex-normalize.test.mjs` (11 cases) drives the pure normalizer from synthetic frames whose shapes are cited, per fixture, to a section of the Codex platform research (which lives OUTSIDE this repo, so it is named in prose rather than cited as a path), including a garbage payload that must still render a card; `test/codex-gate.test.mjs` (27 cases) drives the v2.9 invariant BOTH ways against this adapter, the containment table, the windowless floor resolving to a Codex mode, the no-`acceptForSession` refusal, and the stamp.
- ⚠ **THREE CONFORMANCE CASES WERE REPAIRED BY THE SECOND ADAPTER, NOT WORKED AROUND — each was correct at one adapter and wrong at two.** (1) `runtime-contract.test.mjs`'s resume case asserted "a runtime that declares `resume` MUST be able to resume", which is the OPPOSITE of the field's design; it now asserts a resume is never SILENTLY allowed over an unmeasured baseline, and that a refusal is readable. (2) Its unknown-id case listed `"codex"` among the junk values, so it began asserting that a REAL runtime resolves to the default; the junk is now words no runtime will ever be, plus the inverse assertion that every registered id resolves to itself. (3) `adapter-parity.test.mjs`'s "declared absent somewhere" case ran over EVERY field, including ones that can never be null (`entryFile` is refused as a non-string; `axisB.enforcementPoint` refuses registration) — it now runs over the NULLABLE subset, with a dated `PENDING_UNTIL_CURSOR` census for the six fields that cannot vary until the third adapter, which has its own staleness case and empties itself at three.

#### 11.0e The THIRD adapter and the INTEGRATION (2026-08-31, port wave D) — core actually reaches the adapters

- **`registry.ids()` → `['claude','codex','cursor']` @ 2026-08-31** (`cd dopl-desktop-app && node -e "console.log(require('./main/runtime').ids())"`). The third cost one `register(require('./cursor'))` line and a directory, exactly as the second did. ⚠ **IT REGISTERS AND IT DOES NOT SHIP.** `descriptor.session.interrupt` is `'unverified'` — the SDK documents no interrupt — and Dopl may not own a session it cannot stop. Registration is what makes the conformance suite MEASURE it; the ship gate is Samuel's (smoke item X0). ⚠ **X0 WAS RULED ON 2026-09-02 AND THE ANSWER IS HOLD** — Claude and Codex ship, Cursor does not — so this adapter is FROZEN: it stayed at three profiles when the other two gained `channel_agent` (§11, ruling B7), and `contract.js › LAUNCH_BLOCKING[1]` is what refuses a launch at the fourth. **A runtime that does not ship does not grow a containment table nobody has smoke-tested.**
- 🔒 **A RUNTIME PICK IS A CHOICE BETWEEN ENFORCED ALTERNATIVES, NOT A CONTAINMENT INPUT — WHICH IS WHY IT MAY TRAVEL WHERE A TOOL PROFILE MAY NOT.** `main/runtime/contract.js › sealAdapter` REFUSES to register an adapter that declares no Axis-B enforcement point, or a profile with no deny list in that runtime's own vocabulary — so "registered" already means "this build proved its gate". Every adapter re-derives its own deny lists (`runtime.toolConfigFor`) and its own Axis-A vocabulary (`runtime.axisAAllows`), and the four `grantDecision` steps AHEAD of Axis A (hard-deny, the audience belt, the Axis-B branch, the profile's deny list) are core's on all three. **There is no runtime whose selection opens something another runtime closed.** `main/channel-runtime.js` is the one spelling of this argument.
- **THE PICK IS THE `model`'S SHAPE, NOT THE POSTURE'S — durable per channel, and it has FOUR readers on purpose.** `main/channel-runtime.js › getChannelRuntime` is the named door. ⚠ **THE RECORD BEHIND IT IS THE CHANNEL'S VERSIONED LAUNCH SELECTION SINCE 2026-09-21 (U5), AND THIS BULLET NAMED THE OLD ONE UNTIL 2026-09-22.** It said *"(`electron-store`, key `channelRuntime`)"*; the authority is **`main/launch-selection.js`, stored under `channelLaunchSelection`** (`main/channel-prefs.js › SELECTION_KEY`, local-only, never POSTed). `channelRuntime` survives ONLY as that record's READ-ONLY **MIGRATION SOURCE** (a channel with no selection seeds its runtime from it); nothing writes it any more (the downgrade mirror is deleted, P3-13, 2026-09-23) — **nothing reads it as the pick, and `channel-runtime.js` no longer opens a store handle at all.** 🔒 **THE LAUNCH LANES READ IT THROUGH ONE RESOLVER (Samuel's ruling 5, 2026-09-23: *"Identity's, unless picked"*): `runtime/launch-default.js › resolveLaunchRuntime({ pick, identity, channelId })`** → `{ ok: true, runtimeId, source: 'pick'|'identity'|'channel'|'default' }` or `{ ok: false, reason: 'no-sdk', runtimeId }`. ORDER: the launcher's explicit pick → the identity's runtime (§5A) → the channel's runtime → the registry default. An explicit pick or an identity runtime that is unregistered or not usable on this Mac REFUSES `no-sdk` (the same refusal the directive lane gives an unusable explicit runtime); the channel and default links fail OPEN. If the launcher overrides the runtime, the identity's model is skipped when that runtime does not offer it (`› identityModelFor`, below). Callers: `session-launch-op.js › launchFromButton` (the operator's button), `trigger.js › launchResponderSession` (the peer-triggered responder: no pick, no identity) and `launch-directive-spawn.js` (the orchestrator lane) — **plus `channel-dir-ipc.js`, which serves the channel pick back to the SPA's posture row** through `getChannelRuntime`. ⚠ **RE-DERIVE, NEVER QUOTE: `grep -rn 'getChannelRuntime\|resolveLaunchRuntime' dopl-desktop-app/main/`**. ⚠ **THIS SAID "THREE" UNTIL 2026-09-01 AND THE MISCOUNT BLUNTED THE POINT IT WAS MAKING.** The sentence's whole force is a CONSUMER-COUNT CONTRAST with the durable permission pair, **whose one consumer IS `channel-dir-ipc.js`** — so like for like the contrast is **4-vs-1**, not 3-vs-1, and the omitted reader was the very file the other side of the comparison names. **THE CONTRAST ITSELF IS UNCHANGED AND IS WHAT KEEPS H2 CLOSED** — a posture may only reach a launch a human is attending. A runtime may reach every lane, because a channel whose operator chose one would otherwise answer its peers on a different vendor's model against a different credential, which is the surprise the port exists to remove.
- **`''` IS THE ONLY SPELLING OF "NO PICK", AND AN UNKNOWN ID READS AS THE DEFAULT WITHOUT BEING REPAIRED.** `› normalizeRuntimeId` validates against `runtime/index.js › ids()` — never a second list — and answers `''` for anything else. ⚠ **`setChannelRuntime` NO LONGER EXISTS (deleted 2026-09-21, U5), THIS BULLET DESCRIBED IT UNTIL 2026-09-22, AND IT MUST NOT COME BACK.** It was a SECOND writer of a record whose whole design is that it has one, and since 2026-09-06 it had also CLEARED the channel's stored model as a side effect of a runtime switch. **Both halves are gone and neither is coming back.** The WRITE is a field of the launch selection now, made by that record's one validating writer — `main/channel-prefs.js › setLaunchSelection(id, { runtime })`, own-key, so it leaves every other field alone. 🔓 **THE CLEAR IS REVERSED BY RULING (Samuel, decisions #1/#2): the OTHER runtime's pick SURVIVES BY DESIGN** — Claude → Codex → Claude restores both remembered Axis-A words and both native sets, translating neither (no launch record stores a model since 2026-09-23). The clear existed because one global model field could not hold two rosters and a stale id WON over the new runtime's default; a runtime-keyed record makes the stale id unreachable from the wrong adapter by construction. A census suite over `main/` asserts the symbol has zero live occurrences (`grep -rn 'setChannelRuntime' dopl-desktop-app/main/` → comments only @ 2026-09-22), **because a zero-caller export is not a free seam**: the writer census there is what keeps H2 honest, and it can only stay honest if every name in it is a writer something actually reaches. Reading NEVER repairs: a stored id from a build that knew a runtime this one does not is left alone (re-upgrade and the pick is still there) while the launch lands on the default. An unreadable store is the DEFAULT runtime, **not** a refusal — the opposite direction from `orchestrator-consent.js`, and the difference is what the record means: that one is a consent, this one is a choice between alternatives this build has already proved.

So a switch and a switch back restores BOTH remembered sets rather than mapping, clearing or reinterpreting either.

The core model table is gone from `main/` as well (the session-model module is deleted; the table is `runtime/claude/model-table.js`).

A half-valid legacy pair migrates nothing and reads as unconfigured (`launch-selection.js › legacyPreset`). ⚠ **LEGACY `tools` LANDS IN THE DEFAULT RUNTIME'S RECORD WHATEVER RUNTIME IS SELECTED (a legacy `model` is dropped since 2026-09-23)** — that is the only vocabulary the old validators could store, so filing them under the SELECTED runtime would be the migration asserting that `accept_edits` "is" some Codex approval mode.
  - 🔒 **THE LAUNCH READ IS THE LAUNCH RUNTIME'S RECORD, NOT THE SELECTED ONE'S (C1, 2026-09-23).** `channel-prefs.js › launchStartModes(channelId, runtimeId)` reads `byRuntime[runtimeId || selected || default]` — the LAUNCH runtime's tools in its own words, its native bag, and the windowless-floored messages (`session-profiles.js › floorWindowlessMessage`). `› launchPostureFor(channelId, runtimeId)` is the same record with messages UNFLOORED: the ceiling a per-agent pick or a directive is clamped to, and the live Axis-A value a running session of that runtime gates on. A Codex launch from a Claude-selected channel no longer takes the Claude record (P3-04).
  - 🔒 **READS FLOOR, WRITES REJECT, AND NOTHING ANYWHERE RESOLVES TO UNRESTRICTED.** The operator-defaults record obeys it too since 2026-09-23 (P3-29): `agent-defaults.js › setAgentDefaults` REJECTS a registered runtime's `byRuntime[id].tools` that runtime does not offer (`{ok:false, rejected}`). Every floor surfaces a `needsReview` sentence, because a silent floor is the same failure as a silent widening, one direction along.

    | what is stored | what a READ resolves to | reviewed out loud? |
    |---|---|---|
    | a record version this build does not read | the RESTRICTIVE selection — and the runtime PICK survives when the record is NEWER and the id is registered, because picking a runtime widens nothing | yes |
    | a malformed or unreadable record | the RESTRICTIVE selection, with no preserved pick | yes |
    | a `byRuntime['']` record (a write keyed by the unpicked runtime) | FOLDED into the DEFAULT runtime's record, its fields winning (`launch-selection.js › foldDefaultKey`, called by `› normalizeSelection`; P3-05, 2026-09-23) — read, never carried as an unregistered id | — |
    | a runtime id not registered here | reads as the DEFAULT adapter, **is not repaired**, and its `byRuntime` record is kept VERBATIM and never read — a downgrade must not destroy what an upgrade stored | — |
    | a `tools` value the selected adapter does not offer | that adapter's NARROWEST mode (`toolMode.options[0]`) | yes |
    | a `native` KEY the adapter does not declare | dropped | yes |
    | a `native` VALUE unknown on a CONTAINMENT axis | that axis's NARROWEST option — **never the widest, and never the platform default** | yes |
    | a `native` key that is a MODEL dimension (any value) | dropped — model-scoped settings are not stored since 2026-09-23 | **no** — nothing narrowed |
    | a `model`, any value | dropped — no launch record stores a model since 2026-09-23 | **no** — nothing narrowed |
    | an absent field | absent stays absent, and an explicit clear IS an absence — never `''`, `null` or `{}`, so no reader can grow a third state to get wrong | — |

  - ⚠ **THE WRITE SIDE IS RE-VALIDATED IN MAIN, AGAINST THE SELECTED ADAPTER.** A renderer one version ahead cannot smuggle in an unregistered runtime id, a mode outside that adapter's declared options, or a native setting the adapter cannot spend (a `model` is ignored). There is no free-text field and no path.
  - 🔒 **A PATCH BRIDGE SENDS OWN-KEYS ONLY, AND COERCING ABSENCE INTO A VALUE TURNS "not changing this" INTO "set this to empty" (F-754).** `renderer/app-preload.js` spreads each key conditionally; `test/launch-selection-bridge.test.mjs` is the pin. ⚠ **NEITHER HALF OF THAT DEFECT COULD FAIL A TEST** — main was right, the renderer was right, and only the record between them was wrong.
- 🔒 **A RUNTIME'S MODEL ROSTER IS A VERSIONED CATALOG WITH FOUR STATES, AND COLLAPSING ANY TWO IS THE BUG (2026-09-21, U6).** `main/runtime/model-catalog.js` (`› CATALOG_VERSION`, `› STATUS`), one record per runtime: `{ version, runtime, source, status, reason, key, models[], defaultId, dimensions[], truncated }` — **the same keys on every status**, so a consumer reads `status` and never the shape.
  - **`loading`** — nothing has been read yet. The picker shows the platform default, **never "no models"**.
  - **`ready`** — a roster was read.
  - **`unavailable`** — a read was ATTEMPTED and failed, carrying the binary's own reason.
  - **`stale`** — models from a binary or version we can no longer confirm. They still LABEL; they may not be newly SELECTED.
  - ⚠ **AN EMPTY ROSTER IS NEVER `ready`.** No adapter may claim a platform has no models, so an empty list resolves to `unavailable` with a reason (`› catalogFromRoster`). **This is §11's UNKNOWN-is-not-EMPTY rule applied to a roster** — an empty list had been the answer to every failure, and a picker cannot tell that apart from a platform that genuinely has none. ⚠ A `ready` catalog MAY still carry a `reason` (pagination stopped at the page cap; the server declared no single default): `reason` is a NOTE on `ready` and a FAILURE only on the two statuses that have no models.
  - **ONE STALE-ID RULE, NOT THREE CASES.** `src/features/channels/lib/model-catalog.ts › selectableModels` is EMPTY unless `ready`, so a `loading` / `unavailable` / `stale` id cannot be NEWLY selected, while `› modelLabel` reads any status so a historical card still shows its raw id. `› catalogSelection` DISPLAYS `defaultId` without persisting it — the display-versus-wire discipline.
  - **CACHED BY `<resolved binary path>@<version>`**, so an upgrade or a repointed `DOPL_CODEX_BIN` re-reads by construction. ⚠ **A FAILED READ IS NEVER CACHED FOR THE LIFE OF THE APP** (`› FAILURE_TTL_MS`): an operator who repairs their install with Dopl open recovers without restarting, and a refresh that fails over models already held becomes `stale`, not `unavailable`. ⚠ **`› invalidate` KEEPS WHAT A CATALOG HOLDS (RC-02, 2026-09-23)**: a catalog with models keeps them AND its status (READY stays READY) and is only marked due — the next look re-reads while answering what it held; one with none becomes `loading`. (It became `stale`, which nothing re-polled, and the picker sat "loading" forever.) The web re-read budget for a `loading` catalog is derived from main's settle time (`src/features/channels/hooks/use-runtime-catalogs.ts › MAIN_ROSTER_SETTLE_MS` = the Codex probe 5s + `model/list` 8s; `› MAX_RELOADS` × 1.2s), and a catalog still `loading` once that is spent is re-read on window focus / visibility (F3).
  - **IT CROSSES THE BRIDGE ADDITIVELY** on `channels:getLaunchPosture` and `channels:getAgentDefaults` as `catalogs` + `catalogVersion` (`main/channel-runtime-reply.js`). Renderer and main ship in ONE bundle, so there is no older-desktop fallback (F6, 2026-09-23): a runtime with no catalog reads `null` in the SPA and the picker shows no roster — never a frozen Claude table, never another runtime's catalog.
  - 🔒 **NO RUNTIME'S ROSTER IS HARDCODED (2026-09-22, Samuel: *"if claude or codex add a new model, would dopl auto mark those as options"*).** Every shipped adapter declares `models.source: 'live'`. **Claude** reads `Query.supportedModels()` off a CLI handshake whose streaming prompt never yields — no user message, no API request, **no model turn** (MEASURED: zero SDK messages; `runtime/claude/roster.js › probe`) — and the catalog id is the row's `resolvedModel` (a FULL id, Samuel's 2026-08-22 ruling) while `--model` gets the row's own `value`. The CLI's `default` row is a pointer, not a model, and is dropped. **Codex** reads `model/list` (unchanged).
    - ⚠ **THE FROZEN TABLE IS THE FALLBACK ONLY WHEN THE LIVE READ FAILS, AND IT SAYS SO**: `runtime/claude/models.js › frozenRoster` answers `stale: true` with a reason, and `model-catalog.js › catalogFromRoster` turns that into a `stale` catalog (labels, not newly selectable). ⚠ **DO NOT ADD A ROW TO `runtime/claude/model-table.js › MODEL_IDS` FOR A NEW MODEL** — the live roster already offers it. 🔒 **ONLY A `ready` CATALOG VOUCHES (RC-03, 2026-09-23)**: `model-catalog.js › vouches(catalog)` — a `stale` catalog (the Claude fallback table, or a failed refresh) LABELS only and proves nothing present or absent.
    - **CACHED BY `<binary>@<version>#<credential source>`** (the Claude roster is per ACCOUNT — signed out it omits Fable, measured). `runtime.rosterKey()` is SYNC, and `model-catalog.js › due` re-reads a `ready` catalog whose key MOVED on the next look — a sign-in or an upgrade, no timer, no hook.
    - **AN ENTRY MAY CARRY `aliases`** — other spellings the adapter accepts for THAT model (a legacy stored `claude-opus-5`, a launch alias `opus`). **Matched, never offered**: `model-catalog.js › findModel` / web `model-catalog.ts › findModel` resolve them, so an old pick shows as its row rather than as a second raw option.
    - 🔒 **AN UNKNOWN MODEL IS REFUSED, NEVER COERCED.** `session-launch.js › refuseUnknownModel` awaits `model-catalog.js › settle` ONLY when a model was named and answers `{ skipped: 'no-model', detail }` before anything is constructed; `› modelRefusal` refuses only on a `ready` catalog (a roster Dopl could not read, or a `stale` one, is not evidence a model does not exist — it fails OPEN). `› findModel` is the ONE matcher (`claude/roster.js › matchExact` delegates to it). ⚠ **A LAUNCH MATCHES A PICK BY EXACT ID OR ALIAS ONLY (RC-01, 2026-09-23)**: `claude/models.js › resolveLaunchModel` uses `roster.js › matchExact`, while `roster.js › match` keeps the base-id step for LABELLING and the default marker; `launchArg` sends an unmatched well-formed value as itself, so a resumed `claude-opus-5[1m]` never becomes `--model opus` (200k under a 1M conversation) on the frozen fallback. The live switch (`session-reopen.js › setModelByTask`) refuses the same way (`reason: 'no-model'`); it used to reset the session to the fallback silently.
    - 🔒 **A RUNTIME'S DECLARED `models.launchDefault` IS THE CATALOG'S `defaultId` WHEN A CURRENT ROSTER CARRIES IT (2026-09-23)** — `model-catalog.js › catalogFromRoster` overrides the server's own `isDefault` marker, so the New Agent dialog's display-only preselect (`channels/components/launch-agent-dialog-state.ts › modelRowFor`: own pick > identity > `catalogSelection`'s default) names exactly what a no-pick launch spends. A `stale` roster keeps the server's marker. `test/runtime-launch-default.test.mjs` pins present/absent/unknown. **Claude declares `models.launchDefault` (`claude-sonnet-5`) like Codex** (X-06/RC-05, 2026-09-23 — the runtime default is decided in ONE place); its adapter still spends it itself (`resolveLaunchModel('')`), and `launch-default.js › withRuntimeDefault` skips the roster read for an adapter whose `modelArg('')` already names a model.

Both launch lanes call it directly (`session-launch-op.js › launchFromButton`, `launch-directive-spawn.js`; `session-launch-op.js › identityModel` is deleted, P4-27/P3-28). `''` / `default` is no pick (`runtime/selection-vocabulary.js › pickOf`).
    - **CODEX'S DELEGATION FENCE NEVER DEGRADES A NAMED MODEL**: `runtime/codex/catalog.js › pickModels` REFUSES the launch when no catalog source (cache → bundled → online) has an entry for the session's model, instead of writing an override without it (which started the model on generic defaults).
- 🔒 **THE SESSION'S RUNTIME IS PERSISTED, OR A CRASH RESUME LANDS ON THE WRONG VENDOR.** `session-io.js › baseRecord` and `session-store.js › durableSessionRecord` both carry `runtimeId`. `session-park.js › startResume` rebuilds the whole session from that record and hands the persisted `sdkSessionId` to whatever runtime it acquires — so without the field it resumed onto the DEFAULT adapter, asking it to continue ANOTHER PLATFORM's conversation id in another platform's tool vocabulary against another credential. **Coerced by CHARSET inline (`/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}$/`), not against the registry**, because that projection is evaluated standalone by the extraction tests; `runtime/index.js › resolve` is what turns an unknown id into the default. `null` = a record written before the field, which reads as the runtime it really ran on.
- 🔒 **AND THE RECORD CARRIES WHAT THE CONVERSATION WAS RUNNING AS, NOT ONLY WHICH ADAPTER (2026-09-21, U10).** `main/session-runtime-truth.js › runtimeTruthFields` adds ONE durable field beside `runtimeId`: **`usageBaseline`** (`resets` / `continues` / `unverified`). ⚠ **THE RECORD NO LONGER CARRIES `sdkSessionId`, `effectiveModel` OR `nativePolicy` (P4-18, 2026-09-23)** — none had a reader; the resume map `sessionIds` is the only home of the conversation id. A session rebuilt from a record (`session-boot.js › parkedSessionFromRecord`) carries the record's word as `s.usageBaseline`, and `runtimeTruthFields` writes THAT word back on every later save rather than re-deriving it from today's descriptor. Live/ended summaries and agent-history entries carry no `usageBaseline`. 🔒 **`usageBaseline` IS PERSISTED, NOT RE-DERIVED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON THE FILE EXISTS**: re-deriving it at resume time reads TODAY's descriptor, so a build that later flips `session.usageResetsOnResume` would silently re-interpret a record written under the old answer — a measurement nobody took, about a run that already happened. **A record states what was true when it was written; the live descriptor states what is true now; `runtime/capability.js › resumeRefusal` is still the thing that DECIDES, and none of this weakens it.** ⚠ **READING BACK FAILS CLOSED ON THE ONE FIELD THAT DECIDES ANYTHING** (`› durableRuntimeTruth`): a `usageBaseline` this build does not know reads as `unverified`, which is the direction `canResume` already refuses. 🔒 **PRIVACY — every value is a member of a descriptor's own declared vocabulary**; no prompt, token, approval payload or filesystem path may join this shape, because the record is written to `electron-store` in the clear and read back by diagnostics.
- 🔒 **WHY A RUN STOPPED IS A STRUCTURED CODE, AND THE SENTENCE IS REBUILT AT READ TIME FROM THE RECORD'S OWN `runtimeId` (2026-09-21, U10).** The set is CLOSED — `main/runtime/runtime-copy.js › RUNTIME_ERROR_CODES`: `runtime-missing`, `runtime-signed-out`, `runtime-incompatible`, `runtime-start-failed`, `runtime-crashed`, `runtime-interrupted`, `mcp-unreachable`, `resume-refused` — and an unknown code renders the GENERIC sentence, which names the RUNTIME rather than the condition, instead of a raw key at an operator. **A generic SDK string was the wrong thing to persist**: it cannot be re-said in another runtime's words, cannot be branched on, and carries one vendor's name into a projection every runtime shares. Produced by `main/session-query.js › consume` (start-failure vs crash, split on whether a conversation handle existed) and `main/mcp-connect-guard.js`; rendered by `main/session-detail.js › endReasonFor`. ⚠ **`null` WHEN THERE IS NOTHING TO SAY** — an agent the operator ended, or one that finished, has no failure and must not grow a line claiming one. ⚠ **`detail` IS THE ADAPTER'S OWN SENTENCE, PASSED THROUGH AND NEVER PARSED** — the one part allowed to name a runtime, because it came from one, and the one part whose PRODUCERS are the redaction boundary. ⚠ **`runtime-missing` AND `runtime-incompatible` HAVE NO PRODUCER YET** (`grep -rn 'runtime-missing' dopl-desktop-app/main/` → the vocabulary and its copy table only @ 2026-09-22): the codes exist, and the protocol handshake plus the resolver's unfinished structured state set are what would stamp them. **All of it is local-only** — `main/session-state-push.js › reportRow` picks columns by name, so nothing here widens `channel_sessions`.
- 🔒 **RESUME IS A DECLARED CAPABILITY AND AN UNVERIFIED USAGE METER REFUSES IT — COLD LAUNCH IS UNAFFECTED.** Both resume shapes (`session-park.js › resumeParked`, `› startResume`) ask `runtime/capability.js › resumeRefusal` before they rebuild anything, and refuse IN PLACE with the descriptor's own sentence: nothing is torn down, the session stays parked, and the next wake retries the moment the answer lands. **What is at stake is the SPEND METER, not the resume** (there is no turn/cost cap any more). `resumeParked` zeroes the token baseline only when the runtime restarts its cumulative total (`capability.js › resumeZeroesBaseline(descriptor, s.usageBaseline)`); zeroing it for a runtime that CONTINUES would make every later delta negative, which `session-io.js` clamps to zero — spend silently unmeasured. Re-read 2026-09-23: Claude declares `true`, Codex `false` (measured on 0.155.1 — it resumes, carrying the baseline), Cursor `'unverified'` (refused).
- **`'no-sdk'` IS STILL THE ONE REFUSAL WORD FOR "THIS MACHINE HAS NO AGENT RUNTIME", ON EVERY RUNTIME.** `session-launch.js › launch` forwards `a.runtime` to `acquireRuntime` and invents nothing; a lane that passes nothing lands on the default, which is what every pre-port lane did. **Do not widen the skip vocabulary for a second adapter** — `trigger.js` and the directive lane both branch on the word.
- **THE PICK AND THE DESCRIPTOR TABLE RIDE THE EXISTING POSTURE PAIR, NOT A FOURTH IPC OP.** `channels:getLaunchPosture` answers `{tools, messages, runtime, runtimes, defaultRuntime, …}` (no `model` since 2026-09-23) and `channels:setLaunchPosture` accepts a `runtime` key (own-key: omitting it leaves the pick alone). ⚠ **THIS WAS THE `model` FIELD'S IDIOM** (the deleted `permission-modes.ts` `hasModelKey`: the model rode the existing pair "because there is no new op to feature-detect on, which is what the rest of this family does") **AND THERE IS A HARD CONSTRAINT BEHIND IT**: `renderer/app-preload.js` is AT the 500-line §1 cap and `test/preload-parity.test.mjs` asserts that no preload requires anything but `electron`, so it has no split seam and cannot grow a bridge NAMESPACE without changing that security invariant (F-387). The descriptors survive the structured-clone hop because `contract.js › sealAdapter` deep-freezes them and REFUSES one carrying a function.
- ⚠ **THE RUNTIME PICK IS **NOT** FANNED OUT TO LIVE SESSIONS, and the asymmetry with `applyPostureToLive` is the rule.** That fan-out widens SUPERVISION on a running agent; a session's runtime is stamped at spawn and never read live, because re-pointing one would hand one platform's conversation id to another platform's adapter.
- ⚠ **NINE DESKTOP FILES SIT AT EXACTLY 500 LINES @ 2026-08-31, SEVEN OF THEM CORE SESSION MODULES** (`cd dopl-desktop-app && find main renderer test -type f \( -name '*.js' -o -name '*.mjs' \) | xargs wc -l | awk '$1==500 && $2!="total" {print $2}'`). `max-lines: 500` fails at 501, so all nine are GREEN and invisible to the lint gate — and **a file at the cap does not stop growing, it stops being CORRECTABLE**. This is not a coincidence: a hard cap with no headroom band converges files onto its own boundary. **RUN the command; do not reason about it** — F-388's own first draft asserted "two" and was wrong by seven. `main/session-ipc-ops.js` is on the list and is where the port's step 6 (`claude:signIn` → `runtime:signIn`) lands, so the next wave is already blocked the same way. F-387 (`renderer/app-preload.js`, the one with NO split seam) and F-388 carry it.

#### 11.0g What the port CHANGED in the Claude lane (2026-09-01 — the retraction, and the list)

🔒 **THE CLAIM IS "BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING WITH SEVEN DECLARED OBSERVABLE DIFFERENCES", NOT "BYTE-IDENTICAL".** An independent review diffed the four moved sites against `git show HEAD:` and disproved the stronger phrase; **two of the differences were regressions and are FIXED, and the rest are declared here rather than discovered later.** ⚠ **THIS SECTION EXISTS BECAUSE THE OLD PHRASE WAS AN INSTRUCTION NOT TO LOOK.** A reviewer who reads "byte-identical" skips re-testing the Claude lane, and the phrase was asserted in a header (`runtime/claude/launch-spec.js`) that was itself one of the drifted files.

**FIXED — both converted a swallowed condition into a terminal one:**

1. 🔒 **THE CONTEXT GAUGE IS READ, NOT DISPATCHED (P4-11, 2026-09-23 — this item recorded the swallowed turn-end context dispatch, which is DELETED with its `try/catch`, its injected `log` argument and its `session-model: context dispatch failed` line).** `session-io.js › applyCoreEvents(s, list, dispatch, store)` remembers the runtime's last `context` reading on the session (`s.promptTokens`, `s.promptWindow`, `s.liveModel`) and dispatches nothing for it, so no gauge bug can reach `consume`'s crash path. `session-metrics.js › metrics` is the one reader. 🔒 **CORE HOLDS NO MODEL OR WINDOW TABLE**: `metrics` reports only the window the runtime put on its last `context` reading (none → `null`, raw tokens). A runtime that does not report one supplies its OWN table's answer on the reading — the Claude normalizer calls `events.context(tokens, model, modelTable.contextWindowFor(model))`. A reading that names a DIFFERENT model and carries no window voids the remembered one (another model's window never carries over); a reading with no window for the same model keeps the last. The reducer holds no meter state.
2. 🔒 **THE AUTH SENTINEL'S ANSWER IS THE STOP CONDITION, NOT THE FACT THAT IT WAS ASKED** (`session-query.js › consume`). HEAD read `if (sessionAuth.holdIfAuthMessage(s, msg)) return;` (that function is deleted, P4-03). **`holdIfAuthFailure` answers FALSE without acting in three cases — no bound deps, no session, and `s.settled`** — and the port discarded the return value and returned unconditionally, so a SETTLED session emitting an auth-shaped message stopped draining a stream HEAD kept reading. Settling does not end the child: `holdIfAuthFailure` is the thing that aborts and closes, and it declines on a settled session precisely because the teardown already ran, so returning there abandons a live iterator whose only other exit (`s.query !== q`) a settled-but-not-superseded session never trips. **It reads `if (signal && signal.type === 'auth_hold' && sessionAuth.holdIfAuthFailure(s, signal.text)) return;` on the message path and `if (hold && sessionAuth.holdIfAuthFailure(s, hold.text)) return;` in the catch (re-read 2026-09-23) — the answer is the stop condition on both.**

**DECLARED, AND STILL PRESENT — the list to check before assuming an existing Claude session behaves as it did:**

| # | Site | HEAD | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `claude/loader.js › buildMcpServers` | one custody header, `X-Dopl-Runtime: desktop-session` | **adds `X-Dopl-Vendor: 'claude'`**. Every existing session's MCP requests carry a header they did not, and the server's prose branches on it (§11.0c) |
| 2 | `claude/launch-spec.js › buildOptions` | `allowedTools: cfg.preApproved` | the two agent-ops verbs are pre-approved on every profile, **and a new in-process `dopl_agents` MCP server is mounted**. `main/agent-self-ops.js` DOES NOT EXIST AT HEAD — a feature inside a move. ⚠ **The SHADOW is unchanged; WHERE IT IS DECLARED moved 2026-09-01 — see the rule below** |
| 3 | `runtime/events.js › result` | `Number(msg.total_cost_usd) \|\| 0`, so `Infinity` survived into `s.lastTotalCost` | `Number.isFinite ? total : null` → `0`; non-finite `sessionTokens` clamped where HEAD passed through, and since 2026-09-23 an ABSENT `sessionTokens` is `null` (unmeasured — core moves neither total, CX-02/P4-04) |
| 4 | `runtime/events.js › launched` | `if (typeof msg.model === 'string' && msg.model)` | no string check — **a truthy non-string model now lands in `s.liveModel`** |
| 5 | `session-io.js › applyCoreEvents` (`launched`) | dispatch `launched`, **then** assign `s.liveModel` | assigns `s.liveModel` **before** the synchronous dispatch |
| 6 | `session-gate-reason.js › toolReason` | `(d.BYPASS_TOOLS \|\| []).indexOf(...)` — absent-tolerant, degraded to `'unclassified-tool'` | `d.isClassifiedTool(...)` — **throws** if the injected dep is missing |

**NARRATION — THREE lines changed** (all in `listener.log`; a fourth, `session-model: context dispatch failed`, no longer exists — the dispatch it reported is deleted, item 1 above): `'triage: no SDK —'` → `'triage: no agent runtime —'`; `'no Claude credential on this machine'` → `'no agent-runtime credential on this machine'`; `consume`'s catch now logs the raw error object when there is no `.message`.

- ⚠ **AGENT MANAGEMENT HAS TWO DOORS SINCE 2026-09-01, AND THEY ARE THE SAME TWO VERBS ON THE SAME SUBJECT (Samuel: *"I need you to build out dopl mcp being able to end agents. Dopl MCP need to be able to do all that stuff"*).** `main/agent-self-ops.js` is the IN-PROCESS door — mounted into every spawned session as `mcp__dopl_agents__{rename,end}_agent`. The EXTERNAL door is `dopl_channel(op="end_agent"|"rename_agent")` (§10), which files a `channel_launch_directives` row of kind `end` / `rename` (§6) that this machine claims and dispatches through `main/directive-agent-ops.js`.
  - 🔒 **THE EXTERNAL DOOR IMPLEMENTS NEITHER VERB — IT ROUTES TO THE EXISTING ONE, and that is the constraint on the file rather than a description of it.** `end` → `agent-self-ops.js › endVerdict` then `session-engine.js › controlByTask({action:'end'})`, **the same two calls in the same order** `runtime/claude/axis-b.js`'s in-process `end_agent` makes, bottoming out in the reducer event `sessions:end` and `sessions:delete` also dispatch. `rename` → `agent-self-ops.js › applyRenameTo`, extracted in this wave as the ONE rename write and now shared by all three callers (this lane, `sessions:rename`, the in-process tool). **A second stop path is a second set of teardown bugs** — the sentence `session-reopen.js › controlByTask` already writes about the Agents tab. Pinned at source level in `test/launch-directive-agent-ops.test.mjs`.
  - ⚠ **NEITHER EXTERNAL VERB IS BEHIND THE LAUNCH TOGGLE, AND THAT IS A RULING RECORDED FOR OVERRULING.** §6 carries the argument (a STOP verb and a DISPLAY verb widen nothing; the toggle gates LOCAL COMPUTE BEING SPENT). **TWO LINES IMPLEMENT IT**: the `d.kind === KIND_LAUNCH` test in `launch-directives.js › handle`, and `› refresh` binding realtime on `armed` rather than on the toggle. **The own-operator bound is unchanged and is still the whole fence.**
  - ⚠ **SELF-END STAYS REFUSED IN-PROCESS AND DOES NOT ARISE EXTERNALLY.** `agent-self-ops.js` refuses it because the dispatch would abort the CALLING turn mid-tool-call, so the result could never be delivered and the call would read as a hang. An EXTERNAL caller is not a desktop agent, holds no instance id, and is not mid-turn on this machine — so `directive-agent-ops.js` hands `endVerdict` an empty caller id, which makes the `self` branch UNREACHABLE rather than absent. **One verdict table, not two.**
  - ⚠ **A RENAME CONSULTS NO REGISTRY, ON EITHER DOOR.** `agent-names.js` is keyed by the INSTANCE ADDRESS and outlives the session object on purpose (an idle park, a lazy resume and a crash resume all replace it). Requiring a live session would make a name un-settable at exactly the moments a session is being rebuilt.

The constants (`UNIVERSAL_HARD_DENY`, `CHANNEL_AGENT_HARD_DENY`, `DENIED_BUILTINS`, `READ_BUILTINS`, `WEB_TOOLS`, `DOPL_SAFE_TOOLS`, …) stay — the adapters' tool configs read them. **This is a containment claim — verify it before relying on it.** Under `full` (`runtime/claude/launch-spec.js › buildOptions`):

(it named the retired headless lane and session window until 2026-09-23).

Measured against the bundled binary (claude 2.1.220 / claude-agent-sdk 0.3.220): the init message's `mcp_servers` held **12 entries, 9 of them connectors** — Slack, Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Figma, Granola, Notion, Attio, Dopl. **A construction argument is only as wide as the constructor, and this one enumerated our own option set as if it were the child's whole world.**
    - ⚠ **`settingSources: []` IS WHAT REMOVED THE OFF SWITCH.** The CLI's own kill switch is the `disableClaudeAiConnectors` **setting**, and our isolation is precisely what stops it being read. **Tightening the sandbox deleted the control.** The surviving lever is the process env, set at the one assembly point: `runtime/claude/loader.js › buildScrubbedEnv` writes `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS='0'` **last and unconditionally**, so an inherited value cannot re-admit the lane. ⚠ **THE NAME IS INVERTED AND EMPTY IS A NO-OP** — the binary tests "explicitly set falsy" (`['0','false','no','off']`), so `''`, `'1'` and unset all leave it ON. **Do not "clear" this var.** Measured the same day: unset → 9 connectors, `''` → 9, `'0'` → 0, `'false'` → 0, with the `dopl` entry untouched in every case.

What it cost was an **inventory of the operator's connected accounts inside a prompt that can be auto-sent**, and per-turn tokens across every live session. **`prompt-framing-text.js › LANE_EXCLUSIVITY`** is the belt for the day the env var stops working: it tells the agent `mcp__dopl__dopl_channel` is the only path off the machine and that no other `mcp__` server is its lane. ⚠ **Deny-on-unclassified (R3b) was considered and DEFERRED** — the gate already holds, and turning an allow-list into a deny-list is a change to make deliberately, not as a side effect of this one.
