  - 🔒 **`full` IS BOUNDED ON THE OFFER, AND THE BOUND IS DERIVED FROM AXIS A — NEVER HAND-WRITTEN (2026-09-02, A5).** `runtime/claude/tools.js › FULL_BUILTIN_BOUND` is `BYPASS_TOOLS` minus the `mcp__dopl__*` names (`options.tools` bounds BUILT-INS only), i.e. **exactly the set some Axis-A mode can allow** — measured 17 names on 2026-09-02, asserted BY NAME on the wire in `test/session-builtin-bound.test.mjs`, not by comparing the constant to itself. ⚠ **IT IS OFFERED SURFACE, NOT A FENCE, AND READING IT AS A RE-NARROWING OF `full` IS THE MISTAKE THIS BULLET EXISTS TO STOP.** The hard-deny is still `SESSION_HARD_DENY` and nothing else, every built-in F-177 released still resolves `gate` rather than `deny`, and nothing new is pre-approved. **What it removes is CONTEXT**: `builtinTools: []` meant NO bound, so `full` carried every built-in the CLI ships — measured 29 tools / **87,402 chars of tool schema per turn**, `Workflow` alone 21,332 — of which only the classified ones could ever run, because an unclassified name gates in every mode and a windowless gate DENIES. ⚠ **DERIVING IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART**: a fourth hand-maintained list would drift from the three above it, and the drift's face is a tool the mode picker says runs and the model never sees. ⚠ **AND `Agent` / `Skill` COME OFF WITH IT — a POSTURE DEFAULT RECORDED FOR OVERRULING**: they are what injects the OPERATOR'S PERSONAL Claude Code agent and skill catalogue into every Dopl agent turn (8,322 ch measured 2026-09-02, the F-268 class, and it breaks cross-machine prompt-cache identity), and Dopl's sanctioned delegation path is `dopl_channel(op="manage", action="launch")`. **One line re-offers them; making them RUNNABLE is a second, separate decision.**

- ⚠ **AN ENDED AGENT IS DEAD, AND ITS RECORD LIVES SEVEN DAYS (2026-08-22, Samuel's ruling). THIS SUPERSEDES THE `MAX_ENDED` COUNT BOUND AND THE ABANDONMENT-ONLY RULE BELOW.**
  - **THE RULE HAS BEEN WRONG TWICE, SILENTLY, WHICH IS WHY THE HISTORY IS KEPT.** *v1*: a pill survived exactly as long as its WINDOW. *v2* (2026-08-20, F-234): every session went WINDOWLESS, so `keepWindow === true && windowAlive(s.win)` was false on every end and NOTHING was retained — an agent that finished vanished with no record it had run. The fix made retention unconditional on the caller's flag, bounded by `MAX_ENDED` (12), and **refused a TIME bound** because *"did anything ever have this on screen"* has no answer without a window. *v3* rules the time bound IN, and v2's objection is void: the question is no longer about a window.

The final MEASUREMENT is frozen with it (a live read would blank every number at exactly the moment the operator wants to know what the run cost).

It drops local stores only and cannot touch a LIVE session (the SPA ends those first).

What goes: the five swept stores (via `agent-retention.js › forgetAgent`), the display name (`agent-names.js › clear`, keyed by the id the sweep cannot reach), and any open agent window (`agent-window.js › closeAgentWindow` — main-only, never a bridge op). ⚠ **`agentId` IS REQUIRED HERE AND OPTIONAL ON EVERY OTHER OP IN THE FAMILY:** an omitted id resolves to the OLDEST live agent on the thread, which for a DESTRUCTIVE verb is a different agent than the card that was clicked with nothing reporting the swap. Refusals: a bare `{ok:false}` for a bad payload (byte-identical to the sender refusal), `{ok:false, reason:'no-agent'}` for an address naming neither a live nor a retained agent. Pinned by `test/agent-delete.test.mjs`.
  - ⚠ **⚠ DELETION IS LOCAL; THE CHANNEL RECORD IS IMMUTABLE BY IT.** `sessions:delete` reaches no network and no server store — everything the agent POSTED is `channel_messages`, the shared record owned by the channel, and the transcript keeps every message **attributed exactly as before**: the agent's id rides the MESSAGE (`channels/components/agents-model.ts › parseAgentPostStamp`, off `client_msg_id`) and never a local table, so a deleted agent's rows still read as its rows ("New Agent" since the id fallback was withdrawn). **The only server-visible effect is the one an ordinary `end` already has** — the session projects as `ended`, a peer-facing fact rather than local history, and this lane neither suppresses nor repeats that report (the row then leaves the wire by omission, `liveForWire`). ⚠ **THE DISPLAY NAME IS DESTROYED WITH THE AGENT** (Samuel: *"all information attached"*), so a renamed agent's transcript rows fall back to "New Agent" (the `Agent #<id>` fallback is withdrawn, below) — the identity survives, the local label does not. - 🔒 **THE RAW AGENT ID IS NEVER USER-VISIBLE (Samuel, 2026-08-27; SHARPENED 2026-09-15).** An agent id is an eight-character machine token (`main/agent-id.js`, `^[a-z][a-z0-9]{7}$`). **Every surface that shows an agent shows its DISPLAY NAME** — `agents-model-identity.ts › agentDisplayName` (§1-split out of `agents-model.ts`, which re-exports it), which resolves the operator's own name from `main/agent-names.js` and falls back to **`New Agent`** (`shared/lib/agent-name.ts › NEW_AGENT_NAME` — ONE constant, read by the channels tree, the transcript pill and the Home board's SERVER projection, because all three had their own copy).

What changed is that agents are now TOLD not to write it (`main/prompt-framing-self.js`, `channel-doctrine.ts`): *"they don't need to be telling that or posting the id in the channel, in fact its a bad user experience."*

A failed send RESTORES them — a receipt taken and dropped is one this machine forgot it owed, and nothing ever asks again.

It is a STAMP rather than a clear-on-handover **because a clear has to be triggered by something that notices** — and the branch that would have done the clearing also runs on the FIRST cycle of a run, where there is no previous operator and a real receipt would be destroyed. A's receipts SURVIVE B's push and are still there if A signs back in.

The ladder is **15s / 30s / 60s / 120s / 300s, then 300s indefinitely** (`› RETRY_BACKOFF_MS`); a REAL state change CLEARS it and runs at once (`main/session-state-push.js › schedule`, whose `fromRetry` flag is what stops the retry's own re-run resetting itself into a fixed 15s poll). **ONLY A FAILURE THAT MAY ANSWER DIFFERENTLY ARMS IT** — `› send` answers `'retry'` for a network throw (the aborted fetch) or an exhausted 429/5xx and `false` for a 4xx, because re-posting a bad payload forever is `ui-sync`'s ~39 000-attempt storm with a longer period, and the wire filters are that shape's fix. ⚠ **A MACHINE WHOSE PUSHES LAND HOLDS NO TIMER, which is why this is NOT the keepalive refused in F-294**: it is armed by a FAILURE and never by a clock, so the steady-state write rate is still a state change's. ⚠ **THE DIGEST RULE IS UNCHANGED AND IS WHAT MAKES A RETRY SAFE** — nothing is recorded on a failed push, so the re-run re-derives the CURRENT projection and can never replay a stale set. ⚠ **WHAT IT REPLACES IS THE SENTENCE "the session's next real state change is the retry"**, which was true of a SESSION and false of the BOOT RECONCILE CYCLE (`main/shell-mode.js › startSessionStatePush` kicks one, 2026-09-13): on 2026-09-14 01:02 a boot that quietly ended 65 stale records and re-parked one had its single cycle aborted by a slow local API, had no next state change to wait for, and left the PREVIOUS run's 13 `idle` rows standing — the Overview agents panel, the Agents tab and every peer's `read_sessions` read ended agents as Idle for the whole run (Samuel: *"why do i see so many agents in the overview … i should not see ended agents"*). `dopl-desktop-app/test/session-state-push-retry.test.mjs` (ten cases; the ladder, the reset, and that a clean cycle arms nothing).

Losing the CAS is a normal no-op.
  - **CRASH SAFETY: a claimed-but-undecided directive is LEFT TO LAZY-EXPIRE, deliberately.** A restarted process cannot tell whether the spawn happened, so `refused` would be unsupportable and `launched` would name an agent that may not exist. **An expiry is the only honest terminal state for an outcome nobody observed**, and the orchestrator already handles expiry. ⚠ **THE BREAKER-OPEN BACKSTOP WORKS — F-273 IS CLOSED (2026-08-22) AND THIS BULLET SAID OTHERWISE UNTIL 2026-08-23 (F-291).** `src/app/api/channels/launch-directives/route.ts › handleGet` is the pending-directives read, an authed collection GET over `src/features/channels/server/service-launch.ts › listPendingLaunchDirectives`, fenced on `operator_user_id` and answering `{ directives }` — the envelope and the path `main/launch-directive-wire.js › ROUTES` had already guessed, so no desktop repoint was needed. ⚠ **AND THE DTO CARRIES `operatorUserId` (F-284)**: without it, `main/launch-directives.js › handle`'s local owner re-check compared every POLLED row against `''` and dropped it, so the read returned rows nothing could action while the poll looked healthy. ⚠ **`› pollWorkspace`'s 404 SELF-DISABLE IS RETAINED ON PURPOSE and is NOT dead-code cleanup**: it is the older-deployment degradation (§13 — an older peer is supported), and against such a server realtime remains the only delivery path.
- 🔒 **AN ABORT ON THE CHANNEL LOOP IS TWO DIFFERENT EVENTS, AND THE DISCRIMINATOR IS OWNERSHIP** (2026-08-30). `main/listener-budget.js › isWakeAbort` answers it: `channelLoop`'s own per-iteration `AbortController` is aborted ONLY by `io.wakeEntry` (a realtime INSERT) and `wake()` (powerMonitor), while the fetch budget aborts `listener-io.js › sendOnce`'s separate private controller — so "did OUR signal fire" is exactly "was this a wake". **A wake re-awaits at once; anything else — our own expired budget, a network error — takes the capped-exponential ladder.**
  - ⚠ **THE OLD SINGLE `continue` WAS TRUE OF THE HELD POLL ONLY.** There `AWAIT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (58s) deliberately outlives the server's 50s hold, so the server always answers first and an abort really was a wake. On the CHEAP path `CHEAP_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (15s) sits UNDER a route whose own ceiling is `maxDuration = 60`, so a merely SLOW server blows our budget mid-work — and a zero-delay re-poll then sets the loop's rate to the SERVER'S LATENCY instead of the 45s idle. Self-sustaining, never backing off: 22 watched channels went from one poll per 45s each to one per 15s each, permanently. **A budget expiry now leaves a `await budget expired` line in `listener.log`; it left nothing before.**
- 🔒 **`timeoutMs=1` IN THE SERVER LOG IS THE PUSH TRANSPORT WORKING, NOT A COLLAPSED BUDGET.** `REALTIME.CHEAP_AWAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` is the smallest value `AwaitQuerySchema`'s `.positive()` accepts, chosen so a healthy socket gets a single-DB-read catch-up with no held serverless function, paired with the wake-interruptible `LONG_IDLE_MS` (45s). It has been 1 since 2026-07-28 (`1f76730c`). **`main/listener-budget.js › AWAIT_TIMEOUT_FLOOR_MS` is therefore 1 and must stay 1** — raising it breaks the push transport rather than repairing it, and `test/listener-cheap-await.test.mjs › "FLOOR: timeoutMs=1 is the DESIGN"` exists to stop the next reader "fixing" it. ⚠ **The MCP server's `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/channel-hold-budget.ts` is a DIFFERENT deadline chain for `dopl_channel(op="await")`; the desktop imports none of it.**
  - **The FETCH floor is the one with teeth:** a falsy fetch budget makes `sendOnce` skip its AbortController timer entirely (`timeoutMs ? setTimeout(…) : null`), so ONE hung request holds that channel's loop for the life of the process — and a loop that never returns never logs. `FETCH_TIMEOUT_FLOOR_MS` = 1_000.
- 🔒 **THE PRESENCE LOOP IS A PURE FACTORY (`main/presence-core.js`) BEHIND A WIRING ADAPTER (`main/presence.js`), AND THE SPLIT IS WHAT MADE IT TESTABLE AT ALL** (2026-09-08). `presence.js` requires `./api` → `./auth` → `electron`, so the module carrying the operator's own online dot was the one module `node --test` could not import — and it had **no test** until the rework. Every clock, the transport, `isSignedIn` and the idle reading are injected; `test/presence-core.test.mjs` drives real timeouts, real aborts and a real 30-minute idle. The adapter holds nothing but the bindings and the `powerMonitor` wiring. **The rule the loop implements, and the four defects it fixed, are §7** — do not restate them here.
  - **THE SLEEP HALF OF `powerMonitor` IS WIRED IN `presence.js › armSleepEvents` (`suspend` / `lock-screen` / `shutdown`), THE WAKE HALF STAYS IN `main/wake.js`.** ⚠ **DELIBERATELY NOT BOTH IN ONE PLACE**: `wake.js` already owns `resume` + `unlock-screen` and COALESCES the pair (they fire together), and it reaches presence through `listener.wake()`. Wiring resume a second time here would give the machine two uncoordinated wake paths — the exact shape `wake.js` was split out of `index.js` to end. The three sleep events had no owner, so they are wired at the point of use.
  - ⚠ **AN UNMEASURABLE IDLE TIME READS `active`, NEVER `away`.** `powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime()` throws on a headless/CI Electron; answering `away` there would put every such machine permanently offline. **The app being OPEN is the base fact of the Slack rule** — idle only ever demotes a fact that could be measured.
  - **QUIT POSTS `away`, AND `quit-guard.js › teardown` BOUNDS IT.** `channel-listener.js › stop()` now RETURNS `presence.stop()`'s post (its own 3s leash) and the teardown races it inside `FLUSH_DEADLINE_MS` alongside the final session-state push. ⚠ **The two are `allSettled` and reported separately, never `Promise.all`-ed** — a hung `away` must not make a landed flush log as skipped. Without this, quitting left the operator reading ONLINE on every peer's roster for up to four beats.
  - ⚠ **`main/api.js › sendOnce` FORWARDS A CALLER `signal` INTO ITS OWN TIMEOUT CONTROLLER** (added for abort-not-skip). `AbortSignal.any` is not available on every Electron this app still runs on, so it is a listener that is ALWAYS removed in `finally` — `fetchWithAuthRepair` calls that thunk twice on a 401, and a retained listener on a long-lived controller is a leak.
- 🔒 **AN UNREAD `fetch` RESPONSE MUST BE RELEASED, AND THE SUCCESS BRANCH IS NOT EXEMPT** (2026-08-30). Node's `fetch` in Electron main is undici: until the body is consumed or cancelled the request counts as IN FLIGHT, its socket is never returned to the pool, and the next call opens another connection. What is retained is **native** — socket buffers plus TLS state — so it never pressures GC, never shows in a heap snapshot, and appears only as RSS. **`main/api-repair.js › discardBody` is the ONE helper**; it is best-effort by construction (an already-read, absent or throwing body must not escape into a caller that had finished with the response). ⚠ **THE LEAKING BRANCHES ARE THE ERROR BRANCHES**, which is backwards from where anyone looks — the success path calls `res.json()`, while `if (!res.ok) { … return; }` is the path a saturated server puts every caller on at once. Applied at the three highest-frequency seams (`channel-listener.js › channelLoop`, `presence-core.js › post` — ⚠ **it was `presence.js`'s `beatOnce` until the 2026-09-08 presence rework split the loop into a pure core**, the pre-retry 401 in `fetchWithAuthRepair`) and, in the failing-auth wave later the same day, at the six next by measured rate — `ui-bridge.js › performApiRequest`, `listener-io.js › listWorkspaces` + `› listChannels`, `consent.js › pollStatus`, `session-state-push.js › send` (**success branch included**) and `version-gate.js › fetchFloor`; **the remaining sites are open debt — REFACTOR-FINDINGS F-353**, and `mcp-config.js › withTimeout` is F-362 because it abandons a response by CONSTRUCTION rather than on a branch. Pinned by `test/unread-body-seams.test.mjs`, which also asserts nobody re-implements the helper privately.
- **The listener's member cache is BOUNDED** (`main/listener-people.js › MAX_CACHED_MEMBERS` = 1000, oldest-out through `› cacheMember`; the module was the listener's identity module until 2026-09-23, and only `nameCache` remains — the avatar-URL cache had no reader and was deleted 2026-09-23). Until 2026-08-30 `nameCache` and `avatarUrlCache` were the only structures in `main/` with no cap, no TTL, no `delete` and no sweep. ⚠ **Oldest-out rather than LRU is correct HERE because `refreshNameCache` rewrites every member it sees once per reconcile**, so insertion order IS "last seen": a still-watched workspace's members are re-inserted continuously and one the operator left never is. A miss is not a failure — `displayNameFor` answers `'A teammate'`.
- ⚠ **`MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS = 15`** (`main/session-windowless.js`), **RAISED 6 → 15 ON 2026-09-01 (Samuel's ruling).** The orchestrator-spawns-workers model makes six a ceiling an orchestrator hits with its own staff running; `main/agent-self-ops.js › end_agent` (2026-08-31) is the release valve that lets an agent hand a slot back, and the 17 GB narration incident that made the memory argument bite is closed by `session-narration.js › RING_CHAR_BUDGET`. **The multiplicative-cost rule below is UNCHANGED and still governs** — what changed is that the binding limiter is now N live SDK child processes and API spend, neither of which this constant bounds. Previously **corrected 2026-08-20 — this bullet said `= 4` in `main/session-pool.js`, and was wrong about the number, the file AND the mechanism.** `session-pool.js` was the `claude -p` HEADLESS pool, deleted with its lane the same day (§11's executor bullet says so twelve lines down, so this section contradicted itself); its guard was 4, while the windowless engine enforced a SEPARATE 6 under a window's name (`settings.MAX_SESSION_WINDOWS`). The surviving ceiling took the name this bullet already used for it, at the value the engine was really enforcing. **It IS a COST ceiling, not just a concurrency one: every per-session bound is MULTIPLICATIVE against it** (the narration ring, the pending-inbound queue, the retained-ended set, the gated-body ledger), so raising it is a memory decision.
  - ⚠ **AND `session-park.js › startResume` ENFORCES IT SINCE 2026-08-22 — IT DID NOT, AND THE GAP WAS EXACTLY ONE SESSION WIDE (F-272).** It guarded `hasLiveSession(slot)` ("is THIS slot taken") and never `liveCount`, so a machine at all six could resume a **seventh**; the reachable producer is `offerResume`'s crash-scan notification, which the operator may click at any moment. Now checked **before `getSdk` and again after it**, for the same check-then-act reason `launch()` re-checks its own guard.
    - **ENFORCED RATHER THAN DOCUMENTED AS +1 HEADROOM, and the decision is deliberate.** The case for headroom is that a resume RESTORES work already started — but a resumed session costs a full `claude` child exactly like a fresh one, this is a COST ceiling (above), and **a documented +1 is not a bound**: nothing would have stopped a second crash record resuming at 7, then 8. ⚠ **Samuel ruled the number stays at 6 for the multi-machine wave**, and one lane quietly exceeding it is that ruling overridden by an omission.
    - **The refusal shape is the function's existing `false`** and the vocabulary is `launch()`'s `cap`, said in the diag line — `startResume` answers a boolean, and widening it to a skip shape would change a contract two callers read for no gain. **Settled registry entries do not count** (`liveCount` counts unsettled), which is what keeps a crash resume of a just-ended session from being refused by the guard meant to bound live ones.
- 🔒 **SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-09-22 — READ THIS FIRST.** The Claude pick rule is `open` (`runtime/claude/models.js › descriptor.pick`, a GRAMMAR, `PICK_PATTERN`), not the closed `MODEL_IDS` list; `runtime/selection-vocabulary.js › pickOf` is vocabulary-free (only absent / `default` step aside; it replaced the core `chainModel` 2026-09-23); the launch spec spends `models.js › launchArg` — the LIVE roster row's own `value` — not `modelArg`'s five aliases; the durable session record keeps any grammar-valid id (`session-store.js › durableSessionRecord`), absent `''`; and an unknown pick REFUSES (launch: `no-model`; live switch: `reason: 'no-model'`) instead of clearing to the fallback. `runtime/claude/model-table.js › MODEL_IDS` (and the alias map behind `› aliasForModelId`) survive as the Claude adapter's FAILED-READ fallback and as legacy spellings; `MODEL_CHOICES`, `normalizeModelId`, `normalizeModel` and `modelArg` are deleted with the core module (2026-09-23). And since 2026-09-23 no launch record stores a model at all (§5, §11.0e) — the "durable posture carries `model`" sub-bullet below is history. The bullets below are the 2026-08-22 design and are true only where they do not contradict this.
- ⚠ **AGENT MODEL SELECTION (2026-08-22, Samuel's ruling) — TWO FROZEN VOCABULARIES, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM REACHES `argv`.** The operator picks a model per channel; their agents run on it. The ruling names the values as FULL IDS and the SPA renders exactly those, while this tree's picker was already a frozen list of ALIASES — deliberately, because an alias is version-stable and a shipped build does not go stale the week a new model lands. Both are right about different things, so the Claude table (then core's, now `main/runtime/claude/model-table.js`) held BOTH lists and one map:
  - **`MODEL_IDS`** = `claude-fable-5` · `claude-opus-5` · `claude-sonnet-5` · `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`. What a UI offers and what the durable posture STORES, so an operator's pick round-trips through the bridge unchanged and a select can show what it set.
  - **`MODEL_CHOICES`** (deleted 2026-09-23 with `normalizeModel`) = what could become `--model <argv>`. `aliasForModelId` is the seam; `normalizeModel` accepts BOTH and always answers in the alias vocabulary, so a caller holding either does not have to know which the layer below wants. **The adapter's `buildOptions` re-coerced as the last gate before a child process could see it.** ⚠ The map is LOSSY in one place, stated rather than discovered: the dated haiku id resolves to the `haiku` alias, so the value reaching the child is not byte-identical to the pick.
  - **THE DURABLE POSTURE CARRIES `model` BESIDE THE TWO AXES — a third FIELD, never a third AXIS.** It rides the same record because it is the same decision (what MY agent starts as when I press Launch) but it grants nothing and reaches no gate; `grantDecision` never reads a model. ⚠ **IT VALIDATES SOFT WHERE THE AXES VALIDATE HARD:** an unknown value on either axis rejects the WHOLE write, an unknown model is simply ABSENT (a MISSING KEY, never `''`), which is the SDK default and is what an unset channel already does. Failing the write would mean a desktop that has not heard of a newer model could not store a posture at all.

The model's SECOND reader (`getLaunchModel`, which let the peer-triggered lane inherit the channel's model) is DELETED (2026-09-23): the responder lane names no model and the funnel gives it the runtime default.

(2026-09-23: `DesktopNarrationEntry` itself now lives in `src/shared/lib/spa-bridge-narration.ts › DesktopNarrationEntry`, re-exported by both.) 🔒 **TWO BRIDGE DECLARATIONS, NOT THREE (P9-08, 2026-09-23):** the preload (`renderer/app-preload.js`, ground truth) and `src/shared/lib/spa-bridge*.ts`. The preload no longer exposes `sendMagicLink` (no SPA caller).

The seams are reason-to-change, like `session-park.js` / `session-gate.js` / `session-launch.js` before them:

NEVER AS NOTHING (F-694, 2026-09-13).** `main/session-boot.js › reparkDormant`, reached from `main/session-engine.js › init` in one line before `store.pruneRecords`. For every stored record whose `session-store.js › reloadDisposition` is **`'dormant'`**: with an `sdkSessionId` in the resume map, on a runtime `runtime/capability.js › resumeRefusal` clears, the parked session object is REBUILT in the engine's registry from the record (`› parkedSessionFromRecord`, in the shape `session-park.js › resumeParked` expects) — so `session-summary.js` publishes it, `session-pill.js › queryTornDown` reads the `parked` flag as the **Idle** pill with `listening: false`, `session-state-push.js` re-projects its `channel_sessions` row, and the next addressed message wakes it down the EXISTING lazy path. **Anything else takes the interrupted-END route** — `setRecordPhase('ended')` + the `task_failed {interrupted}` lifecycle + an `agent-history.js › record` entry, which is the half that makes an **Ended card exist at all** (`session-summary.js` reads its ended set from that file). **No third state.** ⚠ **AND ONLY INSIDE A 24h RECENCY WINDOW (amended 2026-09-13, hours after the rule above shipped).** `session-boot.js › REPARK_WINDOW_MS`, measured against the record's most recent of `parkedAt` / `lastActivityAt` / `startedAt` (`› recordFreshness`; **no usable stamp is OLD**, never unknown-means-recent) — a dormant record outside it is **ENDED**, down the same interrupted route, never revived. The first build without the window revived **66** parked records on Samuel's machine, 63 of them older than a week and the oldest 46 days: the F-694 bug had itself been leaving restart-killed agents at `phase: 'parked'` forever, so the first honest read of that phase resurrected months of agents he considered ended ("that's kind of a serious issue"). `store.pruneRecords` never swept them either — `protectedRecord` retains any key with an sdk id. The stamp is written at BOTH park writes (`session-store.js › stampParked`, `setRecordPhase`), because a park path that forgets it leaves an agent dormant-since-`startedAt`. ⚠ **AND AN INTERRUPTED END SAYS ONLY "Ended"** (Samuel, 2026-09-13: "We don't need that line to be there … We can just put 'ended.' We don't need to give a reason why"). `session-effects.js › TERMINAL_BODIES.interrupted` is the word, `agent-bits.tsx › AgentEndedPill` is the same word, and `endInterrupted` records **`diag: null`** so the card carries no red reason line under it. The `{ interrupted: true }` flag is untouched — the copy changed, not the machine-readable half, and a real failure (`mcp-connect-guard.js`) still writes a `diag` because it says something the operator cannot otherwise know (F-692). `test/session-boot-repark.test.mjs`, `test/session-store.test.mjs`.

Measured 2026-09-13: a Dopl channel agent idle across a hard Electron restart was gone from the Agents tab entirely, with its record still on disk.
  - ⚠ **IT IS NOT `startSession`, AND THAT IS FOUR SEPARATE REASONS** (`parkedSessionFromRecord`'s own docblock carries them): the runtime stamp needs an async probe per record, the windowless credential preflight **rolls back with `sessions.delete`** on a signed-out machine — the same invisibility by a second door — a fresh `sessionId` + restamped `startedAt` would destroy the record's identity and its Agents-tab time bucket by the act of restoring it, and it resolves avatars. **Three fields cannot come off the record and are stated rather than discovered:** `nonce` is minted fresh (never persisted; `startResume` does the same and the SDK resume carries the original ROLE block), `awaitingDirective` is **false** (this agent has a conversation and has already been directed — unlike a spawn-idle shell, which `session-gate.js › feedInbound`'s belt fences on that flag), and `operatorUserId` is **null, which is FAIL-CLOSED**: the record carries no owner and `setSelfIdentity` has not run at `init()`, so `session-reopen.js › messageByTask` refuses a DIRECTED 1:1 until the session has actually resumed. ⚠ **THE PUSH IS UNAFFECTED** — `session-state-push.js › trackOrigin` stamps origin from the live push identity per key, not from that field.
  - ⚠ **A RUNTIME THAT REFUSES RESUME ENDS THE RECORD HERE, AND THIS DOES NOT TOUCH THE LIVE RULE ABOVE.** `resumeParked` still refuses IN PLACE and leaves a RUNNING session parked for the next wake; a refusal is a fact about the BUILD, so a re-parked pill on such a runtime would be Idle forever — visible, addressable and silently unwakeable, which is the third state this pass exists to forbid. **The cost, stated:** `reloadDisposition('ended')` is `'ignore'`, so a later build that verifies the meter cannot revive what this ended.
  - ⚠ **A RECORD WITH NO SDK ID IS THE ORDINARY CASE, NOT A CORRUPTION** — a SPAWN-IDLE agent ("New Agent") never started a query, so nothing ever reported a conversation id for it, and the record carries neither its launch goal nor its identity body. There is nothing to rebuild it from, so it gets an Ended card with a readable reason.
  - ⚠ **THE TWO RECORD READERS ARE SHARED, NEVER COPIED.** `session-park.js` exports `contextFromRecord` and `knownProfile` for this lane (`test/request-strip-park.test.mjs` pins that list positively, and neither mints a window). `knownProfile` is the fail-restrictive one: a raw stored profile falls through `tool-profiles.js › normalizeProfile`'s global fallback and comes back at FULL access, from the least trustworthy input there is — so a THIRD spelling of that set is the dangerous drift, not a tidy one.
  - ⚠ **THE WINDOWLESS MESSAGE FLOOR APPLIES (F-236) AND THE ABANDONMENT TIMER IS ARMED.** A rehydrated session has no accept surface, so an axis left at the reducer's `ask` makes `session-gate.js › enqueue` HOLD the peer's next reply with nothing able to release it; and `scheduleIdle` is called for the reason the spawn-idle lane calls it — `session-state.js › idleTimeout` reads `parked === true` and answers the ABANDONMENT bound, so an agent nobody comes back to ends on its own instead of holding a slot forever.
- **PER-MESSAGE DESKTOP NOTIFICATIONS ARE RETIRED. THE MENTION IS THE ESCALATION; THE TAGS INBOX IS THE RECORD (2026-08-18, wiring plan Phase 7).** Agent/thread activity raises an OS banner ONLY when the message's SERVER-STAMPED `metadata.mentionedUserIds` names this operator (§5). One predicate decides it, `main/targeting.js › mentionsMe`, and it has exactly TWO readers on the `isChatIntent` precedent: `classify`'s `fyi` verdict, and `main/listener-messages.js`'s dispatch arm for `task-reply`. **A second copy of the comparison is the bug** — that is how two readers came to disagree about one post before.
  - **THREE THINGS NOTIFY, AND NOTHING ELSE DOES PER MESSAGE.** (1) an **addressed** request — `to_user_id === me` → `trigger` → `consent.notifyInbound`, **deliberately NOT mention-gated**, because a request is a decision somebody is waiting on and the consent → launch flow depends on that notification arriving; (2) a message that **@-tags me** → `trigger.js › sendFyi`, which NARROWED rather than died and whose copy is now author-kind neutral ("<name> mentioned you"), because **human-to-human mentions notify on the same terms and a DM notifies when you are tagged**; (3) a **thread reply that @-tags me** → `task-notify.js › notifyTaskReply`. Everything else — an agent narrating turn after turn, a courtesy no-op, a peer's chat line, a reply in my own thread that names nobody — is silent on the desktop and fully present on the web.
  - ⚠ **THE GATE FAILS TOWARD SILENCE, ON PURPOSE.** An absent key means "tags nobody", which is the shape of every row written before Phase 6, and a non-array value reads the same way. A missed banner is recoverable from the Tags inbox; a banner nobody can stop is not, and a throw inside `dispatchMessage` is a DEFERRAL that holds the channel's cursor.
  - ⚠ **DO NOT REINSTATE ANY PART OF `myNotifyScope` (F-170).** There is a real per-message mute in the product again, which makes "quiet in this one channel" look like a feature that already existed. It did not: two of its three options did not do what their labels said. A quiet-in-one-channel control is a NEW design, not a revival.
  - ⚠ **SHIP-ORDERED (§13), one-way:** the WEB half (Phase 6's stamping) must be live before this desktop build ships. An old desktop against the new server keeps notifying exactly as it does today — noisy and safe. A new desktop against an old server sees no stamped mention set anywhere and goes silent, which is the direction that breaks.
- **THE PERSISTED CURSOR MOVES ONLY PAST A MESSAGE WHOSE DISPATCH LANDED.** The per-page loop lives beside the dispatch it gates; `dispatchMessage` returns a **deferral REASON, falsy = handled**. A held cursor is bounded (8 attempts ≈ 4 min) then a LOUD escape — retrying forever trades a bounded announced loss for an unbounded silent stall of every later message.
- **QUIT DOES NOT ORPHAN `claude` CHILDREN.** `main/quit-guard.js` NAMES the threads a quit would interrupt (title + channel, never a count alone), ends each through the calm `inactive` terminal so the peer is told, and RACES one final state-push flush against `FLUSH_DEADLINE_MS` (1500 ms, verified 2026-08-11) rather than awaiting a 15s HTTP budget. **The kill predicate is "holds a live child" (`session-reopen.js › liveChildSessions`, `!settled && !parked`), NOT the pill state** — a session between turns reads `idle` and still owns a process; a PARKED shell (including a spawn-idle "New Agent") owns none and rehydrates from its durable record, so it is excluded and the dialog never calls it permanent. **Every path fails OPEN.**
- **QUITTING WITH LIVE AGENTS CONFIRMS FIRST, AND THE CONFIRMATION HAS A REAL CANCEL** (2026-08-30, Samuel's ruling). `main/quit-guard.js › buildDialogOptions` offers **three** buttons — `Quit anyway` / `Wait for them to finish` / `Cancel` — and the copy states the consequence as PERMANENT (`quitDetailTail`, singular/plural aware). **`Cancel` takes both `defaultId` and `cancelId`**, so Return and Escape do nothing. `cancelQuit` aborts outright: no teardown, no `disarmed` latch (the next quit re-prompts), any pending wait stopped, and **`app.isQuitting` set back to `false`**. ⚠ **Cancel must be CHOSEN, never fallen into** — a throwing or malformed dialog still resolves to `BUTTON_QUIT`, because a broken dialog must not become an app that cannot be closed. Zero live sessions still quits silently with no dialog.
- **All THREE auth legs arm `beginPendingAuth({ requireState: true })`** — browser OAuth (`main/auth-actions.js`), in-process password adoption and the magic link (`main/auth-password.js`). **The gate fails closed in BOTH directions:** a fragment echoing a state may spend ONLY the record carrying that exact nonce (a mismatch matches nothing and does NOT fall back to presence+TTL), and a state-less fragment may spend only a record that does not require one — of which nothing writes any more.
- ⚠ **SHIP-ORDER GATE, one-way: the state-echoing WEB deploy must be LIVE before the new desktop build ships.** Never the reverse, never the same window without confirming the web half landed first.
- **"Signed in" = the encrypted blob OR a fresh cookie identity.** `isSignedIn()` stays SYNC; `ensureSignedIn()` is the ASYNC gate for the two boot callers that can await.
  - 🔒 ⚠ **…AND NOT WHEN NOTHING CAN BE STORED (2026-08-30).** That rule assumed the blob is STALE, hence repairable from the jar. With `safeStorage` unavailable it is IMPOSSIBLE — `persist()` refuses AND deletes the keys — and `auth.refreshInner()` reads its refresh token from that blob, so nothing on the machine can rotate the jar's JWT either. A cookie session then buys one hour of an unrenewable credential followed by every cookie lane 401ing forever. `signedInFrom` takes **`canPersist`** (`auth-store.js › encryptionAvailable`, read LIVE, never latched) and answers `signedIn:false`, `source:'storage-unavailable'`, **`needsRefresh:false`** — re-probing cannot change an answer that turns on the keychain, and re-probing is what made it a storm. ⚠ **UNKNOWN IS PERMISSIVE HERE**, deliberately against the house default: only an explicit `canPersist:false` narrows, so every caller that predates the input keeps the Q4 table. ⚠ **Recovery is by GESTURE, never by poll** — an explicit sign-in re-enters `persist()` and re-asks the OS; a background probe doing the same would re-prompt the operator forever. Pinned by `test/auth-storage-unavailable.test.mjs`.
- 🔒 **A 401 THAT SURVIVED A FORCED ROTATION IS LATCHED, NOT JUST ANNOUNCED (2026-08-30).** Both repair seams answered it with a bare `emitAuthState('signed-out')` — a payload that FORCES `signedIn:false` into one push and changes nothing else — so the next request rotated again and announced signed-IN, `lastEmitKey` cannot dedupe an alternating pair, the renderer never sees the STATUS (`broadcastAuthState` forwards `{signedIn,userId}` only), and `app.tsx › App` read one auth TRANSITION per 401 and answered each with `queryClient.clear()` + `persister.removeClient()` + a navigate to boot. **`auth-tokens.js › noteSessionRejected` is the one entry point**; `getAuthState()` reports it ahead of the blob, and `getAccessToken`/`refreshNow`/`kick`/`tick` all stop working off a refused session. ⚠ **Cleared only by `onSignIn`/`onSignOut`, NEVER by a successful rotation** — rotating the same session mints a different token for the same rejected identity. ⚠ **It does NOT drop the blob**: that stays bounded in `noteRefreshOutcome`.
- 🔒 **THE BEARER SEAM DOES NOT SEND A REQUEST IT KNOWS WILL 401 (2026-08-30).** `ui-bridge.js › performApiRequest` attaches a bearer and nothing else, so with no stored session the request is unauthenticated by construction. It answers the envelope `src/shared/auth/with-auth.ts` would return — **copied, not invented**, so one condition cannot read two ways depending on whether the request left the machine. Otherwise each doomed call held a socket for `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` and rejected the IPC with a **status-less** error, which `page-states.isUnauthorized` cannot read as signed-out and the shared TanStack predicate DOES retry. ⚠ **Gated on `getAuthState().signedIn`, never on a null token read** — `getBearerToken()` also answers null for a signed-IN operator mid-backoff after a network blip.
- **ONE CREDENTIAL, ONE ROTATION, BOTH STORES (2026-08-29).** A successful refresh writes the new session into the blob AND the cookie jar (`main/auth.js › refreshInner` → `writeSessionCookies`) — the jar's old refresher was the remote page's supabase-js, which is gone, and a jar left behind by rotation is a stale copy of a dead credential. **A DEFINITIVELY REJECTED REFRESH TOKEN IS NEVER ADOPTED BACK**: the bounded drop marks it (`main/auth-store.js › markRefreshTokenRejected`, in-memory only), `rebuildBlobFromCookieSession` refuses it, and a jar holding that SAME session is cleared at the drop (`main/auth-cookies.js › clearCookiesIfSameRefreshToken`) while a different jar session is kept. Without all three the drop→adopt→drop loop flaps 'signed-out' every ~30s (field log, 2026-08-29). Pinned by `test/auth-rejected-token.test.mjs`.
- 🔒 **…AND ONE HOLDER OF THE FAMILY (2026-09-04).** The three rules above make the MACHINE rotate once; they say nothing about who else is holding the same refresh-token family, and Supabase revokes the WHOLE family when a rotated token is presented again. `/auth/callback?desktop=1` used to exchange the PKCE code with the cookie-WRITING server client, so the SYSTEM BROWSER kept the very session the app then adopted — a second holder that never rotates, refreshes once hours later, and takes the app's live token down with it. **The desktop leg now exchanges with `src/shared/supabase/admin.ts › createDesktopHandoffSupabaseClient` (reads the jar for the code-verifier, `setAll` a literal no-op), hands the session over in the URL FRAGMENT, and `src/app/auth/desktop-handoff/page.tsx` constructs NO Supabase client** — merely constructing one there re-plants the session, because `createBrowserClient` defaults `detectSessionInUrl` to true in a browser. ⚠ **The web leg keeps the writing client**: there the browser IS the holder. ⚠ **An earlier web sign-in's `sb-*-auth-token` in that browser is a DIFFERENT family and is left alone** — clearing it would sign the user out of the site as a side effect of signing in to the app. The refresh 400 now logs GoTrue's `error_code` (`auth-token-rules.js › refreshFailureCode`, enum-shaped or nothing — I11), because "HTTP 400" alone cannot tell `refresh_token_not_found` from `refresh_token_already_used` and that distinction is the entire diagnosis. Pinned by `dopl-desktop-app/test/desktop-handoff-one-family.test.mjs`, which carries the field evidence. ⚠ **RESIDUAL, F-665**: main authenticates `/api/**` with the COOKIE, so the server's own supabase clients can still rotate the app's family and drop the result.
- **The cookie jar is HOST-locked, not origin-locked** — a cookie must be HOST-ONLY for the app origin (leading dot stripped, then `===`), and in-window navigation is locked to the exact origin.
- **Identity is CROSS-CHECKED; a conflicted machine adopts nothing.** Resolution is an explicit sign-out.
- **`signOut()` tears down FOUR credentials** — the Supabase blob, the cookie jar, the MCP device token (server-side revoke FIRST, while the cookie jar it authenticates on still exists), and the Claude inference token. **Clearing the inference token does NOT revoke it at Anthropic**, and the log says so.
- **ONE 401 REPAIR, SHARED (`main/api-repair.js`).** Force ONE rotation through the shared single-flight, write the cookies so the retry carries a DIFFERENT credential, retry EXACTLY once, and let a 401 that survives a fresh token SURFACE. **Exactly two cookie-attaching seams; a third copy of the rule is the bug** — pinned by a test that ENUMERATES the seams rather than trusting a memory of them.
- **`null` means "COULD NOT ASK"; `[]` means "there are none".** Never collapse them. **UNKNOWN is not EMPTY.**
- 🔒 **A RATE IS NOT A GIVE-BACK, AND A CADENCE UNDER THE REQUEST TIMEOUT IS AN AMPLIFIER (2026-08-30).** Two halves, and neither is sufficient alone. (1) **Every self-re-arming retry needs a CEILING, not just a single-flight latch.** `listener-heal.js › listRetryDelay` doubles the workspace-list re-ask from 30s to the 5-minute periodic reconcile's own period, and `› noteWorkspaceListOk` brings it back down — *a ladder that only climbs is a give-up with extra steps.* ⚠ It never gives UP: a failed workspace list starves presence, push, identity and every channel loop at once. (2) **A poll must not fire while its own last request is in flight.** `useMcpConnectionPoll` was `setInterval(3.5s)` against a 30s transport — ~9 doomed requests at once, per window, forever — and is now scheduled from the SETTLEMENT with a backoff to 60s; `session-windowless.js › watchRow` distinguishes a FAILED read from a pending row (F-354) on the same terms. ⚠ **The first failure keeps the base delay** in both ladders: a blip must still recover at the old speed, and only a pattern earns a slower rate.
- **`claudeAvailable()` and `sessionSpawnAvailable()` are NOT the same question.** The first asks "is there an EXTERNAL `claude` on PATH" (what `claude mcp …` needs); the second asks "can a session RUN at all" on ANY registered runtime (`claude-runtime.js › sessionSpawnAvailable` → `runtime/index.js › connectedIds`, leashed and cached — P3-01, 2026-09-23: it required the deleted `./sdk-loader`, so a Mac with no external `claude` deferred every peer request forever, and a Codex-only Mac could not answer at all). The startup notice is vendor-neutral (`runtime-copy.js › noRuntimeCopy`). **Anything gating a channel TRIGGER or a session launch asks the second.** Do not collapse the names.
- **A CONTAINED SESSION'S PROMPT MAY NOT ORDER A DENIED TOOL** — an ordered call the operator must clear before the agent does anything is no better than a denied one.
- **ZERO PEER BYTES IN AN ATTENDED-HANDOFF PREFILL.** That session is the operator's personal Claude with no containment, so the identity interpolates narrowed IDs and nothing else — no names, no titles, no bodies. **Treat any new field there as the security boundary it is.**
- ⚠ **WINDOWING IS INVERTED: A REQUEST DOES NOT MINT A WINDOW (2026-08-18).** An inbound channel request fires a native notification and nothing else; **clicking it FOCUSES the main app and navigates to the CHANNEL the request was made in** — `main/targeting-window.js › openChannelForEntry` → `main/shell-mode.js › navigateToChannels(segment, channelId)` → `/{segment}/{CHANNELS_PAGE}/{channelId}`, over the existing navigate bridge. **`CHANNELS_PAGE` is `'channels'`** — ONE named string, which is what made the Phase 12 cutover's rename an edit rather than a grep (it was `'channels-v2'` from Phase 9 to 2026-08-18). The decision surface is the Inbox's launch panel, one nav row away with its own badge (F-214).
  - **ONE DESTINATION FOR ALL THREE NOTIFICATION PRODUCERS** — the inbound request (`main/trigger.js`), the silent FYI (`main/trigger.js › sendFyi`) and the passive task-reply notice (`main/task-notify.js`) all reach the same seam, which does not distinguish them. **Do not fork it per kind:** the Inbox read is workspace-wide by construction, so routing requests there instead would discard the one fact the notification carried.
  - ✅ **THE SESSION WINDOW IS DELETED — 2026-08-20, F-228 EXECUTED IN FULL.** Samuel's live-test ruling retired the master switch (it governed the operator's own runs and DEFAULTED ON until then); the machinery went in the next wave and the switch itself in the one after, deliberately last so nothing could re-arm in the gap. **What is gone:** `renderer/session/**` (19 files), `session-window.js`, `session-shell.js`, `session-ipc.js`, `session-consent.js`, `session-replay.js`, `session-peer-post.js`, `session-history*.js`, `attended-handoff.js`, `attended-prompt.js`, the tray's "Run sessions in a window" checkbox and its whole "Sessions" submenu, and both `settings.getWindowMode()` / `getPreConsentWindow()`. **Eight surviving modules were CUT DOWN rather than deleted** — the gate's hold/accept family, the park's shell-recreate family, the auth module's in-window sign-in remedy (the HOLD survives; only the in-place remedy went), `session-dispatch`'s four window-gated routes, the engine's window factory + consent reflow, and `session-summary.keptWindow`.
    - ⚠ **`sessionWindowMode` AND `preConsentWindowMode` ARE RETIRED STORE KEYS WITH NO READER, AND THAT IS A RULE, NOT A LEFTOVER.** A machine that ran an older build still carries `sessionWindowMode: true` on disk. Adding a reader resurrects the sender-side session pop-up for exactly the installs that had it — **route (2) minted a session window on the SENDER'S OWN thread opener and launched their agent against their own message, which is the self-trigger bug the whole retirement was ruled from.** Pinned by `test/removed-vocabulary.test.mjs`, which fails on a code-level touch of either key and on any comment naming one without saying it is retired.
    - **Route (1), `feedLiveSession`, was deliberately UNGATED throughout and survives** — it claims nothing into existence; a live session's own existence is the gate. The `classify` widening that pairs with this retirement is §5's task-reply bullet. ⚠ **It is a FAN-OUT since 2026-08-21 — see the multiplayer block below.**

- ⚠ **MULTIPLAYER AGENTS — ONE OPERATOR, N AGENTS, ONE THREAD (2026-08-21, Samuel's ruling). THIS SUPERSEDES "one session per (channel, thread)" EVERYWHERE IT WAS WRITTEN.**
  - **A SESSION IS KEYED `(channel, thread, AGENT INSTANCE)`** — `main/session-store.js › sessionKey`, `<channelId>:<taskId>:<agentId>`. The agent id is a random per-INSTANCE token from `main/agent-id.js` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9]{7}$`, CSPRNG, never recycled). It is the pill's name, the `@`-address a human types, the third segment of the slot, and the `X-Dopl-Session-Id` stamp. ⚠ **`(channel, thread)` now names a GROUP**, and the ONLY sanctioned way to ask about one is `main/session-registry.js` (`liveOnThread` / `sessionOn` / `agentIdsInChannel`) — **the key is COMPARED, never split.**
  - **THE CURATED STONE-NAME POOL IS DELETED IN BOTH TREES**, with its parity test: `main/agent-names.js`, `src/features/channels/server/agent-names.ts`, `agent-names.test.ts`, `agent-names-desktop-parity.test.ts`. **Do not re-file it as an unused-export loss.** A pool handle was RELEASED when its pill left and re-issued within one projection pass, so under multiplayer `@flint` in a transcript could name a different agent than the one it was typed at. `agent-id.js`'s charset is a deliberate SUBSET of `channel_sessions.name`'s CHECK, so no migration was needed.
  - ⚠ **EVERY SPAWN MINTS AN ID, AND `startResume` IS THE ONE THAT DOES NOT GO THROUGH `launch` (2026-08-22).** `session-launch.js › launch` is the funnel that guarantees no session exists without an address; `session-park.js › startResume` builds its own spec, and it passed `rec.agentId || null` straight through — but **every durable record written before 2026-08-21 has no `agentId`**, and those records are on shipped operators' disks. It mints one now (`isAgentId(rec.agentId) ? rec.agentId : newAgentId()`), uses it for BOTH the slot key and the spec, and writes it back onto the record so a second click of the interrupted-notice still finds the live slot instead of starting a second session on one `sdkSessionId`. **What `agentId: null` cost was not local:** `session-summary.js › nameOf` answers `''`, the push files `name: ""`, and the server 400s the WHOLE array — see the wire bullet above.
  - **THE SERVER'S `SESSION_KEY_RE` WAS WIDENED TO MATCH** (`src/features/channels/schema-sessions.ts`, one line by design — the desktop suite lifts the literal out by regex). **The two-segment form is still accepted**: an older desktop is a supported peer during a rollout (§13), and refusing its keys blanks its whole workspace's rows rather than degrading.
  - **THE FEED IS A FAN-OUT, AND THE COUNTERPARTY FENCE IS GONE.** `main/session-dispatch.js › feedLiveSession` feeds EVERY live agent on `(channelId, firstClassTaskId)` **except the one that wrote the message** — counterparty posts, the OPERATOR'S OWN posts and SIBLING agents' posts alike. ⚠ **This is a real widening, stated plainly: a third member posting into the thread now reaches my live agents as a turn.** What still holds: nothing there MINTS a session, the body is still fenced as DATA, and **`targeting.classify` is UNCHANGED** — the addressing law that decides whether a message may START an agent is untouched.
  - **SELF-FILTERING IS BY `client_msg_id`, NEVER BY AUTHOR.** Every agent posts under the operator's own account with `authorKind: 'agent'`, so authorship cannot tell three of my agents apart. `main/session-outbound-tag.js` injects `client_msg_id: agent-<agentId>-<n>` on an own-channel post — the SAME seam and the SAME rules as the forced thread tag (own-channel only, never an overwrite, never on a deny) — and the session records it in a bounded `ownPostIds` set. **An unstamped post is fed to everyone, which is a duplicate turn rather than a lost one.**
    - ⚠ **THE COUNTER IS PERSISTED, BECAUSE THE AGENT ID IS (2026-08-22).** `n` counts from `s.ownPostSeq`, which `startSession` initialised to 0 on every session object while `startResume` deliberately RE-USES the stored agent id — so a crash+resume re-minted `agent-<id>-1, 2, …`, ids the server already had rows for, and its idempotency short-circuit **silently discarded the resumed agent's replies**. It is whitelisted onto the durable record (`session-io.js › baseRecord`, `session-store.js › durableSessionRecord`) and rehydrated through `session-store.js › resumedPostSeq`, which **adds slack** — the record is written at spawn / init / park / settle, so it always lags the posts a crash hid, and resuming from a lower bound is the collision. ⚠ **The SERVER half of that same failure is a different bug and was fixed in the same wave** — idempotency there was channel-scoped, not author-scoped (§5).
  - **`@<agentId>` IS PARSED ON THE DESKTOP, AND MUST STAY THERE.** The server's `metadata.mentionedUserIds` resolves against the channel ROSTER and correctly answers "nobody" for an agent id — that fail-closed behaviour is right and may not be widened, because a caller-settable mention set is a notification-forgery primitive. The parse is intersected with THIS machine's live ids, and **it decides only FRAMING** (`main/session-seed.js › addressingLines`). ⚠ **THE PREMISE UNDER IT IS GONE (2026-09-02, B9 + G13).** This read *"an addressed message and an unaddressed one are both DELIVERED to every sibling; the difference is what the turn SAYS about it"* — true while the desktop fanned a message out to every live agent on the thread, and false now: the server resolves the recipient at write time and stores the verdict (`service-wake-verdict.ts`, RR1/RR2/RR3), and the desktop feeds only that recipient. **A session that was not named is not fed.** ⚠ **SO THE VOLUNTARY CLAIM PROTOCOL IS DELETED, IN BOTH OF ITS COPIES** — the per-turn stand-down preamble in `addressingLines`' unaddressed branch (330 chars per reader per message), and the ~870-char standing block in what is now `prompt-framing-self.js › agentSelfFraming`, which is the agent's own id line and room roster and nothing else. It had been measured not to work in the first place (zero fires across 40 real messages), and deleting prose no agent executed removes no enforcement. ⚠ **WHAT MUST NOT COME BACK:** a sentence anywhere in the framing that asks an agent to decide whether a message is its own. If addressing is wrong, the fix is the VERDICT. ⚠ **`addressingLines(undefined)` still answers `[]`, and `null` is what gets the prose** — `undefined` means no caller ran the fan-out verdict, `null` means it looked and found nobody; every production path supplies `null` (`session-reducer.js › pushInboundEffect` normalizes).
  - **SPAWN IDLE — `sessions:launch` REGISTERS AND STARTS NOTHING.** It mints an agent id, returns `{ ok, agentId }`, and registers a PARKED session with prepared context and **no first SDK turn**; no `claude` child exists until the first message for that agent arrives, which then launches the query with the full framing plus that message. ⚠ **Not "build the query and hold the prompt"** — a held query is a live child holding this session's pre-approved `dopl_channel` access with nobody watching it, the orphan shape C3/C-8 exist to prevent. The abandonment timer is armed at the spawn, so an agent nobody messages ends on its own. **The RESPONDER lane still spawns WITH a first message** and mints an id like every other.
    - ⚠ **IT IS STILL A SPAWN, SO IT ANSWERS THE CREDENTIAL QUESTION LIKE EVERY OTHER LANE (corrected 2026-08-22).** `startSession`'s `parkedShell` early return used to sit IN FRONT of the preflight credential hold (now `session-auth.js › holdIfNoRuntimeCredential`, which asks the session's OWN runtime and fails OPEN when that runtime has no probe — no Claude `~/.claude` fallback for other runtimes, P4-15), so **New Agent on a signed-out machine answered `{sessionId, agentId}` — a success** — and registered an agent holding a slot against `MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS` that could never start a query, while `{skipped:'auth-hold'}` and every refusal line behind it were unreachable on the one lane an operator reaches by CLICKING. The preflight runs first now. 🔒 **AND THE LAUNCH FUNNEL ASKS BEFORE ANYTHING REGISTERS (P4-07, 2026-09-23)**: `session-launch.js › launch` checks, after `acquireRuntime`, whether any live agent on the thread is auth-held ON THE ACQUIRED RUNTIME (P4-22) and then asks that runtime's `credentialState()` (`› credentialMissing`) before `startSession`, so a signed-out launch answers `{skipped:'auth-hold'}` having registered, persisted and posted nothing (the old rollback left a parked record the next boot ended as a card). A probe that throws is not a refusal. `startSession`'s own preflight — now ONE branch, `if (credentialHeld) { sessions.delete(…); return { authHold: true }; }` — still guards the record-driven rebuild (`session-park.js › startResume`). Pinned in `test/session-preflight-hold.test.mjs` through the real engine. **Starting no query is not the same as needing no credential**: the whole point of registering is that a later message wakes it, and on a signed-out Mac that wake produces a dead session with a peer waiting on it. Pinned behaviourally against the shipping tail in `test/spawn-idle-auth-hold.test.mjs`.
    - ⚠ **THE WAKE RULE IS THE SERVER'S ANSWER (2026-09-02, ruling B1 — this REPLACES the TIERED rule of 2026-08-28, which replaced the 2026-08-22 one; both are kept below because a reversal must be readable).** A DORMANT agent — a spawn-idle shell that never started a `claude` child (`awaitingDirective`), or a session an idle park tore the query down for (`state.parked`) — wakes when the STORED VERDICT on the row names it, and on nothing this machine derives. `main/session-dispatch.js › planFor` is the one place the seven verdicts become a delivery; `main/session-gate.js › feedInbound` is the belt behind it.

Two 1:1 messages sent while the agent worked left the session permanently gated, with every later CHANNEL turn silently unable to auto-send. A plain boolean would gate the in-flight CHANNEL turn and then be cleared by ITS `result`, leaving the private turn ungated — the exact failure the rule exists for. Decremented at `result` in the engine's ONE dispatch funnel and **floored at zero** (a drained tail's stray `result` must not make the NEXT private turn public). The `+2` over-covers by one turn, deliberately: the safe direction.

A derivation from the tree was tried and rejected on measurement — it found 3 of ~20 ops, because the tree destructures the bridge or reaches it through typed wrappers. **ADDING an op fails this test on purpose**: the pin is worth only what its last review was, so a new op gets looked at rather than absorbed. The reason any of this exists is unchanged — the shared `src/` tree feature-detects each capability and renders **nothing** when absent, so a gap does not fail, **it deletes a feature silently.** **Adding an op is still a FOUR-file change** (the preload, the `ipcMain` handler, the renderer-side typed mirror, the web tree's feature detector) — **plus the pin.**

What made that safe was CONTENT POLICY rather than a check — the session window shipped `default-src 'none'` with no `frame-src`, denied every `window.open` and blocked navigation off `file://` — and all of it went together. **Nothing was merged into the surviving regime and nothing should be: the rule below is now the whole rule.** ⚠ Why a second binding shape was ever acceptable is ENGINEERING §18's to keep. What follows is the `channel:*` / `ui:*` / window regime, unchanged.

- **The version floor FAILS OPEN.** Offline, timeout, 5xx, captive-portal HTML, a malformed floor, an unparseable own version — all "no floor", app opens. **No floor is ever cached to disk.** Two anti-brick guards from two sources of truth: the server refuses a floor above the declared latest; the client degrades when no updater exists or when a COMPLETED check found nothing newer (a FAILED check never sets that evidence).

- **Never log token values.** Every silent decision is one line to `userData/listener.log` via `diag()`.


#### 11.1 The agent-efficiency wave (2026-09-01) — what an orchestrator may ask for, and what it is told

- 🔒 **A HELD READ — `dopl_channel(op="read", wait_ms=…)` — IS DENIED ON EVERY SESSION THIS MACHINE RUNS, AHEAD OF EVERY GRANT AND BOTH AXES.** ⚠ The `await` OP is gone (2026-09-02): a hold is one argument on `read`, and what is refused is the HOLD, not a spelling — `isAwaitOp` asks `op === "read" && wait_ms != null`, and `wait_ms != null` rather than `> 0`, because a value the server may clamp to zero is still a request to be held. `session-profiles.js › isAwaitOp` is asked inside `grantDecision`'s CHANNEL branch immediately after `postFieldsOk`, so no standing grant, no posture and no operator click can open it. **It is not a permission question**: a desktop-run session is woken by the MESSAGE ITSELF (`session-dispatch.js › feedLiveSession` delivers an addressed post as a TURN), so a hold buys nothing an ended turn does not already get and costs a long-poll plus the whole held context on the far side of it. A GATE would be worse than either — on a windowless session it becomes a notification a human must answer for a call that could not have helped. ⚠ **`read` STAYS A MEMBER OF `OWN_CHANNEL_READ_OPS`**, and the two statements are not in tension: membership answers "what KIND of call is this" (it is what makes a cross-channel hold say *another channel* instead of *unknown op*), the deny answers "may THIS session make it" — and it is now visibly a policy on a SHAPE of an admitted call rather than on an op of its own. ⚠ The refusal carries its own reason code `await-desktop-session` and its own SHORT sentence (`session-permissions.js › AWAIT_DENY_MESSAGE`) — short because the whole ticket is that the call wastes tokens, and it NAMES WHAT REPLACES IT, or the agent reaches for the poll loop the refusal was steering it away from. ⚠ `denyMessageFor` is a `Map` and not an object literal: `reason` is a plain string, and an object lookup answers `constructor` with a FUNCTION, which is truthy and would be handed to an agent as its refusal message. 🔒 ⚠ **AND THE PERMISSION GATE IS ONE OF TWO FENCES SINCE 2026-09-02 (batch-3 review; Desktop Agent default, Samuel may reverse).** That gate covers the runtime it runs in — another vendor's runtime, a raw loopback and a `full`-profile shell all reach `/api/mcp` without passing through it, and each got the whole wake-length hold. `@dopl/mcp-server › tools/channel.ts` refuses the hold server-side on `tools/identity.ts › isDesktopRun`: the `X-Dopl-Runtime: desktop-session` stamp **or** the credential's container lock (`CallerIdentity.containerId`, from `mcp_tokens.container_id` — it rides the token row, so an agent with a shell cannot drop it). ⚠ It refuses the HOLD and never the read, and it answers `AWAIT_DENY_MESSAGE` **verbatim** — `packages/*` cannot import the desktop's CommonJS main, so `dopl-desktop-app/test/session-await-refusal.test.mjs` reads both sources and fails from either side.
- **A WINDOWLESS DENIAL IS COUNTED AND ANNOUNCED ONCE (T25).** `session-windowless.js › noteDenied` keeps `deniedCalls` + `lastDeniedTool` on the session object, written at the two denials that bridge DECIDES — the platform-without-notifications fallback and a prompt that expired unanswered. ⚠ **A `deny` VERDICT FROM `grantDecision` IS NOT COUNTED AND MUST NOT BE DESCRIBED AS IF IT WERE**: it never reaches `claimGate`, because `session-gate-bridge.js › gateCall` answers it settled. The FIRST denial per session writes exactly ONE `task_progress` line (`denied <tool> (tool mode <mode>); further denials counted`) — one per SESSION because this lands in the shared transcript every member reads, so a per-denial post would be `notifyDenied`'s banner storm one turn worse with a peer's listener paying a decision per row. The MODE is on the line because the mode is the REMEDY (a narrow posture is widenable; an unclassified tool is not). `task_progress`, never `message`, so it wakes nobody.
- **THE PROJECTION CARRIES A HEALTH HALF (T50 / T51 / T83): `turns`, `tokensDelta`, `stale`, `deniedCalls`, `lastDeniedTool`, `lastWakeSeq`, `lastWakeAt`.** `main/session-health.js` is the derivation and it starts no counter — four writers stamp the facts, each at the one site that knows it, pinned by `test/session-health.test.mjs`. ⚠ **IT IS CARRIED INTO THE PROJECTION THROUGH `session-metrics.js › metrics`, WHICH IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT A PREFERENCE**: `session-summary.js` stands at exactly the 500-line §1 cap, so a require line and a spread line there would be a lint error. ⚠ **`stale` IS THREE CONDITIONS AND ALL THREE ARE REQUIRED** — WORKING, quiet past `STALE_QUIET_MS` (ten minutes), and still SPENDING. Quiet-and-working alone describes every agent doing a long piece of work, and a flag that fires on those is one everybody learns to ignore, which is strictly worse than no flag. An unmeasured spend WITHHOLDS the claim rather than asserting one. ⚠ **"SINCE LAST REPORT" MEANS SINCE THE LAST CHANNEL POST**, deliberately: the telemetry push is CHURN floored at ten seconds (`session-telemetry.js`), so a delta measured against it says nothing an orchestrator can act on, while the last post IS the last thing that orchestrator saw. ⚠ `stale` rides the CHURN half of the wire row and is absent from `session-telemetry.js › STATE_FIELDS` — it is derived from a WALL CLOCK, and putting it in the state half would let it flip a set past the cadence floor on a timer, which is the "digest gate stops gating" defect that module exists to prevent. ⚠ **THE SERVER HALF OF THIS CHAIN IS WRITTEN — F-409 CLOSED 2026-09-02.** This bullet said it was NOT, on a branch that supplies all six pieces: the migration (`20260909120000_channel_sessions_health.sql`), the zod fields on `schema-sessions.ts › SessionStateEntrySchema`, `collab-dto.ts`'s upsert / operator-only column list / `mapOwnSessionStateRow`, `ChannelSessionHealth` in both type trees, and the render in `channel-session-health.ts`. ⚠ **WHAT IS STILL OWED IS THE APPLY, WHICH IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT A CLAIM (§12)** — until that migration replays, the columns do not exist and `zod` keeps stripping the seven at the route, which is the safe direction: dropped rather than 400-ing the whole push, so nothing regresses and nothing renders yet.
- **A WAKE IS ACKNOWLEDGED ON A FIELD, NEVER ON A POST (T50).** `session-gate.js › enqueue` stamps `lastWakeSeq` / `lastWakeAt` when the wake VERDICT is true — at DELIVERY, past the queue-overflow return, because a wake recorded above that line claims a turn for a message the queue rejected. ⚠ **IT READS THE VERDICT, NEVER THE BODY**: `a.wake` is the tier decision already made for THIS message and THIS agent, and the LOOP FENCE lives inside that decision, so a body-reading stamp would credit an agent-authored post that woke nothing. ⚠ **`typeof` FIRST, WHERE `lastInboundSeq` BESIDE IT COERCES**, and the asymmetry is deliberate: `Number(null)` is 0, harmless for a consent-row de-dupe hint and a LIE for a field rendered as `woke on #0`.
- 🔒 **THE DIRECTIVE MAILBOX CARRIES FOUR KINDS, AND THE CONSENT SET IS DATA.** `launch-directive-wire.js › KINDS` is `launch | end | rename | set_agent_mode`, and `KINDS_NEEDING_LAUNCH_CONSENT` is `launch` + `set_agent_mode`. ⚠ **`set_agent_mode` SITS ON THE GATED SIDE WHERE ITS TWO NON-LAUNCH SIBLINGS DO NOT**: a STOP verb and a DISPLAY verb widen nothing, and Axis A at `bypass` PRE-APPROVES work tools on hardware this operator pays for — which is the LOCAL COMPUTE the toggle exists to gate. The set is a LIST rather than a `||` chain so a fifth kind cannot be admitted past whichever reader nobody updated.
- 🔒 **A DIRECTIVE MAY ASK FOR A POSTURE AND IT MAY NEVER WIDEN ONE (T24), ON BOTH LANES, THROUGH ONE RULE.** `main/launch-posture.js › narrowTo` / `resolvePosture` / `resolveChain` are required — never copied — by `launch-directive-spawn.js › planPosture`, and `directive-agent-ops.js › setAgentMode` goes through the engine's own clamp (below). The ceiling is the operator's OWN durable record FOR THE LAUNCH RUNTIME (`channel-prefs.js › launchPostureFor(channelId, runtimeId)`, and the native bag from `› launchStartModes` — never the selected runtime's record, P3-03/P3-04, 2026-09-23); an unset or unreadable record is that runtime's narrowest word / `ask`, so a store failure NARROWS.
  - 🔒 **EACH RUNTIME'S OWN WORDS (Samuel's ruling 2, 2026-09-23).** Axis A on the directive wire is the UNION of every registered runtime's words — `launch-directive-vocab.js › TOOL_MODES` = `src/features/channels/schema-launch-modes.ts › LAUNCH_TOOL_MODES` (`› LAUNCH_TOOL_MODES_BY_RUNTIME`: Claude `manual|accept_edits|auto|bypass`, Codex `untrusted|granular|on-request|never`, Cursor `allowlist|auto-review|run-everything`) = the column CHECKs (`20261020120000_channel_launch_directives_runtime_tool_words.sql`, §12). It is a SET, not an order: a word is validated against the RESOLVED runtime (`session-profiles.js › toolModesFor`) and clamped in THAT runtime's narrowest-first order. A word the runtime does not offer is NOT applied: a launch runs that axis at the channel posture (the echo says so); a `set_agent_mode` asking only that axis is refused `no-bridge`. MCP `dopl_channel`'s `posture.tools` lists the words per runtime, and the pulled doctrine (`channel-doctrine.ts › MANAGE`) teaches them.
  - 🔒 **LAUNCH RUNTIME ORDER (ruling 5): `launch-directive-spawn.js` asks `runtime/launch-default.js › resolveLaunchRuntime`** — the directive's pick → the identity's runtime → the channel's → the default; an unusable pick or identity runtime refuses `no-sdk`. The pick is answered before the identity fetch; the identity/channel links after it.
  - 🔒 **NARROWER STICKS, PER AXIS (ruling 3).** A launch pins EXACTLY the axes it asked (`› planPosture` hands `startModes.pinned = { tools, messages }`; `session-state.js › initialSessionState` accepts `pinned: true` for both or that object) and an unasked axis follows the channel live. `set_agent_mode` calls `setModeByTask({…, pinned: true})`, and the ENGINE validates in the session's words, clamps to the channel's value for its runtime and floors — the lane no longer clamps it. The echo on both lanes is what the gate enforces (P3-08; the decide `done` arm carries `appliedTools` / `appliedMessages`, F2).
  - **ONE MODEL PATH (P3-09).** `launch-directive-spawn.js › resolveModel` hands `pickOf(d.model) || identityModelFor(runtime, identity.model, identity.runtime)` to the funnel on every runtime — no per-launch `runtime.models()` spawn; the funnel's cached check refuses an unknown pick and fails open on an unreadable roster (the pick is never dropped). `appliedModel` is the model `session-launch.js › launch` launched with, resolved by the adapter's `modelArg` (`› appliedModelId`); `launch-directive-vocab.js › MODEL_MAX = 120` bounds `directiveFrom`'s `model` and the decide's `appliedModel` (P3-30). ⚠ **T24's OWN CARVE-OUT — "unless the caller is the operator's own account" — WAS REFUSED, AND THE REASON IS MEASURABLE.** Every caller on this lane IS that account: a spawned session calls the MCP server with the OPERATOR'S credential, which is why `operator_user_id` never refused a launched agent and could not have. The exception is the whole set, and taking it would hand every agent on the machine the power to launch children wider than its operator's room allows. ⚠ **CLAMP, THEN FLOOR, IN THAT ORDER** — flooring first would let a clamped `ask` come back out as `auto_inbound` and read as though the ceiling had allowed it. ⚠ **A CHAIN REQUEST THE CHANNEL FORBIDS REFUSES UP FRONT RATHER THAN CLAMPING**: a clamped posture still produces a working agent under more supervision, where a clamped chain produces one that hits a bound it was told it did not have, mid-run, and `channelAgentChain` is a SPAWN-TIME stamp nobody can flip for a session already started. ⚠ **`narrowTo` ASKS MEMBERSHIP BEFORE COMPARING INDEXES** — an unknown request also indexes to -1 and `-1 > n` is FALSE, so a bare comparison fails OPEN on the one axis that must not.
  - 🔒 **`chain` IS A TRUE TRI-STATE AND ALL THREE VALUES ARE HONOURED (fixed 2026-09-01).** `true` ASKS IT ON and is refused where the channel forbids it; **`false` ASKS IT OFF, is ALWAYS granted, and WINS over a channel set to ON** — it only ever narrows, so there is nothing for the operator's setting to protect and NARROWING IS NEVER REFUSED; `null` did not ask and inherits the channel setting. ⚠ **TWO DEFECTS HID EACH OTHER AND EACH ALONE MADE `chain: false` UNHONOURABLE**: `launch-directive-wire.js › directiveFrom` narrowed the column as `r.chain === true || r.chain === 'true' ? true : null`, so a stored `false` arrived as "did not ask", and `resolveChain`'s `false` arm fell through to `allowed === true`. **A suite that drives ONE half cannot close this** — `dopl-desktop-app/test/launch-chain.test.mjs` drives a RAW ROW through `directiveFrom` into `resolveChain` and on into the spawn spec, which is the only shape that goes red on either revert (3 reverts, 4 failures each, 0 vacuous). Every copy on the lane said `false` did nothing and every one is corrected in the same change; the column type did not move.
  - 🔒 **THE CLAMP IS NOW A WIRE FIELD AS WELL AS A DIAG — F-410 CLOSED (2026-09-01).** The decide echoes the APPLIED pair and chain (§10's T24 bullet), so a caller can read back what landed. It is reported on EVERY launch, not only a clamped one: otherwise silence would mean both "an older desktop said nothing" and "a current one agreed with you", and the render has one word for it.
- ⚠ **`spawn` LEFT `main/launch-directives.js` ON 2026-09-01** for `main/launch-directive-spawn.js`, at the 500-line cap F-388 measured that file sitting exactly on. The seam: the WATCHER decides whether to act on a row (arming, the owner re-check, the per-kind consent gate, the CAS, the dedupe ledger, the backstop poll); the SPAWN decides what a session is built out of. **The §6 THREAT MODEL stayed with the watcher; the field-by-field containment statement went with the code it governs**, and `test/session-preset-census.test.mjs`'s posture census now names `launch-directive-spawn.js`.

Why/history: ENGINEERING.md §18 (v1.1–v1.9, F-119/F-125/F-138/F-140/F-177, the reliability round, H1–H3).
