## 12. Migrations

- **REPLAY IS THE GATE.** `supabase db reset` → exit 0 is the check that means something. Local config is `supabase/config.toml` (present, verified 2026-08-11), ports remapped off the defaults so a second stack can run beside it.
- **MIGRATION-LIST-IS-CLAIMS DOCTRINE.** `supabase migration list` compares history ROWS to FILENAMES and **structurally cannot notice that the files do not build a database** — it reported "in sync / 0 pending" through months of a tree that died on its first file. **Treat "in sync" as evidence about the history table only.**
- 🔒 **THE HISTORY VERSION IS NOT THE FILENAME — MATCH ON THE *NAME* (measured 2026-08-24, F-304).** Every migration in the recent wave applied under a RE-STAMPED version: `20260822150000_channel_sessions_telemetry` → `20260823091543`, `20260822170000_overview_time_range_indexes` → `20260823091749`, `20260823150000_home_link_channels` → `20260823205007`, `20260823160000_default_workspace_kind_guard` → `20260823205026`. **Order is preserved, so nothing is broken** — but roughly ninety doc and code sites cite a migration BY FILENAME, and the one command an agent runs to check them (`supabase migration list` / MCP `list_migrations`) prints VERSIONS. **So "is `20260823150000` applied?" returns a list not containing that string, and the honest reading of that is "no" — which is exactly the wrong answer this file gave for a day.** ⚠ **Do NOT mass-rename the files to match:** the filenames are the anchors every reference (and `check-doc-refs.mjs`) resolves against. Re-derive with the command; join on the NAME.
- **`20260907120000_channel_launch_directives_kind.sql` — THE DIRECTIVE **KIND** (2026-09-01, Samuel's external end/rename ruling).** ⚠ **WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED** — this directory's standing gate; replay is OWED and recorded rather than glossed (Docker is unavailable on this machine, so `supabase db reset` cannot start, and the applied state was measured instead by `supabase migration list --linked` **joined on the NAME** plus a live `information_schema.columns` read of `channel_launch_directives`). **ADDITIVE ONLY, and it edits no applied file.** Adds `kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'launch'` + its three-word CHECK, `target_agent_id` (the INPUT an end/rename names — ⚠ **never merge it with `agent_id`, which is the OUTPUT a launch produced**), and `target_name` (the rename's new display name, bounded at 60 = `main/agent-names.js › MAX_NAME`, ⚠ **where `''` is LEGAL and means CLEAR**). It also widens the status CHECK with `done` and the refusal CHECK to nine words, and rewrites the terminal-shape CHECK to be KIND-AWARE.
  - ⚠ **`DEFAULT 'launch'` + `NOT NULL` IS WHAT MADE IT A NO-BACKFILL CHANGE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS** — every existing row IS a launch, and an older SERVER build mid-rollout that inserts without naming a kind writes what it meant (§13: an older peer is supported).
  - ⚠ **A TYPED `target_name` COLUMN, NOT A `payload JSONB`, AND THE REASON IS THE DESKTOP.** `main/launch-directive-wire.js › directiveFrom` is a LITERAL WHITELIST, and that whitelist is the only thing stopping a widened table from influencing that machine by accident; a JSON blob passes it as one opaque key and then carries whatever it likes into main. A named column with a CHECK is refusable AT REST.
  - ⚠ **AND A TENTH WORD, `no-chain`, JOINED ON 2026-09-02 (review fix).** A directive that asked to CHAIN in a channel where the operator has not enabled it answered `no-bridge` — the SAME word this machine sends when it is not watching that channel at all, and the two are OPPOSITE instructions: one says go elsewhere, the other says the channel is right and ONE NAMED SETTING (`main/launch-posture.js › CHAIN_SETTING` = `channelAgentChain`) is off. Producer: `main/launch-directive-spawn.js › spawn`; CHECK: `20260910120000_channel_launch_directives_posture.sql` §3A, which re-creates the constraint WHOLE and RAISEs if any earlier word or the `identity-approval` negative pin went missing.
  - ⚠ **THE REFUSAL CHECK AND ITS PRODUCER LAND IN THE SAME WAVE** — `no-session` and `bad-name` are produced by `main/directive-agent-ops.js`, which ships with this file. That is the 2026-08-22 sequencing lesson APPLIED: `no-identity` spent a day in four TypeScript files while the CHECK was still at six, and a `decide` carrying it would have passed zod, passed the route and been refused AT REST. ⚠ **The NEGATIVE PIN on `identity-approval` is carried forward and the `DO $$` block still RAISEs on it** — this file REWRITES that constraint whole, which is exactly the change that drops a word by accident, so the block also RAISEs if `no-identity` went missing.
  - ⚠ **IT NEVER TOUCHES THE REPLICA IDENTITY OR THE POLICY SET, and asserts both survived rather than assuming.** Losing the replica-identity index stops every UPDATE frame reaching the desktop; a non-SELECT policy appearing on a table whose ENTIRE authorization story is "no write policy exists" would be the quietest possible regression. Pinned from the desktop side too, in `test/launch-directive-agent-ops.test.mjs`.
- **`20261019120000_rename_agent_templates_to_agent_identities.sql` — AGENT TEMPLATES → AGENT IDENTITIES (2026-09-22, §5A).** ⚠ **WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED** — this directory's standing gate. `ALTER … RENAME` only (tables, columns, constraints, indexes, triggers), so data, OIDs, table + column grants, RLS and publication membership travel with the objects; the four functions whose BODY names the old table or the `agent_template` resource word are restated from the live catalog with their headers and ACLs, and the two SELECT policies are re-created on the renamed predicate `can_current_user_read_agent_identity`. The two vocabulary words (`resource_grants.resource_type`, `refusal_reason`) are re-worded between dropping and restating their CHECKs; the refusal CHECK is restated WHOLE (`20260910120000` §3A's ten words, `no-template` → `no-identity`, plus `no-model` — the eleventh word, 2026-09-22, producer `main/session-launch.js › launch`) and §9 asserts every word; the separate `no-model` file that once preceded it was DELETED 2026-09-23 (P7-08 — unapplied anywhere, and applying it by name AFTER this one would have dropped `no-identity`). ⚠ It touches `home_scoped` only behind an existence guard (the §8 column comment, which no longer claims a reader), so the held `20260923120000_drop_home_scoped.sql` may replay before it. ⚠ **No model-id CHECK exists anywhere to loosen** — every model column (this table's, `agent_identities.model`) is grammar-only, deliberately. ⚠ **THE REPLAY GATES READ RENAMES THROUGH `shared/supabase/migration-renames.ts › forwardRenamed`** — each file is rewritten with the renames LATER files perform — so `knowledge/migration-replay.ts`, `shared/supabase/rls-policy-scan.ts` (and through it `scripts/check-rls-pair-gate.ts`) and `scripts/check-tenancy-move-gate.ts` see `agent_identities` created where `agent_templates` was — all three read the one loader, `shared/supabase/migration-files.ts › readMigrations` (2026-09-23). A column rename is applied as a whole-word substitution on every table, correct here because `template_id` / `template_name` were renamed wherever they existed.
- **`20261020120000_channel_launch_directives_runtime_tool_words.sql` — DIRECTIVE TOOL MODES IN EACH RUNTIME'S OWN WORDS (2026-09-23, Samuel's ruling 2).** ⚠ **WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED.** Re-creates `channel_launch_directives_tool_modes_check` (start / target / applied) and `channel_launch_directives_resolved_check` (`resolved_tool_mode`) WHOLE over the eleven-word UNION of the registered runtimes' Axis-A words (Claude four, Codex four, Cursor three — a SET, validated per runtime on the machine, §11.1), mirroring `channels/schema-launch-modes.ts › LAUNCH_TOOL_MODES_BY_RUNTIME` and `launch-directive-vocab.js › TOOL_MODES`. Widening only; idempotent; a closing `DO $$` block asserts the outcome. The message-mode CHECKs are runtime-neutral and untouched.
- **`20261021120000_agent_identities_runtime.sql` — IDENTITIES CARRY A RUNTIME (2026-09-23, Samuel's rulings 4–6).** ⚠ **WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED.** Adds nullable `agent_identities.runtime` with `agent_identities_runtime_shape_check` (the runtime-id GRAMMAR, pinned to `channels/schema-launch-modes.ts › LAUNCH_RUNTIME_ID_RE` by `agent-identities/schema-sql.test.ts`; never an enum). **Backfill (ruling 6):** a Claude model id (`claude-*`) or alias (`opus|sonnet|haiku|fable`, optional `[…]` suffix) → `claude`; everything else (no model, a Codex id) stays NULL = no preference. Idempotent; a closing `DO $$` block asserts the column, the CHECK and zero un-backfilled Claude rows. No grant/RLS/function change: the table's SELECT grant and policy are table-level and no function selects an explicit column list of it. **Apply after `20261019120000`** (it names the renamed table).
- **`20261017120000_channel_launch_directives_runtime.sql` — AN MCP LAUNCH MAY NAME ITS RUNTIME (2026-09-21, U9).** Adds `runtime` (the request) and `applied_runtime` (what the machine started on) with `channel_launch_directives_runtime_shape_check`, a GRAMMAR mirrored by `channels/schema-launch-modes.ts › LAUNCH_RUNTIME_ID_RE` and `launch-directive-vocab.js › RUNTIME_ID_RE` (pinned by `schema-launch-runtime.test.ts` and `test/launch-directive-runtime.test.mjs`; the MCP field checks length only). This row was missing until 2026-09-23 (P7-33). Whether it is applied is a measurement (below), not this line.
- 🔒 **RELEASE-TIME MIGRATIONS OF THE 2026-09-23 CLEANUP — APPLY BY NAME, IN THIS ORDER: `20261019120000_rename_agent_templates_to_agent_identities`, `20261020120000_channel_launch_directives_runtime_tool_words`, `20261021120000_agent_identities_runtime`.** This file records the COMMAND, never the answer: `supabase migration list --linked` (or MCP `list_migrations`) **joined on the NAME** (F-304's re-stamp); apply each missing file by NAME, byte-exact, never `supabase db push`, and md5-check the applied text against the file. The server, the desktop and these three ship together — a desktop built before them reads renamed columns that do not exist, and the server's zod accepts Codex words the un-widened CHECK would refuse at rest.
- **`20260903120000_channel_agent_directions.sql` — THE PRIVATE DIRECT LANE's mailbox (2026-08-31).** ⚠ **WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED** — this directory's standing gate; replay is OWED and recorded rather than glossed. Cloned from `20260822160000_channel_launch_directives.sql` with three differences that are each rulings: `agent_id` is **NOT NULL** (a direction with no addressee is a broadcast into somebody's private lane), the TTL is longer (a direction is answered by a TURN, not a process start), and it carries a **`reply`** column. 🔒 The owner-only SELECT matters more here than on the launch mailbox because `reply` holds a PRIVATE TURN's answer — the closing `DO $$` asserts the policy still scopes on `operator_user_id`, not merely that one policy exists.
- **`20260904090000_direction_sender_agent.sql` — `sender_agent_id` on that mailbox (F-376a, 2026-08-31).** ⚠ **WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED**, and it is OWED behind the one above rather than instead of it. Nullable TEXT with `agent_id`'s own charset CHECK; **no index** (nothing queries by sender and every read is already narrowed by `operator_user_id` to at most 50–100 rows), **no publication or replica-identity change** (a nullable column simply appears in the frames the desktop already receives, and `agent-direction-wire.js › directionFrom` is a whitelist that reads it as absent on an older server). 🔒 It carries a `COMMENT ON COLUMN` saying in as many words that the value is UNVERIFIED and may not be gated on, plus a closing `DO $$` re-asserting that the table still has no non-SELECT policy and no write grant to `authenticated`/`anon`.
- **`20260902120000_channel_escalation_answer_unique.sql` — ONE ANSWER PER ESCALATION, at rest (2026-08-31).** A UNIQUE PARTIAL index on `channel_messages ((metadata -> 'escalationAnswer' ->> 'escalationMessageId')) WHERE metadata ? 'escalationAnswer'`. ⚠ **WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED** — this directory's standing gate; replay is OWED and is recorded rather than glossed.
  - **THE PREDICATE IS THE COST CONTROL, NOT A DETAIL:** the index holds one entry per ANSWER — a handful of rows per channel, ever — where an unqualified one would make every ordinary post pay an index write to store a NULL.

## 13. Release pipeline

- **`npm run release` in `dopl-desktop-app/` is a WRAPPER SCRIPT, not `electron-builder --publish always`.** It is `bash scripts/release.sh` (verified 2026-08-11). ⚠ ENGINEERING.md §18's "Commands" block still documents the raw invocation — **the script is the supported way to ship.**
  - **The POST-UPLOAD ASSERTION IS THE ENTIRE POINT.** `electron-builder --publish always` reports success on a partial upload; two consecutive releases each lost a DIFFERENT artifact silently. The script re-reads what GitHub actually has and refuses to call it a release until every expected name is there and the public feed URL serves the same bytes as `dist/`.
  - It re-hashes after stapling: the afterSign hook staples the `.app`, THEN `latest-mac.yml` is generated, and only THEN is the DMG stapled — which changes the DMG's bytes.
  - Flags: `--dry-run` (build + staple + re-hash, publish nothing), `--skip-build` (resume from an existing `dist/` — the repair path both real incidents needed). **No secret is ever echoed** — credentials are probed for PRESENCE only.
- **The GitHub release TAG must be `v<version>`** or electron-updater will not match the feed.
- **`renderer/app/` must exist before a release** — build output of `apps/desktop-ui` (`npm run build:ui` at the repo root), gitignored.
- **The auto-updater never force-restarts.** It installs on normal quit or an explicit tray action — a background listener must not yank an active spawned session.
- ⚠ **UPDATE DISCOVERY IS THE INTERVAL *PLUS* A FOCUS CHECK, AND THE FOCUS CHECK IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS (2026-08-22, Samuel's ruling).** The steady interval is **30 minutes** (`update-policy.js › DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS`, measured 2026-08-22 — **it was 4h**, and a release published while the app was open went unnoticed for most of a day; the operator's workaround was to QUIT AND REOPEN the app to force the boot check, which is the feature failing at its one job). `DOPL_UPDATE_CHECK_MS` still overrides it, still clamped to **[60s, 24h]** — those two did NOT move.
  - **THE SIGNAL SET IS APP-LEVEL AND IT IS EXACTLY TWO:** `browser-window-focus` (covers the SPA shell, the pop-out, the agent window and the update screen at once, and it is what fires on the TRAY path — how a tray-resident app is usually reached) and `activate` (the macOS bring-forward: a dock click, or a cmd-tab into a run with no focused window yet). ⚠ **Per-window `win.on('focus')` was refused**: same event, plus a registration to keep in sync with `app-windows.js`, and the F-228 sweep is the record of what a missed one costs. ⚠ **`powerMonitor` resume/unlock is deliberately NOT in the set** — `wake.js` owns that seam for the listener, a machine waking is not the operator looking, and the interval covers it within 30 minutes.
  - **THE GAP IS THE RATE LIMIT: `FOCUS_CHECK_MIN_GAP_MS` = 10 minutes**, pure and tested (`update-policy.js › shouldCheckOnFocus`). Cmd-tabbing fires focus constantly, so without it "check when the operator looks" is "check tens of times a minute". ⚠ **It is SHARED with the interval — one `lastCheckAt`, stamped WHEN A REQUEST IS ISSUED, not when one succeeds.** An errored check still cost a request, so a success-only stamp would turn an offline machine into one request per window focus. Edge answers: never-checked → yes; clock moved backward → yes once (the stamp is rewritten); unreadable clock → **no**, the only branch that fails closed.
  - ⚠ **A FOCUS CHECK IS NOT A MANUAL ONE.** It passes no `{manual:true}`, so every no-op path stays silent — a staged update is left alone (**no re-check and no restart prompt**, unlike a manual check, which goes straight to the prompt because an explicit ask deserves the action), a download in flight says nothing, and a failure is swallowed by the global handler. The operator did not ask a question, so nothing answers one.
  - **NOTHING ELSE MOVED**: not the never-auto-restart rule, not the live-session prompt suppression, not the clamp. **RATE-LIMIT SANITY, measured 2026-08-22:** 30-min polling is 48 requests/day and focus checks add at most one per 10-minute gap (~144/day worst case) against a public GitHub Releases asset — far clear of the 60/hr unauthenticated API quota.
  - **THE MIN-VERSION FLOOR RIDES THE INTERVAL AND GAINED ONLY FRESHNESS** (`min-version.js § Cadence`, re-verified 2026-08-22): a raised floor is now noticed in half an hour rather than half a day. ⚠ **The floor read is NOT hung off the focus signal** — it is a *second* server (`/api/version`), and a request per cmd-tab is a cost nobody asked for. If the two are ever coupled, couple them at the interval, where the gap already bounds them.
- **The download URL is RESOLVED, never guessed.** electron-builder stamps the version into the artifact name, so `/releases/latest/download/:asset` is evergreen in the RELEASE, not in the asset NAME; `GET /download` reads the dmg's name out of `latest-mac.yml`. **Every failure still lands on a github.com URL** — a Download button may not show anybody a stack trace.
- **`latest` is DERIVED, not declared** (`shared/version/latest-release.ts` reads the electron-updater channel file — a release ASSET, outside the `api.github.com` 60/hr-per-IP quota, and the same fact the client reads). **Nothing is bumped by hand at release time.**
- **The floor rides CODE with an env override read per request** (`shared/version/desktop-floor.ts`). `DEFAULT_MIN_VERSION` and `DEFAULT_DECLARED_LATEST` are bumped in the same release commit, and a same-commit test pins floor ≤ latest so the clamp can never refuse its own release. **Malformed = no floor**, the fail-open direction. **Do not set `DOPL_DESKTOP_LATEST_VERSION` from `dopl-desktop-app/package.json`** — that file is a claim about what should ship and runs AHEAD of what is published; a latest ahead of reality permits a floor nothing can install.
- **THE SHIP-ORDER GATE IS WEB-BEFORE-DESKTOP.** Any desktop build requiring a server behaviour ships only after the web deploy carrying it is LIVE. The `requireState` auth gate (§11) is the worked example; the notify-scope column drop is the pattern: code deploy → raise the desktop floor → then the destructive migration.
  - ⚠ **A FORCED UPGRADE IS A DEPLOY STEP, NOT A CODE CHANGE — AND THE REPO CANNOT ARM ONE AHEAD OF A RELEASE.** Worked example, open right now: `/api/home/relationships` was DELETED on 2026-08-24 (§9), so every desktop build predating `/api/home/channels` renders an empty, erroring home page. Samuel ruled force-update. **`dopl-desktop-app/main/version-gate.js` is the imperative shell and holds NO minimum** — it fetches `/api/version` and obeys whatever floor comes back. The floor is `shared/version/desktop-floor.ts › DEFAULT_MIN_VERSION`, overridden per-environment by `DOPL_DESKTOP_MIN_VERSION`.
  - 🔒 **THE ANTI-BRICK CLAMP REFUSES A FLOOR ABOVE `latest`, WHICH MAKES "BUMP IT NOW" A NO-OP RATHER THAN AN ERROR.** `› resolveDesktopFloor` serves **no floor at all** (`rejected: "above-latest"`) when the configured floor exceeds the newest PUBLISHED build, and `latest` is derived from the release feed. **So committing a floor for an unreleased version does not gate anybody — it silently disarms the gate**, which is worse than leaving it alone because it looks done. `desktop-floor.test.ts` pins `DEFAULT_MIN_VERSION ≤ DEFAULT_DECLARED_LATEST` in the same commit for exactly this reason, and §13's standing rule forbids sourcing `latest` from `dopl-desktop-app/package.json` — that file is a claim about what SHOULD ship.
  - **THE ORDER, therefore:** publish the release carrying the new client → confirm the release feed serves it → THEN raise the floor, either by `DOPL_DESKTOP_MIN_VERSION` on Vercel (no deploy, instant, reversible) or by bumping `DEFAULT_MIN_VERSION` **and** `DEFAULT_DECLARED_LATEST` together in the release commit. **Measured 2026-08-25: `DEFAULT_MIN_VERSION` = `1.10.0`, `DEFAULT_DECLARED_LATEST` = `1.10.2`, `dopl-desktop-app/package.json` = `1.19.0`** — the code defaults are nine minor versions stale, so if the release feed is ever unreachable the cold-start clamp would refuse any floor above `1.10.2`. Re-measure before acting; do not quote.
  - ⚠ **A NEW SPA ROUTE IS NOT THAT GATE, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT.** The SPA is BUILT INTO the app bundle (`renderer/app/`, from `npm run build:ui` — see the `renderer/app/ must exist` bullet above), so main and the route it navigates to ship as **one artifact**: `channels/:channelId` and the desktop `navigateToChannels(segment, channelId)` that pushes it (§11, 2026-08-18 — the path was `channels/components/:channelId` until the Phase 12 cutover renamed both ends in one change, which is the same argument again) cannot be out of order with each other, and there is no web deploy in the path. **The gate that applies is the RELEASE gate — build the SPA before packaging** — not the server one. **The web-before-desktop gate applies when the desktop needs a SERVER behaviour**, which a router path is not; do not invoke it for renderer-only changes, and do not skip it because this case did.
- **Deployed values are measurements.** Whether `CRON_SECRET` is set, which migrations are applied, what `DOPL_DESKTOP_MIN_VERSION` holds — **verify by observing the deployment**, e.g. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://www.usedopl.com/api/cron/oauth-cleanup` (401 = gated and live, 503 = secret unset; the apex 307-redirects to `www`, so check without `-L` or you learn nothing). Never record the answer here.
- **THREE crons, wired in `vercel.json`, gated by `requireCronSecret`** (re-measured **2026-08-30**, `ls src/app/api/cron/` and `jq '.crons[].path' vercel.json`): `oauth-cleanup`, `reconcile-seats`, **`playground-reaper`**. ⚠ **This said TWO until 2026-08-30 and had said so since 2026-08-18** — the reaper landed with the playground tree that F-208 recorded as untracked, and nothing re-ran the measurement the bullet itself prescribes.
  - ⚠ **`stale-threads` WAS THE THIRD AND IS DELETED (2026-08-18, wiring plan Phase 4).** Its entire body was a close PROPOSAL — a `task_progress` carrying `closeProposed` on any thread idle 14 days — and there is no close to propose (§5). The route, `repository-tasks.ts › listStaleOpenThreads` and the caller of the `channel_tasks_stale` RPC went together. **The RPC survives in the database with no caller; dropping it is F-207.**
  - ⚠ **THE `vercel.json` ENTRY DID NOT GO WITH THEM, AND THIS BULLET SAID IT HAD.** Phase 4 claimed the schedule was removed; the file was never touched, so `vercel.json` carried `/api/cron/stale-threads` at `0 7 * * *` for the whole interval and **every deploy re-registered a cron whose only possible answer was 404 — daily, indefinitely, not "until the next deploy"**. The entry was deleted 2026-08-18 in the wave-2 fix pass. **The lesson is the file, not the cron: a claim that a config entry was removed is checkable in one grep, and nobody ran it.** Whether the deployed schedule is actually gone is a MEASUREMENT (`vercel crons ls`, or the project's Cron Jobs tab) — the repo can only hold the claim.
  - ✅ **THAT DISAGREEMENT IS RESOLVED, AND §10 WAS RIGHT (2026-08-30, F-208 closed).** This bullet said *"§10's playground bullet names a THIRD cron, `app/api/cron/playground-reaper`, and no such directory or `vercel.json` entry exists in this tree"* (measured 2026-08-18). **The measurement was honest and the cause was that the playground was UNTRACKED WORK in the main checkout** — it has since landed: `src/app/api/cron/playground-reaper/route.ts` is tracked and `vercel.json` carries its schedule. §10 was correct-but-early, which was one of the two readings F-208 named.
  - 🔴 **SO THE COUNT IN THIS SECTION IS THREE, NOT TWO** — `oauth-cleanup`, `reconcile-seats` and `playground-reaper`. ⚠ `playground-reaper` has been running unobserved since 2026-08-19 and is named in no other doc; **F-133's job set is wrong for the same reason.** Re-derive rather than quoting: `grep -A2 '"crons"' vercel.json`.

- **A bug-fix PR must include a test that would have caught it.** Tests live next to code (`pipeline.ts` → `pipeline.test.ts`); no `__tests__/` tree.
- **MUTATION-VERIFY CULTURE: an assertion is not verified until reverting the code turns it red.** State the count when you claim it ("N reverts, N failures, 0 vacuous"). A suite that stays green against the bug it names is the defect, not the evidence.
- **A PIN ON A SYMBOL IS NOT A PIN.** Asserting a constant is *referenced* stays green while its VALUE is rewritten out from under the thing it must match. Pin the value, on both sides of any join with no shared module.
- **A REGEX OVER SOURCE TEXT IS NOT A BEHAVIOURAL ASSERTION.** It goes red on a refactor that changed nothing and green on a path that does the wrong thing. Drive the real function.
- **Assert the object that CROSSES the process boundary**, not the function that computes it (§11).
- **A comment asserting where a filter lives is not evidence the filter exists.** When a comment says a constraint is enforced somewhere else, open that somewhere else.
- **A MIXED TEST FILE WHOSE FEATURE IS DELETED IS REWRITTEN DOWN TO WHAT SURVIVES, NOT REMOVED** — deleting one whole has twice taken an unrelated live guard with it.

An unregistered shell has its entire privileged IPC surface refused, silently, and nothing else in the suite would notice.

## 15. Standing rulings — Samuel, cross-cutting

Rules that are not one feature's. Each carries the date it was ruled. A rule here outranks a
recommendation in any spec; a spec that disagrees is the thing that is wrong.

- 🔴 **ANYTHING CLICKABLE SHOWS THE HAND, AND IT IS ONE RULE RATHER THAN A CLASS PER CONTROL
  (2026-09-18).** Samuel: *"for a lot of buttons across the desktop app, when I hover over them,
  the cursor does not change into the clickable cursor. … Is there one way you can set one piece of
  code that will make it so that, anytime there's a button or something that can be clicked, the
  cursor should change into the hand cursor? That's super important."* The rule lives in `@layer
  base` in **both** stylesheets — `src/app/globals.css` and `apps/desktop-ui/src/styles/tokens.css`
  (F-074: hand-copies, no shared module) — over `button`, `a[href]`, `summary`, `select`, the
  clickable ARIA roles, the clickable `input` types, `input[type="file"]::file-selector-button`
  and `[data-clickable]`, with a second rule giving `:disabled` / `[aria-disabled="true"]` /
  `[data-disabled]` `not-allowed`.
  - ⚠ **`label[for]` IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE LIST, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT.** Every
    `htmlFor` in this tree points at a TEXT field (re-derive: `grep -rn htmlFor src apps
    --include='*.tsx'`), where a hand promises a press that is really a focus. A label tied to a
    CHECKBOX or a RADIO is the case that wants one and takes `data-clickable` the day it exists.
  - ⚠ **THE CAUSE WAS TAILWIND v4, NOT THE COMPONENTS.** v3's Preflight carried `button { cursor:
    pointer }`; v4's declares no `cursor` at all, so every `<button>` fell back to the UA
    `cursor: default` and only components that happened to spell `cursor-pointer` had a hand.
    Re-derive rather than trusting this: `grep -n cursor node_modules/tailwindcss/preflight.css`.
  - 🔒 **ZERO SPECIFICITY IN THE WEAKEST LAYER IS THE CONTRACT.** Every compound is `:where()`, so
    any explicit cursor still wins — `cursor-text` on the inline editors, `cursor-col-resize` on the
    channel info divider, `cursor-ns-resize` on a `SectionBox` grip, `cursor-grabbing` on a dragged
    graph card, and every `disabled:cursor-*` a component already spells.
    **Do not raise the rule's specificity to make it stick** — that inverts it into an override.
  - 🔴 **AND THIS RULING OVERRIDES THE CURSOR HALF OF THE 2026-09-15 AGENT-TAB RULING (Samuel,
    2026-09-18, asked directly).** That one read *"the ACTIVE tab takes neither the fill nor the
    cursor"* and held by SILENCE — a `<button>` had no hand unless a component asked for one.
    **The FILL half stands** (no `hover:bg-*` on the active tab); **the CURSOR half does not** — an
    active tab is still a button you can click, so it shows the hand like every other control.
    ⚠ **`agent-window-chrome.tsx › TAB_ACTIVE` THEREFORE STATES NO CURSOR UTILITY AT ALL, AND THAT
    ABSENCE IS LOAD-BEARING** — a `cursor-default` bolted back on would out-layer the base rule and
    silently re-take the override. Pinned by `agent-window-chrome.test.tsx`, which asserts the
    absence of any `cursor-` class rather than of `cursor-pointer` (the old spelling passed with
    `cursor-default` present).
  - ⚠ **`[data-clickable]` IS THE ESCAPE HATCH AND IT IS NOT A STYLE HOOK.** A clickable that is
    neither a control nor a role — a card or a header row that selects on click while a real
    `<button>` inside it carries the keyboard — takes the attribute, never a `role="button"` that
    would nest buttons inside a button.
  - ⚠ **PINNED BY `src/shared/ui/clickable-cursor.test.ts`, WHICH IS NOT A NEW CI GATE** — it rides
    the existing root suite. `check-css-token-drift.ts` **cannot** see this rule (a `cursor`
    declaration is neither a `--*` token nor a `@layer components` name), so that test is the only
    thing holding the two copies equal, and its second half is a source scan: an `onClick` on a
    non-interactive tag must carry `role` or `data-clickable`, or be named in its allowlist with the
    reason it is not a click target. **The allowlist may only ever shrink.**

- 🔴 **AN UNKNOWN FAILS CLOSED, AND "CLOSED" IS DECIDED BY WHICH SIDE DENIES — NOT BY WHICH
  LITERAL IS THE DEFAULT (2026-09-18).** Samuel, ruling F-718 and F-729 together: fix both
  fail-closed. Two rules came out of it, and neither is a style preference.
  - **ASK THE SHARED PREDICATE, NEVER RE-SPELL IT.** "Is there a second audience in this room" is
    `shared/tenancy/shared-room.ts › isSharedRoom` (and its hand mirror in `packages/mcp-server`);
    "is channel scope a thing in this container" is `shared/tenancy/channel-scope.ts ›
    channelScopeAllowedForKind`. A hand-spelled `memberCount <= 1` answers SOLO to a real `0` — a
    roster race, a `status` flip mid-request — and a hand-spelled `kind !== 'link'` admits every kind
    added to the union after it. **Both failures are silent and both were live.**
  - ⚠ **`(kind ?? "standard")` IS FAIL-CLOSED ONLY WHERE `standard` DENIES.** It is the required
    positive form in `isStandardWorkspace` (F-295/F-564, enforced by `check-role-drift.ts`) and it
    is fail-OPEN in any feature where `standard` is what UNLOCKS — global search was one
    (F-729, §9). **Before copying the idiom, say out loud which side of the question denies.** Where
    the answer is "the default's side serves", carry the raw nullable column out of the repository
    and ask positively at the gate.
  - ⚠ **AND A DEVIATION LIST IS NOT A PARKING SPACE.** F-718 sat for a day as the single
    DOCUMENTED deviation in `shared-room-parity.test.ts`; the list is empty now. An entry there
    means a ruling is owed, not that one was made.

- 🔴 **DEAD CODE IS DELETED (2026-09-17).** Not disarmed, not parked, not left behind a flag nobody
  passes. **The one exception is something Samuel built and forgot: ASK ONCE, then delete.** One
  question, not a standing hold — an unanswered ask does not convert a dead lane into a live one.
  ⚠ This is the rule the `delete-don't-disarm` bullets have been applying case by case; it is now
  general, and it is why an unreachable component with a width budget attached is a defect rather
  than inventory. ⚠ **"Dead" is a MEASUREMENT** — re-derive the call sites before you delete, because
  `bits.tsx › agentAccent` was called an orphan and still had a live call site.

- 🔴 **THERE IS NO ARCHIVE. A CHANNEL EXISTS OR IT IS DELETED (Samuel's ruling R-21, 2026-09-17):**
  *"a user can delete a channel; no point in archives."* The whole feature is gone on BOTH surfaces —
  the Archive / Unarchive row in the Settings tab, the Status row (Active / Archived) on the Info
  tab, the client write (`archiveConfig` / `toggleArchive`), the `archived` field on
  `ChannelUpdateSchema` and on `service-writes-channel.ts › MANAGED_CHANNEL_FIELDS`, the
  `archived_at` stamp that was its only writer, `?include=archived` with its second cache variant,
  and every read that filtered on the flag (`channels/server/repository.ts › listChannels` and both
  filters in `workspaces/server/repository-overview.ts`).
  - 🔴 **SO CHANNELS THAT WERE ARCHIVED ARE BACK, AND THAT IS THE RULING'S OUTCOME RATHER THAN A
    SIDE EFFECT.** A row carrying an old `archived_at` stamp now appears in every list, count and
    activity feed as an ordinary channel. Nothing hides a row for having one; nothing may start.
  - ⚠ **THE COLUMN SURVIVES THIS WAVE, WITH NO WRITER AND NO READER.** `channels.archived_at`, the
    `Channel.archivedAt` DTO field and `@dopl/client › Channel.archivedAt` are vestigial — **do not
    branch on them.** The drop is written and deliberately NOT applied
    (`supabase/migrations/20261010120000_drop_channels_archived_at.sql`); it carries the re-derive
    command rather than a count, and the DTO field, the client type and the fixtures go with it in
    that same change.
  - ⚠ **`deleted_at` IS A DIFFERENT THING AND STILL FILTERS EVERYWHERE.** A soft-deleted channel is
    NOT-FOUND to every read; that is the lifecycle R-21 left the user, and it is not "archive under
    another name".
  - ⚠ **THE MCP SURFACE NEVER HAD AN ARCHIVE OP** and still does not — `dopl_channel(op="rooms",
    action="update")` writes the info card and nothing else (Q12 (b)). What it lost is
    `listChannels({ includeArchived: true })` in `channel-shared.ts › resolveChannelOr`, which
    existed so an archived room stayed addressable; the plain list now carries every channel.

- 🔴 **THE HOME SPACE IS STRUCTURAL — CONTAINER KIND IS A TYPED FIELD, NEVER A PROMPT (2026-09-17).**
  Samuel: *home must be structurally distinct, never just a prompt line.* Every container is
  **addressable**: personal = the reserved name **`home`**, resolved per caller · a home-channel
  container = **its channel slug** · a workspace = **its slug**. **One `container=` parameter**
  addresses all three, and an unaddressed call resolves to **home**. The **KIND** travels as a typed
  field on every MCP row and list, and `dopl_map` renders **"Home space" as its own top-level node**.
  ⚠ **A sentence in a system prompt is not an implementation of this rule.** If an agent can only
  learn which kind of container it is in by reading prose, the field is missing. ⚠ It also means
  the home space is **auto-created per account and permanent**: there is no MCP door onto its
  existence — nothing creates or deletes it via a tool (R-34). And **signup mints exactly a home
  space — no default standard workspace** (R-35).
  - ✅ **IMPLEMENTED ON THE MCP SURFACE 2026-09-17 (wave 3, `wave3/container-addressing`).** The
    `container=` parameter, the `home` reserved word, the home-channel slug address, the typed
    `ContainerKind` in `@dopl/contracts`, `dopl_map`'s Home-space node, the refusal of an
    unaddressed mint and the `checkContainerKind` drift gate are all in the tree — §10 carries the
    contract, `packages/mcp-server/src/container-addressing.test.ts` carries the census. ⚠ **What
    this does NOT yet cover is the rest of the estate**: `src/features/**` and the desktop still
    say "workspace" wherever they name a container, and the one projection R-32 was ruled to decide
    the addressing of (Wave 3's P30) is not built. The rule is implemented where an AGENT meets it.

- 🔴 **THE GUIDANCE LAYER IS DELETED, PENDING A REIMPLEMENTATION (Samuel's ruling R-49,
  2026-09-17).** *"Delete the guidance-banner code now, reimplement later."* Not mounted on /home,
  not left on the workspace: **the Tour, the join-request notices, the connect-agent banner and the
  welcome popup are off disk**, and a first-run experience is designed fresh when it is wanted.
  ⚠ **THIS REMOVED A SHIPPED WORKSPACE AFFORDANCE**, not an absent home one — all four were live in
  the desktop workspace shell. **Do not re-add one of the four on its own**; the ruling is about the
  layer.
  - **What went — re-derive with `git log --diff-filter=D`, never from this list:** the whole of
    src/features/tour (the provider, the popover, its CSS, and the five tour steps keyed to
    `NavSection`) · the join-request notices core in `src/features/workspaces/components/`, with
    `GET /api/me/join-requests`, its `/ack` POST and `src/features/workspaces/server/join-links.ts`'s
    `listMyJoinNotices` / `acknowledgeJoinNotice` / `JoinRequestNotice` · the connect-agent banner and
    the welcome popup in `src/features/onboarding/components/`, with `buildBootstrapPrompt` and
    `DOPL_CARD_TEMPLATE` out of `src/features/onboarding/bootstrap-prompt.ts`, plus the
    `MCP_SERVER_NAME` constant beside it that the prompt was the last reader of, and the `dopl:welcome`
    write in `src/features/onboarding/components/onboarding-flow-core.tsx` that nothing reads any
    more · every mount in `apps/desktop-ui/src/components/app-shell/app-shell.tsx`.
  - **What SURVIVES, and why each one is not dead code.**
    `src/features/onboarding/hooks/use-mcp-connection-poll.ts` — `OnboardingFlowCore` still mounts it.
    `src/features/onboarding/bootstrap-prompt.ts › buildConnectPrompt` — onboarding step 2.
    `src/shared/layout/app-shell/app-sidebar-core.tsx › NavSection` — the sidebar's own union, which
    the tour merely keyed off.
  - 🔒 **THE TWO ACK COLUMNS ARE DATA AND STAY: `workspace_join_requests.pending_acknowledged_at`
    and `.resolved_acknowledged_at`.** They are a user's own "I have seen this", still stamped `null`
    on insert, with **no reader and no writer** until a notice is rebuilt. ⚠ **Do not branch on them
    meanwhile, and do not drop them without Samuel's word** — same posture as `channels.archived_at`
    above. The per-device `dopl:welcome` flag is NOT in this class and went with its reader.
  - **The absence is pinned** by `apps/desktop-ui/src/components/app-shell/app-shell.test.tsx ›
    mounts NO guidance layer`, whose bridge stub REJECTS an unexpected path — so a re-mounted poll
    fails loudly rather than returning quietly. Deleting that test deletes the ruling.

- 🔒 **THE SETTINGS PAGE IS FROZEN (Samuel's ruling R-10, 2026-09-17), pending his own overhaul.** No restyle, no
  header migration, no section-language sweep, no dialog conformance pass touches `/settings`.
  A wave that needs a settings change waits for the overhaul or asks.
  - ⚠ **THE POPUP HALF OF THIS FREEZE IS SPENT: THE OVERHAUL RAN ON 2026-09-18**, directed by
    Samuel, and the two are no longer one surface. **The settings POPUP** (the gear, and /home's
    black **Profile** pill — `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/home/home-settings-control.tsx`) is now a
    FLAT four-row rail with no group headers: **Workspaces · Connect · Account · Plans & Billing**
    (`shared/layout/settings-modal/settings-modal-core.tsx › NAV`). The rail's rows are the app
    sidebar's own recipe — `nav-chip` / `nav-chip-active raised-tab`, resting fill `--shell-chip`,
    a 20px lucide glyph at `strokeWidth={1.8}` — so the two rails read ONE declaration and cannot
    drift to a second gray; `.navGroup` / `.navGroupLabel` are deleted from
    `settings-modal.module.css`.
  - ⚠ **"General" IS NOT RENAMED, IT IS GONE FROM THE POPUP.** `SettingsSection` is
    `"workspaces" | "connect" | "account" | "billing"`; **Workspaces** LISTS the home space plus
    every standard workspace (`sections/workspaces-section-core.tsx`, filtered through
    `isStandardWorkspace` — §4A) and EDITS none. **The one surface that edits a workspace is
    `/{segment}/settings`**, which still mounts `WorkspaceSectionBody` and IS still frozen.
  - ⚠ **THE CONNECT/LOGIN BLOCK MOVED, AND ONLY ITS MOUNT POINTS CHANGED.** `RemoteConnect` left
    `WorkspaceSectionBody` and `ConnectedAppsSection` left the desktop page's `extras` slot; both
    are `sections/connect-section-core.tsx` now. Both are ACCOUNT-scoped (`/api/mcp`,
    `/api/oauth/grants`) and neither reads a workspace. **`extras` has no caller left** and is kept
    as the body's one extension point. Pinned in both directions:
    `apps/desktop-ui/src/pages/settings/index.test.tsx › renders no connect block and reads no
    grants` and `components/settings-modal/settings-modal.test.tsx › revokes a connected app from
    the Connect tab`.
  - ⚠ **The web's now-unmounted General composition is F-751, not a deletion** — its icon uploader
    is the tree's only workspace-image control.

- 🔴 **CHANNEL DELETE IS CREATOR-ONLY, AND BLOCKED WHILE OTHERS ARE MEMBERS (R-14, 2026-09-17).**
  The creator removes people first. Ruled in the same breath: the public claim surface gets a RATE
  LIMIT (F-297), there is NO mint quota (F-298 declined), and a claim reveals NAMES only, never
  emails (F-299). ⚠ Not yet built — no wave carries it.

- 🔒 **THE AUDIENCE-CHANGE PREVIEW FIRES FOR ANY CONTAINER WITH A SECOND AUDIENCE (R-31,
  2026-09-17)** — standard workspaces included. The confirm token was built as a home-channel
  mechanism and is not one: **kind is not the question, a second audience is.**

- 🔒 **A FOLDER-SCOPED KNOWLEDGE ATTACHMENT NARROWS AN AGENT'S REACH (R-37, 2026-09-17).** It does
  not re-point an agent at a folder inside a base it may still read whole — the agent may read the
  attached folder and nothing else.

- 🔒 **THE MEMBER ACTIVITY TAB STAYS (R-11, 2026-09-17).** The table, the revoked grant and the
  server-side filter are worth their cost. Not a deletion candidate again.

- 🔒 **PRE-2026-08-24 HOME CONTAINERS STAY DISPLAY-ONLY (R-50, 2026-09-17).** Their channel name and
  description are NOT restored and there is no migration.

- 🔴 **THE WORKSPACE SIDEBAR AND THE FIVE PAGE TITLES STAY (R-02, 2026-09-17).** The /home header
  strip vs the workspace sidebar is an INTENTIONAL difference, not drift. Header GEOMETRY may be
  unified; no title is deleted. ⚠ The Knowledge hero band is **not** deleted on this ruling's
  authority — ledger row 16 was narrowed, not granted.

- 🔴 **ONE SEARCH SURFACE (R-04, 2026-09-17).** The search popup IS the workspace's search. No page
  gets a per-page filter.

- 🔒 **NO PAGE SKELETONS NOW — LATER, NOT NEVER (R-06, 2026-09-17).** Skills, Chats and Ontology keep
  resolving through `PageLoading`, which renders a SHAPE. A wave may not add one.

- 🔒 **R-07 (2026-09-17, "both Agents names stay") IS SUPERSEDED (Samuel, 2026-09-22).** The /home face
  is **Identities** (agent identities) and the channel **Agents** tab (running sessions) keeps its name — see §5A's rename bullet.

- 🔴 **A HOME-ONLY DESIGN ASYMMETRY NEEDS NO RECORDED REASON (R-40, 2026-09-17).** The label-less
  credit bar, `HOME_CARD_FACE_SELECTED` and the Agents-page face all stay. *"This differs from the
  workspace and nothing says why"* is not a finding.

- 🔴 **THE 2026-08-30 DRIFT-AUDIT ASKs ARE DEAD AS A BATCH — R-43 AND R-13 ARE EXPIRED
  (2026-09-17).** An item from that audit is live only if it is RE-FOUND in current code; an
  unanswered ASK holds nothing. This is why nothing waits on ASK-9.

- 🔒 **THE PLAYGROUND STAYS (R-47, 2026-09-17).** It does NOT retire with the website; deletions
  ledger row 21 is vetoed and `docs/RETIREMENT-UNWIRING-PLAN.md` does not reach it.

- ⚠ **OWED: THE PERSONAL-SHELF BOUNDARY IS A RULE NOBODY HAS WRITTEN (R-30(a), 2026-09-17).** Samuel
  ruled *"keep both, and write the boundary down as a rule in INVARIANTS §4A"*. §4A still does not
  carry it, so the ruling is executed nowhere.

Why/history: `docs/specs/workspace-parity/00-MASTER.md` §2.4 (the 49 rulings recorded 2026-09-17).
